How to read this file — copper

How to read a card

  • 2nd 3×? (the chip on each card): after a first 3× in years 1–5, is there room for another 3× by about year 10? Yes = a believable path (big or growing resource, several assets, growth paid from cash flow); partly = capped or dependent on the metal price; little = the first re-rating is most of the value. Judged per share at today's market value. It is not about cash: months of cash left are on the card's Financials tab (where it exists) and in the funding line. Full explanation on the rankings page under table B.
  • Financials (tab on the card, pilot on 29 companies so far): the last 8 quarters and 3 fiscal years read from the original financial statements on the company's own website (no data feed), simplified to the lines that matter — cash, burn, months of cash left, what went into the ground vs overhead, money raised and share count, and for producers revenue, margin and free cash flow. Every column links to the PDF it came from; every quarter is checked (opening cash + net flow = closing cash). The findings feed the runway and risk notes; there is no separate score.
  • Management (chip on each card, full review in the card's Management tab): the people graded A–D on track record (what they built, sold or ran before, misses included), fit (have they done this exact job: same stage, deposit type, region) and candour (a dated promises-vs-delivery log). A★ tier 1 · B solid, or unproven but clean — the default · C real weaknesses · D a pattern of failing shareholders. Neutral by default: the odds move only with evidence, full weight for explorers and developers, half for producers. A fourth score, skin in the game (1–5, in the Management tab), is the team's own money at risk — a conviction signal that never moves the odds but breaks near-ties in list B; a team that gets paid while shareholders lose scores 1. Reviewed 5 Oct 2026, refreshed every Saturday.
  • Bucket (the colour bar): the archetype — cheap defined pounds needs at least an Indicated resource plus a study; grade / discovery is drill-bit optionality, however cheap it screens; quality / jurisdiction is de-risked and priced for it; scale & financing is a big asset whose gate is the cheque.
  • Gate: the one thing that has to go right. Differentiator: what the company has that peers don't. When those two are the same fact seen from two sides, that is usually the most honest thing to know about the name.
  • Funding & next catalyst (top of every card): cash, debt, burn, next dated event, and a verdict — funded / partly / not funded to that event — with the gap in money and months. The verdict is about the next catalyst, not the mine build.
  • Anchor: EV per pound of contained copper (¢/lb), or P/NAV where a study exists. Always read against the confidence category — an Inferred pound is not a cheap pound, it is an unproven one.
  • Rule screen (Rick Rule's developer test): after-tax IRR ≥ 25–30% at a conservative price, NPV ≥ 2–3× capex, payback ≲ 3 years, 8–10% discount rate. Few names pass at their own deck; the Numbers tab shows where each one passes and where it doesn't.
  • Risk 1–5: chance of permanent loss or no re-rate inside a 3–5 year horizon (1 lowest). Risk and ranking are deliberately separate — a 4 can top the multi-bagger list if the price pays for the risk.
  • Metal badge beside the name (Cu · Cu·Au · Cu·Mo) and the matching filter row: what drives the value — a Cu·Au name moves less on the copper-price columns of the rankings than its copper share suggests; Copper Giant's Mo credit is the thesis, hence Cu·Mo.
  • Shareholder structure is on every card but never scored: insider ownership is a tell, not a criterion. Shares bought with cash at market are a vote; options and RSUs are pay; settlement shares are a negotiation.
  • 💸 Pick: a personal flag with an event-driven entry plan on the card (Entry plan & Watch tab). Picks do not enter the rankings.
  • News tab and the file-level News section: the company's own releases for the current and previous month, linked to its site, with a grey note where a release changes the card.

Figures are mixed-date and sit on each study's own metal-price deck and discount rate — read anchors and NPV/capex as shapes, not decimal-precise rankings. Research shorthand, not investment advice. The rankings page uses the same scales.

Thesis

The Lundin Group's discovery vehicle. Lunahuasi (100%, San Juan) is one of the highest-grade copper-gold-silver discoveries in the Andes, 9 km from Los Helados (Chile) and inside the Vicuña district next to the BHP–Lundin Vicuña JV — the natural consolidator.

The Gate

Turning spectacular intercepts into a maiden resource that justifies ~US$4B. Phase 4 is complete (27,318 m, 32 holes; final assays released Jul 30, 2026); Phase 5 is expected to start Q4 2026 alongside construction of an exploration adit; no MRE date set. The specific geological question: does the bonanza gold component (veins found 660 m apart) build into continuous mineable tonnage, or stay as spectacular narrow veins?

DepositNo Lunahuasi resource yetStandout intercepts: 94 m @ 8.99% CuEq incl. 21.7 m @ 31.92% CuEq (Mars); Saturn 327 m @ 3.74% and 335 m @ 4.08% CuEq; DPDH049 1,246.5 m @ 0.86% CuEq incl. 131 m @ 5.09%; 17.3 m @ 207.79 g/t Au; Jul 2026: 20.5 m @ 17.83% CuEq. The Lunahuasi porphyry is now known to include a large breccia body with significant Cu-Au grades. Plus Los Helados (~69%): Indicated ~2.08 Bt @ 0.40% Cu (~18.4 Blb Cu, ~10.2 Moz Au) + ~1.08 Bt Inferred.
NPV : capexn/a — no study.
Valuation Anchor

~US$4.0B with no Lunahuasi resource — above the ~C$4.1B (≈US$3.0B) BHP and Lundin paid for all of Filo after it had a resource and a PEA. The market is already pricing a Filo-type outcome. An outstanding asset with little discount left — same bucket as Atex and Gladiator, but at a scale where the re-rate has largely happened.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~2.7% (CEO Wojtek Wodzicki ~0.95% ≈ C$53M; Chair Adam Lundin ~0.84% ≈ C$47M — small percentages, large dollars). Control: Nemesia (Lundin family trusts) ~34%, which added ~€20M Oct 2025 and took part in the C$175M placement at C$25. Funds: Rothschild & Co ~5.3%, Mirae ~3.2%, BlackRock ~3.1%. Lundin Mining owns 31% of Los Helados, not NGEx equity. Wodzicki sold 50k sh Jan 2026.

Read: Strong alignment through the family and management's dollar exposure, though management's percentage is small.

Jurisdiction risk

National: favourable on both sides. San Juan is pro-mining and RIGI-eligible; Los Helados sits in Chile's Region III; and the revived Chile–Argentina Mining Integration Treaty targets exactly this kind of cross-border district. Local: low — remote high-altitude Andes, no organised opposition; exploration adit approved by the San Juan Mining Authority (Mar 2026).

The real local risk is altitude and logistics, not licence.

Differentiator

Grade no other name in the file comes close to, plus a buyer next door and a balance sheet that never needs a bad-tape raise. The Lundin precedent is explicit: Filo was bought by BHP and Lundin for ~C$4.1B (≈US$3.0B), closing in 2025. Lundin Mining's move into ~31% of Los Helados (from JX, 2026) is creeping consolidation.

Read honestly: every one of those strengths is in the price.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, better tonnes · moves the needle: very high geologically — but largely priced. Multiple high-grade zones and styles (epithermal, porphyry, gold veins), not closed off at depth or along strike; new zones north and 300 m east of Mars; Jupiter the Stage 5 target. The best exploration story in the file.

Next Catalyst

Phase 5 drilling from Q4 2026 (Jupiter a priority target); exploration adit construction; maiden MRE (undated); any Vicuña-district consolidation move. Lunahuasi sits ~6 km north of Filo del Sol and ~8 km west of Josemaría.

Open Questions
  • When does a maiden Lunahuasi MRE arrive, and how many tonnes at what grade?
  • Does the bonanza gold build tonnage?
  • Does Lundin Mining's stake in Los Helados foreshadow a district consolidation — and at what price relative to today?

Management review
A★tier 1 — proven at this job, candid, investedTrack record 5/5 · Fit 5/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

The same technical team found and sold Josemaria (C$625M) and Filo del Sol (C$4.1B) in the same belt, and the company is funded for years. Caveat: family-aligned exit terms.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 35% → 40%, odds of a 3× 3% → 3%.

People
Wojtek Wodzicki (President & CEO, since CEO of NGEx since 2019 spin-out (Lundin Group since 2007)): PhD geoscience (Arizona), age 62. Led teams credited with Los Helados, Josemaria, Lunahuasi discoveries; 2024 PDAC Thayer Lindsley award. Former CEO Josemaria Resources, Filo Corp (early), Sanu Resources. · Adam Lundin (Chair, since 17 Sep 2026 (director before; succeeded William Rand, chair since 2019)): Age 39, Lundin family; also chair of Lundin Mining and other Lundin Group companies. · Bob Carmichael (VP Exploration, since n/a (ex-Filo Corp VP Exploration)): Ran exploration at Filo del Sol before BHP/Lundin Mining takeover. · Arndt Brettschneider (VP Operations & Projects, since Lundin Group 2019): Ex-Filo VP Operations/Projects; relevant for planned underground exploration adit. · Alex Tong (CFO, since n/a): Ex-VP Finance Lucara Diamond.
Track record
  • Wodzicki as CEO of Josemaria Resources: sold to Lundin Mining in 2022 for about C$625M (intra-group deal) - a win in the 2021-22 cyclesource
  • Filo Corp (NGEx spin-out 2016; Wodzicki early CEO, later director) sold to BHP/Lundin Mining for C$4.1B in 2024 - the biggest win; discovery made under the same technical team (Carmichael, Rode)source
  • Sanu Resources (Eritrea explorer, Wodzicki CEO) went nowhere and was folded into NGEx in 2011 - a misssource
  • Lunahuasi discovered 2023; four drill phases delivered through Apr 2026 with consistently high grades; cash + investments of C$463M at Jun 2026, no debtsource
  • Chair Adam Lundin: inherited role; his personal record as an executive is at Lundin Mining (chair) and Josemaria (CEO 2018-19, sold 2022) - not independently proven as a discoverer or buildersource

Boards today: Wodzicki: NGEx CEO + director of Fireweed Metals and LunR Royalties (3 public roles). Adam Lundin: chair of NGEx and Lundin Mining, plus other Lundin Group boards (count not verified, likely 4+).

Fit to this job
Stage: explorer/discovery - exactly what this team has done three times in the same district (Los Helados, Josemaria, Filo del Sol) in the same Vicuna belt, same high-altitude Argentina/Chile jurisdiction, same porphyry/high-sulphidation system type. Martin Rode (SA GM) has 20+ years in the district. New for them: Lunahuasi is a high-grade underground-style target (adit planned), whereas prior wins were bulk-tonnage open-pit deposits; and neither Wodzicki nor the chair has built a mine.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Nemesia S.a.r.l. (Lundin family) 33.97% / 73.7M sh; Wodzicki 2,061,600 sh (~1.0%); 216.9M shares outstanding (May 2026). Insiders net sellers ~C$4.2M over last 12 months. CEO total comp ~C$5.5M (Simply Wall St; salary C$515,000 per 2026 circular, full table not extracted). Sources: https://ngexminerals.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2026-NGEx-Information-Circular-vF.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-ngex/ngex-minerals-shares/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Insiders net sellers of ~C$4.2M in the last 12 months (options and market), including a CFO sale of ~C$1.2M in Dec (per Simply Wall St).
  • Control block: Nemesia (Lundin family trust) holds 33.97%; prior exits were sales INTO Lundin-related buyers (Josemaria to Lundin Mining; Filo to BHP+Lundin Mining) - minority holders depend on family-aligned deal terms.
  • CEO pay ~C$5.5M (Simply Wall St) is high for an explorer with no revenue, though the company is valued in the billions.

  1. Liquid funds were about C$211M at 30 June 2026 including C$130M of short-term investments; at C$11M a month that is roughly 19 months.

  5. The LunR Royalties stake, about C$250M, swings equity by hundreds of millions each quarter; a second spin-out goes to a vote on 29 October 2026.

Thesis

A permitted, construction-ready, high-grade US copper mine with sovereign financing behind it. Robert Friedland exec chair. Sits on 24.2 km² of private land with its own water rights, so all key permits are secured without a federal-land NEPA process. First cathode targeted Q2 2029 (slipped from 2028). Other assets are free options: Tintic (Utah), Hog Heaven (Montana), a 50/50 Saudi JV with Ma'aden, and the Typhoon geophysics system.

The Gate

Closing the project financing — a transaction, not a permit. US EXIM upsized its indication to a US$1.1B Preliminary Project Letter (Aug 24, 2026) from the original US$825M LOI, weeks after a presidential endorsement at an Aug 7 State Department mining roundtable — but a Preliminary Project Letter is indicative, not an executed facility, and the final EXIM board vote is expected in 2027, which is what actually gates major construction. Bridged meanwhile by a US$200M senior secured facility (Dec 2025; NBC/BMO/SocGen, 2-yr) plus ~US$231M raised in 2025 and the Alacrán sale; BMO says treasury funds early works and the TBM into 2027 without drawing the bridge — financing risk "moderate." Secondary: single-TBM execution risk (novel underground access; capex rose 15% to US$1.43B in the 23 Sep PFS), groundwater inflows of 6,000–8,000 gpm at peak needing grouting/lining, and copper-price sensitivity.

Santa Cruz, Casa Grande — "the largest high-grade copper oxide orebody in America." Underground longhole stoping, 20,000 t/d, on/off heap leach → LME Grade A cathode on-site; ~75 kt/yr cathode first 15 yrs, 24-yr life; C1 US$1.47/lb, AISC US$2.28/lb (Sep 2026 PFS).
NPV : capex1.05x @ base US$4.75/lb → ~2.45x @ US$6.79IRR 18.7% base / 30% spot. Fails Rule at base; passes only near spot copper.
Valuation Anchor

Two readings that disagree — hold both. On defined pounds it's expensive: EV ~US$1.4B / 3.3 Blb reserve Cu ≈ ~44¢/lb, more than ten times Los Andes — the Marimaca profile (small, high-grade, near-term). On P/NAV it's cheap for what it is: sell-side puts it at ~0.5x NAV at US$6 copper, a discount for a permitted, construction-ready, government-backed US project. The gap is the market pricing the 2027 financing timing and TBM execution. Same bucket as Osisko (quality you pay for) — but unlike Osisko, the premium here shows up in EV/lb, not P/NAV.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~16% — Robert Friedland ~8% personally (exercised and kept 917k options Jun 2026) plus I-Pulse (Friedland-chaired) ~6% (last filed 2023; unverified). Strategic: Ma'aden ~7.4% (board-nomination rights). BHP holds no equity — exploration alliance only. Funds: T. Rowe ~7%, State Street ~6.8%, Chow Tai Fook ~6.5%, BlackRock ~5.9%, FMR ~5.7%.

Read: Strong at the founder level; other executives hold little.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the strongest position in the file. US critical-minerals priority, presidential endorsement (Aug 2026), US$1.1B EXIM Preliminary Project Letter. Local: effectively solved. 24.2 km² of private land with its own water rights — all key permits secured, no federal-land NEPA process.

Permitting risk, which dominates Los Andes and Copper Giant, is simply absent here — and that is precisely why it trades near fair value.

Differentiator

The only name in the file with a sovereign lender. A US$1.1B EXIM indication under Make More in America plus explicit White House backing is a category of support no Andean or Canadian name here has — and if EXIM closes, it sets the template for financing US greenfield copper. Second: private land + own water — permitting is done, which removes the gate that dominates Los Andes and Copper Giant entirely. Third: highest reserve grade of any developer in the file (1.08% Cu vs. Los Azules 0.45%, Los Andes 0.36%) with first-quartile C1, and cathode at the mine gate — no smelter, no TC/RCs, no export. Fourth: Friedland's record of financing mines — his name buys capital, not execution (Kamoa was built by others; see the Management tab), and the Arizona operating team only arrived in September 2026.

Read honestly: the differentiator is also why the market pays up per pound — it's a small, high-grade orebody, so EV/lb is high even though P/NAV isn't.

Exploration upside

Beyond-reserve resource plus free options · moves the needle: low within the horizon. Indicated 182.8 Mt @ 0.81% and Inferred 422 Mt @ 0.79% sit beyond the reserve; Tintic, Hog Heaven, the Saudi JV and Typhoon are optionality. Execution and financing dominate the next 3–5 years.

Next Catalyst

PFS released 23 Sep 2026 (capex US$1.43B, NPV US$1.5B @ US$4.75, IRR 18.7%); EXIM final board consideration (spring 2027); TBM arrival H1 2027 and decline start mid-2027; first ore to leach pads H2 2028; project-level equity partner. Update: COO (ex-ASARCO) and Santa Cruz GM (ex-Nevada Gold Mines) appointed effective Sep 1, 2026 — execution leg strengthened. Texaco deposit (Inferred 2.7 Mt Cu @ 0.8%) is expansion upside outside the mine plan.

Open Questions
  • The 23 Sep PFS raised capex to US$1.43B — does EXIM size its loan to the new number?
  • Does EXIM's 2027 board vote clear at the indicated size — and does construction start slip further if it doesn't?
  • Does the single TBM perform?
  • Who takes the project-level minority equity the financing plan contemplates?

People
Taylor Melvin (President, CEO, Director, since 2023-01): Ex-Freeport-McMoRan VP corporate development (~15 yrs); first CEO role; no mine build on his own record. (Tenure start unverified in this research.) · Robert Friedland (Executive Chairman, founder, since 2021 (IPO June 2022)): Age ~76. Also founder/executive co-chair of Ivanhoe Mines; controls Ivanhoe Capital, I-Pulse, HPX. Promoter-financier, not an operator. · Michelle Lammers (COO, since 2026-09-01): 20+ yrs ASARCO (Arizona): GM Ray mine, Silver Bell heap-leach project manager, Operations Director USA. Arizona copper operator. · Daniel Worthy (SVP Operations & GM Santa Cruz, since 2026-09-01): Ex-GM Cortez and Hemlo (Barrick/NGM); underground operations. Glen Kuntz (SVP Mine Development, ex-Yamana) continues.
Track record
  • Friedland hits: Diamond Fields/Voisey's Bay sold to Inco C$4.3B (1996); Oyu Tolgoi discovered and financed, Ivanhoe Mines ceded control to Rio Tinto (2012, Turquoise Hill); Ivanhoe Mines (DRC/SA): Kamoa-Kakula built and in production since 2021, Kipushi restarted 2024 - the one genuine mine-building record, executed by Ivanhoe Mines' operating teamsource
  • Friedland misses: Galactic Resources/Summitville (Colorado) - 1991 cyanide release, 1992 bankruptcy, US$100M+ EPA cleanup; Friedland resigned the day of the EPA notice and later paid ~US$20M in a settlement without admitting liability (settlement figure unverified)source
  • Friedland misses (unverified in this research): Ivanhoe Energy insolvency (2015); Ivanhoe Capital Acquisition SPAC merged into SES AI (2022), shares down >80%; Ivanhoe Australia written down and absorbed; Ivanhoe Electric IPO June 2022 at US$11.75, traded well below that through 2024-25; Kamoa-Kakula seismic shutdown 2025 handled by Ivanhoe Mines.
  • Melvin/IE delivered: PEA 2023, PFS June 2025, updated PFS Sept 2026 (capex US$1.43B, after-tax NPV8 US$1.5B at $4.75 Cu, 19% IRR); US$200M bridge facility Dec 2025; US EXIM preliminary project letter US$1.1B Aug 2026 (non-binding)source
  • Wins came in 1996 (nickel), 2001-2012 (China copper supercycle) and 2021-26 (copper); the big miss (Summitville) came at the 1990 gold-cycle bottom.

Boards today: Friedland: executive chair IE, founder/executive co-chair Ivanhoe Mines, chair HPX, I-Pulse, Ivanhoe Capital (private), plus other Ivanhoe-group vehicles - at least 2 listed executive-chair roles and several private; effectively a portfolio chairman. Melvin: IE only (as found).

Fit to this job
Stage: pre-construction with a US$1.43B capex and 2029 first production - Friedland's group has built one large copper mine (Kamoa) but with a different team; IE's own executives (Melvin, Kuntz) have never taken a project through construction. Deposit/mining: underground (TBM decline) high-grade oxide/sulfide copper with SX-EW cathode in Arizona - Lammers (ASARCO Ray/Silver Bell heap leach, Arizona) and Worthy (underground GM) were hired Sept 2026 precisely to close that gap; this is a good fit on paper, 35 days old in practice. Jurisdiction: Arizona private land, state permits - lower risk than federal; Lammers knows it. New: TBM-driven decline is unusual for a copper mine.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Robert Friedland personally reported 13,272,880 shares = 9.0% of the class at 31 Dec 2025 (Schedule 13G/A filed 28 Jan 2026) — founder stock, not open-market buys; other Friedland vehicles may hold more (unverified). Melvin ownership and 2025 total compensation not retrieved (SEC proxy blocked) — unverified; prior proxies showed multi-million equity-heavy packages for the CEO (unverified). No open-market insider buying found.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Friedland's record includes a bankrupt, environmentally catastrophic mine (Summitville) and a failed SPAC; his wins were discoveries and sales, built by others.
  • Executive chairman splits time across Ivanhoe Mines, IE and private vehicles.
  • Capex up ~15% in 15 months, first production now 2029 vs earlier guidance (earlier date unverified).
  • Financing (US$1.4B+) not in place; EXIM non-binding; company already buying a US$65M TBM.
  • Promotional language ('highest grade, most advanced US copper project') in every headline.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was US$256.9M at 30 June 2026; at US$20M of operating burn a quarter that is roughly 3 years, before Santa Cruz construction.

  4. Shares rose 33% from 120.0M to 159.6M after US$231M of offerings in 2025 and US$81.5M of warrant exercises.
  5. Debt is down to a US$35.2M 8% convertible due December 2026; the Alacrán sale produced a US$124.7M gain, and an affiliate lends US$5M a year.

Valuation Anchor

Large PFS NPV vs. the construction-funding question — the gap is now build financing, not survival.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~42% — Chairman Richard Warke / Augusta ~36%, director Daniel Earle ~4.3%. Funds: Helikon ~11.4%, Mirae ~2.7%, PSquared ~2.4%. Royal Gold holds no equity (stream + NSR); Zijin's proposed 15% stake was terminated May 2024. Warke's large buys were 2021; no 2025–26 open-market purchases found.

Read: Very high — one man controls over a third; alignment is strong, and minority holders ride his decisions.

Jurisdiction risk

National: improving but historically the weakest — Ecuador has killed projects on consultation grounds; EIA technical approval Apr 2026, full permits now targeted H1 2027 (FID late 2027; moved from end-2026 on 28 Sep). Local: earned, not given — and it's the moat. Shuar Life Plans formally recognise mining (Sep 2026); FICSH/PSHA cooperation agreements renewed. In Ecuador this consent is harder to replicate than the geology.

Fragile if community politics shift, but currently a genuine asset.

Differentiator

100% ownership of a tier-1-scale asset — ~304 kt/yr CuEq early-years output puts it in genuine major-company territory, yet no partner or major owns a slice. Combined with the Royal Gold US$200M non-dilutive package (a stream, not equity — Solaris kept the asset), that's the rare combination of scale + undiluted ownership. Second, and underrated: the social licence itself is the moat — Shuar community Life Plans formally recognising mining, plus renewed FICSH/PSHA agreements, in a country where Ecuadorian projects usually die on exactly this. In Ecuador, community consent is harder to replicate than geology.

Flip side: 100% of a US$3.7B build also means 100% of the funding problem, with no major's balance sheet behind it.

Exploration upside

Beyond-reserve scale · moves the needle: low near term. 3.7 Bt M&I against a 1.3 Bt reserve; technical drilling completes by Q4 2026. Scale is already tier-1 — more tonnes won't move the price; financing will.

Next Catalyst

Final permits (end-2026); final Royal Gold tranche (Q4 2026); construction-financing / partner announcement; FID early 2027.

Open Questions
  • Who funds construction, and at what dilution or partnership terms?
  • Do full permits land by end-2026?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 3/5 · Fit 2/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Augusta sells projects and has never built one; at Solaris every dated target since 2024 (PFS, EIA, FID, permits) slipped, communicated by omission; the CEO owns 0.09%.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 35% → 30%, odds of a 3× 13% → 11%.

People
Matthew Rowlinson (President, CEO, since 2025-01-01): Ex-Head of Copper Business Development, Glencore (11 yrs, M&A/portfolio). First CEO role; no construction record. Replaced Daniel Earle (CEO 2019-2024, now Highlander Silver). · Richard Warke (Executive Chairman, founder (Augusta Group), since 2018 (founder)): Serial Augusta exits: Ventana Gold (AUX, ~C$1.5B 2011), Augusta Resource/Rosemont (Hudbay ~C$555M 2014), Arizona Mining (South32 C$2.1B 2018). Largest shareholder (~60M shares). · Javier Toro (COO, since 2024-01): 25+ yrs open-pit copper engineering studies; led the PFS; bought C$100k of stock Jan 2024. · Richard Hughes (CFO, since 2025-01): Ex-CFO Trident Royalties.
Track record
  • Warke hits: Ventana Gold sold to AUX/Eike Batista (~C$1.5B, 2011); Augusta Resource (Rosemont, Arizona) sold to Hudbay (~C$555M, 2014); Arizona Mining (Hermosa) sold to South32 (C$2.1B, 2018) - all sales to larger companies before constructionsource
  • Warke misses: Rosemont was never built - permits later overturned in US court (2019) after the sale; Augusta Gold (Nevada) and Titan Mining (NY zinc) remain small and have underperformed (performance unverified); nothing in the Augusta group has been built and operated at scale by Warke's own team.
  • Wins came in 2011 (gold peak), 2014 (copper mid-cycle) and 2018 (zinc/base-metal top) - timed sales, not builds.
  • Solaris: Zijin 15% strategic deal (Jan 2024, C$130M) terminated May 2024 after Investment Canada review stalled (termination detail unverified); replaced by Orion US$60M facility (Dec 2023) and Royal Gold US$200M (May 2025)source
  • Rowlinson delivered: PFS Nov 2025 (US$3.7B capex, post-tax NPV8 US$4.6B, 26% IRR), EIA technical approval April 2026, renewed Shuar community agreements Sept 2026source

Boards today: Warke: executive chair Solaris, Augusta Gold, Titan Mining and other Augusta-group companies (4+ public chair roles, exact count unverified). Rowlinson: Solaris only (as found).

Fit to this job
Stage: permitting a US$3.7B open-pit porphyry in Ecuador through environmental licence, FPIC consultation and exploitation contract - the Augusta model is to sell at this point, and the team's skills (Warke's deal-making, Rowlinson's Glencore M&A) match a sale better than a build. Deposit/mining: large open-pit porphyry - Toro has the study experience, nobody has built one. Jurisdiction: Ecuador (Shuar communities, government-led consulta) - Adventus/Curipamba and Lundin/Fruta del Norte are the only precedents; Solaris has an in-country team but the chair and CEO have no Ecuador operating record. A Chinese strategic was tried and failed; the Royal Gold stream is the substitute.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Warke ~60M shares (largest holder; founder stock plus option exercises at C$0.80-4.90, no open-market buys found); Rowlinson 0.09% (~C$1.75M, grants); Toro bought C$100k (Jan 2024). Insiders net buyers C$1.7M over 12 months, mostly option exercises. CEO total compensation not disclosed in sources reached (circular not fetched) - unverified. Royal Gold stream US$200M, Orion US$60M facility.source

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Three consecutive timeline slips (PFS, EIA, FID/permits) each communicated by moving the goalposts rather than stating the miss.
  • Strategic investor (Zijin) failed; funding now via stream and debt on a pre-permit project.
  • Executive chairman chairs several Augusta companies; CEO's ownership 0.09%, essentially nil, all grants.
  • Management checks 0/4 (Simply Wall St); CEO compensation not disclosed in sources reached.
  • US$54M cash against a US$3.7B project; Ecuador consulta timing outside company control.

Jurisdiction risk

National: favourable and contractually locked. RIGI gives 30-yr tax/FX/customs stability — a legal shield, not just a policy mood; ~US$277M in benefits. Argentina macro volatility remains, but RIGI is designed to survive it. Local: low. Remote high-altitude San Juan, pro-mining province, EIA approved, no organised opposition campaign.

The risk here is cost and remoteness, not licence.

Differentiator

The 1.25% NSR royalty MUX holds on top of its 46.3% equity — undiscounted cash flows up to ~US$1.4B in higher copper-price scenarios, off gross revenue, non-dilutable. Every equity raise thins the 46.3%; the royalty is untouched. It is quietly the highest-quality exposure MUX has to this project. Second differentiator: RIGI — 30-yr tax/FX/customs stability plus ~US$277M in benefits, a legal shield no Chilean name in this file has. Third: cathode via SX/EW — no smelter, no concentrate, no TC/RC exposure or offtake dependency.

Exploration upside

Open at depth, technology-dependent · moves the needle: low within the horizon. Hypogene mineralisation runs >1,000 m with holes ending in mineralisation, and the system is open to the north under cover — but it's low-grade primary ore (0.1–0.35% Cu) that needs Nuton or a concentrator.

More tonnes, not better tonnes: a long-dated option.

Next Catalyst

McEwen Copper IPO (~US$300M) "in preparation", no date given (29 Sep). FID now expected mid-2027; Société Générale leading project debt. Not yet priced as of Sep 2026.

Open Questions
  • McEwen Copper IPO terms and timing?
  • Post-financing ownership % (MUX's 46.3% gets diluted by the ~US$1.6B equity raise)?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 2/5 · Fit 2/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 5/5

McEwen's big win is twenty years old; MUX missed guidance in 2019, 2024 and 2025, Los Azules dates have slipped ~3 years, and nobody on the team has built at this size.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 45% → 40%, odds of a 3× 10% → 9%.

People
Rob McEwen (Chairman & Chief Owner (CEO) of McEwen Inc.; Chairman of McEwen Copper, since 2005 (US Gold → McEwen Mining)): Age ~76. Founder of Goldcorp; $1/yr salary; says >US$200M personally invested; ~16% of MUX per company site. · Michael Meding (Managing Director, McEwen Copper (runs Los Azules), since unverified (c. 2021)): Ex-Barrick (Pascua-Lama/Veladero region) and Trafigura; led PEA 2023 and FS Oct 2025. · Perry Ing (CFO, McEwen Inc., since unverified): Ex-CFO Kirkland Lake Gold and Mountain Province Diamonds. · Stefan Spears (Corporate Development Officer, since unverified): Fronts investor events with McEwen.
Track record
  • Hit (last cycle): McEwen founded/ran Goldcorp, Red Lake high-grade zone; Goldcorp grew from ~$50M to ~$8B market cap before he left in 2005source
  • Miss: McEwen Mining 2019 guidance cut after Gold Bar start-up problems and Black Fox underground delays; 2019 total gold guidance cut to 131-138k ozsource
  • Miss: 2024 Fox Complex produced 30,150 GEO vs 40-42k guidance (stope failure); consolidated 135.9k GEO within 130-145k only because San Jose/Gold Bar over-deliveredsource
  • Miss: 2025 production 115,687 GEO vs original guidance 120-140k; cash cost $2,106/GEO and AISC $2,444/GEO vs original guidance $1,550-1,750 and $1,800-2,000source
  • Dilution/financing: 1-for-10 reverse split 2022 (unverified date); US$110M 5.25% convertible notes Feb 2025; flow-through shares 2025; McEwen Copper raised >US$500M privately 2021-2025 and a $240M term loan 2026source
  • Los Azules: PEA 2023, FS delivered Oct 2025, RIGI approved Sep 2025, IFC collaboration, SocGen as debt adviser; FID work 27% complete at 30 Jun 2026, FID targeted Q4 2026, construction early 2027, first production 2029/2030source

Boards today: Rob McEwen: chairman/CEO McEwen Inc. and chairman McEwen Copper (private); plus personal investments in other juniors (e.g. Goliath Resources, 2.6%). At least 2 chair roles; non-exec board seats elsewhere unverified.

Fit to this job
Team has built and run small-to-mid gold mines (Gold Bar heap leach, Fox underground, San Jose JV with Hochschild) with a weak operating record. Nobody in the group has built or financed a US$2.7B+ heap-leach copper mine at 3,500m+ in Argentina; Meding brings Barrick/Trafigura Andean experience but not a mine build as the responsible executive. Project financing of this size, IPO execution and Argentine construction are all new for them.
Skin & pay
5/5 — large stake bought with their own money, still buying. Rob McEwen owns ~16% of MUX (company site) and personally holds a stake in McEwen Copper (~13%, unverified); salary US$1/yr; bought heavily in the market over many years (>US$200M stated). Recent open-market MUX buying in 2026 not verified. CEO comp therefore nominal; other NEO pay from 2026 proxy not retrieved. Source: https://www.mcewenmining.com/about-us/management-team/default.aspx

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Repeated production and cost guidance misses (2019, 2024 Fox, 2025 consolidated).
  • IPO/FID dates for Los Azules have slipped ~3 years from first statements.
  • Heavy promotional tone from the chairman (price-target style statements at conferences).
  • Convertible notes and flow-through issued while chairman says the company is 'internally funding' growth.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was US$78.9M at 30 June 2026 plus US$12.8M of securities, up from US$13.7M in 2024, driven by US$58.3M of San José dividends in H1 2026.
  2. Revenue rose from US$174M in FY24 to US$198M in FY25 and US$133M in H1 2026, with gross margin after depreciation improving from 18% to 39%.
  3. Capex of US$40-45M a year means free cash flow before dividends was roughly nil until 2026; debt is a US$110M 5.25% convertible plus a US$20M related-party loan.
  4. Overhead is rising fast: G&A was US$17.4M in H1 2026 alone, about 13% of revenue; shares rose from 49.4M to 59.7M.
  5. McEwen Copper's Los Azules is now debt-funded with a US$240M 12% loan, US$85M of it from Rob McEwen, ahead of a planned IPO; MUX owns 46.3%.

Funded to the next catalyst None for 2026–27 Gaspé drilling and study work (>C$100M cash, no debt). Gaspé mine-build capex is a separate, much larger future requirement; OCMC is being financed on its own balance sheet.
Thesis

Large, defined, brownfield restart of the past-producing Gaspé (Noranda) copper-moly mine in tier-one Québec; up to 160,000 tpd throughput. Osisko team pedigree (Canadian Malartic, Windfall). Fully funded to a construction decision; Glencore in the cap table. MRE (Apr 2026): M&I 1.83 Bt @ 0.32% CuEq + Inf 239 Mt @ 0.46% CuEq = 10.8 Blb Cu, 673 Mlb Mo, 93 Moz Ag. Blue-sky: higher-grade porphyry at depth (852 m @ 0.95% CuEq).

The Gate

Low grade (0.32% CuEq) → economics hinge on scale + copper price, unproven until the PEA. Long-dated: restart ~2031, ~C$1.8B initial capex. Already re-rated hard (+300% 1-yr). PEA slipped — guided mid-2026, now late 2027 (Wares, 2 Oct 2026).

Valuation Anchor

~7–10¢/lb Cu (~6–8¢/lb CuEq) on M&I contained metal — richer than the cheap bucket. Third archetype: quality/jurisdiction premium — the near-mirror of Los Andes (cheap because permitting is a fight; Osisko dear because Québec + proven team + Glencore + brownfield is about as de-risked as copper gets).

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~7.8% — founder Robert Wares ~5.0%; John Burzynski ~1.6% (bought ~C$673k at C$0.90–0.98 Jan 2026, then sold 2M sh at ~C$1.45–1.74 in Aug 2026 — date corrected 16 Oct from Aug 2025); CFO, President and Corporate Secretary all net buyers (C$200–500k each). Strategic: Glencore ~11.9% (converted debenture Jul 2026, then sold 21.5M shares at ~C$1.60 on 28 Jul), Agnico Eagle ~10–11%, Hudbay ~3%, Franco-Nevada, CDPQ ~2%, Konwave ~3%.

Read: Meaningful — a founder with ~5% and an executive team buying on weakness, plus two majors.

Jurisdiction risk

National: arguably the best in the file — Québec, provincial government collaboration, established mining culture. Local: low — brownfield past-producing Noranda site at Murdochville, a mining town, with Mi'gmaq engagement in hand.

This is a large part of why it's expensive: de-risked jurisdiction is exactly what the market pays up for.

Differentiator

Brownfield — the only past-producing mine site in the file. Gaspé ran as Noranda's mine for decades, so tailings facilities, roads, power, port access and a mining town already exist, and the deposit's behaviour is known rather than modelled. That is why a 0.32% CuEq grade can still work: you're not paying to build a district. Second: management pedigree — the team that found, built and sold Canadian Malartic and Windfall, which is the closest thing to a track-record guarantee in this sector, plus Glencore on the register. Third: Québec — arguably the most de-risked mining jurisdiction on earth, with provincial support and Mi'gmaq engagement in hand.

This is precisely why it's dear: every differentiator here is a reason the market pays up, which is the mirror image of Los Andes.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, better tonnes · moves the needle: medium. Hole 30-1228, 800 m west of the MRE model: 256.5 m @ 0.85% Cu incl. 28.5 m @ 4.74% Cu; grade improving near Needle Mountain; Porphyry Mountain at depth (852 m @ 0.95% CuEq). Higher-grade material could reshape the PEA's grade profile. Already priced as a quality name.

Next Catalyst

Maiden PEA (overdue vs. guidance); ongoing conversion/expansion results (fully funded 110,000 m 2026 program); Porphyry Mountain. Funding path: CEO Wares has said he wants Investissement Québec or private equity at 20–25% project level to avoid equity dilution — watch for a project-level partner. Scotia target raised to C$3 (Sep 2026).

Open Questions
  • When does the PEA land, and what NPV/IRR at what copper price?
  • Does Needle Mountain / Porphyry Mountain lift the grade profile enough to matter?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 4/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 4/5

A team with two multi-billion exits and heavy insider buying, but the Gaspé PEA slipped from early 2025 to late 2027 without a headline admission and the Pine Point study vanished. Smaller cut because the slip itself was scored on 3 Oct.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 40% → 37%, odds of a 3× 7% → 7%.

People
Robert (Bob) Wares (CEO, founder, since 2020-01 (CEO); founder): Geologist; co-discoverer of Canadian Malartic (Osisko Mining Corp, sold C$3.9B 2014). Owns ~5%. · John Burzynski (Executive Chairman, since 2024-11): Ex-CEO Osisko Mining (Windfall sold to Gold Fields C$2.2B 2024); co-founder of original Osisko (Malartic); chair of O3 Mining (sold to Agnico Eagle early 2025). Named CEO of the planned spin-out Osisko Critical Minerals (Sept 2026). · Don Njegovan (President, since 2024-11): Ex-COO Osisko Mining; ex-Scotiabank mining banker; ex-director St Andrew Goldfields. · Blair Zaritsky (CFO, since 2024-11): Ex-CFO Osisko Mining.
Track record
  • Burzynski/Wares: Osisko Mining Corp - Canadian Malartic discovered, built (2011) and sold to Agnico/Yamana for C$3.9B (2014) - a genuine discovery-to-mine-to-sale record, Quebec, open pitsource
  • Burzynski: Osisko Mining (Windfall) - discovery to FS and sale to Gold Fields C$2.2B (2024) without building; O3 Mining sold to Agnico Eagle (2025, ~C$204M unverified)source
  • Misses: Osisko Metals' first asset Pine Point (NWT zinc) - FS promised Q2 2025 (Nov 2024), project since handed to Appian JV / wound down from the Osisko Metals story (outcome unverified); Gaspé PEA promised early 2025 has not appearedsource
  • Wins came in 2014 (gold, post-peak) and 2024 (gold bull) - all exits to majors; none in copper.
  • Funding: C$107M bought deal Dec 2024 at C$0.26; C$32.5M strategic placement Dec 2025 (Agnico ~12.5%, Hudbay ~4.3%); Glencore US$25M debenture converted July 2026source

Boards today: Burzynski: OM exec chair, incoming CEO of Osisko Critical Minerals (new listing), plus other Osisko-group boards (count unverified). Wares: OM CEO; other boards unverified. Board flagged: 5 new directors in 3 years.

Fit to this job
Stage: resource growth (824 Mt indicated) toward a PEA that was due early 2025 and is now (per owner's note) late 2027 - the team's model is drill-expand-sell, which fits an Agnico/Hudbay/Glencore-registered asset. Deposit/mining: open-pit porphyry/skarn copper at a past-producing Noranda mine site in Quebec - same province and open-pit method as Malartic, but copper flotation and a brownfield pit/tailings legacy are new. Nobody on the team has built a copper mine; the Malartic build was 2009-11 with a different operating team. The executive chairman is now also launching a spin-out.
Skin & pay
4/5 — meaningful stake with real market buying. Wares ~5% (~C$79M, founder stock + buys of C$259k); Burzynski 14.4M shares, net buyer C$3.1M then sold 2M shares Aug 2026; CFO Zaritsky bought C$500k; Njegovan bought C$208k - real market buying by the new team. CEO total pay C$1.83M last year at a ~C$1.6B company. Agnico Eagle ~12.5%, Hudbay ~4.3%, Glencore converted US$25M.source

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • PEA slipped from 'early 2025' to late 2027 with no headline admission.
  • Pine Point FS promised Q2 2025 was never delivered by the company.
  • CEO pay C$1.83M (73% equity) while the project has produced no economic study in six years under him.
  • Executive chairman becomes CEO of a sister company; sold C$2.9M of stock Aug 2026.
  • High board turnover.
  • Financials: 256.6M shares (Sep 2024) → 895M (Aug 2026) after the Glencore convertible converted; share-based pay C$13.0M in H1 2026 and cash overhead up from ~C$1.1M to ~C$2.9M a quarter.

Partly funded to the next catalyst Funded through permitting, engineering, early works and Pampa Medina drilling into 2027 (US$140M vs ~US$11M/quarter). Not funded for the US$587M initial MOD capex (+US$77M expansion): needs the project-debt package plus roughly US$200–300M of equity, stream or strategic capital before FID — the open item for 2027.
Thesis

Permitted, DFS-stage, low-capex oxide project in the Antofagasta coastal belt near the port of Mejillones — the fastest and cheapest build in the file, with first cathode targeted 2029. A new sulphide discovery at Pampa Medina is the free option on top.

The Gate

Closing the construction financing on non-dilutive terms. Endeavour Financial launched the MOD debt process in May 2026; a final funding strategy is targeted for Q4 2026 against US$587M capex. The equity share of that package is the single most consequential variable for shareholders. Secondary: SERNAGEOMIN sectoral permits (submitted Apr 2026, approvals now targeted October 2026) and surface rights. Acid supply largely de-risked: Marimaca bought its own sulphuric-acid plant (May 2026), removing most of a heap-leach project's exposure to acid cost. The company's illustrative planning split is ~US$350M equity + ~US$350M debt — a conservative scenario, not a signed structure.

Cash US$140M at 30 Jun 2026, no debt after the Feb 2026 C$409M global offering: C$136.5M of new shares at C$10.00 plus ~C$273M of secondary selling by Greenstone and others — which is why Greenstone fell from 21.6% to 6.4%, and a large part of why the stock has drifted since.

NPVAfter-tax NPV US$709M @ US$4.30/lb (US$1.1B @ US$5.05/lb; ≈US$1.6B extrapolated at US$6). Aug 2025 DFS, 8% discount.

NPV : capex1.21x@ base US$4.30/lb → 1.87× @ US$5.05 → ~2.7× @ US$6. IRR 31%. Payback 2.5 yr.The closest name in the file to Rick Rule's screen: the only developer clearing his 30% IRR bar at base case, with a sub-3-year payback; the NPV test passes from ~US$5.50 copper.
Valuation Anchor

~1.0× NAV at the DFS deck (US$4.30), ~0.67× at US$5.05, ~0.46× at an extrapolated US$6 deck. Quality you pay for — but the 2026 drawdown has reopened some discount, which is why it now leads the certainty ranking. EV ~US$580M.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~1–2% (CEO Hayden Locke ~0.5%; net insider selling ~C$2.9M over 12 months, including a director sale at C$11.58 Jan 2025). Strategic: Assore ~19.7%, Ithaki ~9.4%, Greenstone ~6.4% (sold ~C$137M in the Feb 2026 secondary), Mitsubishi ~3–4% (unverified), Konwave ~2.7%.

Read: Low — a strategic-holder register with modest, option-derived management ownership.

Jurisdiction risk

National: favourable (same Chilean reforms as Los Andes and Hot Chili). Local: low — coastal desert in an established mining and industrial corridor near Mejillones, low elevation, grid connection authorised (El Lince 110 kV line, 13 km, May 2026), RCA granted Nov 2025, no organised opposition campaign.

Like Hot Chili, and unlike Los Andes: same country, opposite local risk.

Differentiator

The best project economics in the file at a conservative price. 31% IRR, 2.5-year payback and ~US$11,700/t capital intensity at US$4.30 copper — while most developers here need US$5+ to look robust. Market cap already exceeds capex (~1.26×; only Ivanhoe also does), so financing is a question of terms, not survival. Cathode on site, no smelter or TC/RC exposure; port 45-minute drive; strategic register (Assore 18.7%, Ithaki ~9.4%, Greenstone 6.4%, Mitsubishi 3.4% as of Feb 2026).

Read honestly: 50 kt/yr is small — high-quality but not strategic scale for a major, which caps takeout appeal until Pampa Medina adds size.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, better tonnes — and potentially scale · moves the needle: medium-high. Pampa Medina: high-grade bornite zone extended (Jul 2026); 30,000 m delineation programme with six rigs concluding end-Sep 2026; maiden oxide + sulphide MRE targeted early 2027 — entirely outside the MOD mine plan. Management compares the stacked sediment-hosted system to Kamoa-Kakula; consistent mineralisation across 20+ holes over ~3 km × 1.5 km. On a 1.65 Blb reserve, a sulphide discovery could change what kind of company this is.

Next Catalyst

Sectoral permits (October 2026) + project-financing announcement (before end-2026) → pre-FID early works end-2026/early 2027 → FID and construction 2027 → first cathode 2029. Pampa Medina maiden MRE early 2027. Board strengthened (ex-First Quantum projects director, ex-Mantos Copper CEO).

Open Questions
  • What equity share does the Q4 2026 financing package require?
  • Does the acid self-supply route land?
  • Does Pampa Medina's maiden MRE (early 2027) add real scale?
  • Does the overhang from the Feb 2026 secondary sale clear once the financing package is announced?

Remaining construction permits still guided 'early October' and the financing package before year-end — neither announced yet. Ithaki holds ~9.4% (the 14.9% figure is stale).

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

Track record
  • Locke: Papillon Resources (Head of Corporate) sold to B2Gold for ~US$600M in 2014 - a win, in the 2011-14 gold cycle, but as corporate head not CEOsource
  • Locke: CEO of Emmerson plc (Khemisset potash, Morocco) from 2018; project's environmental permit was refused by Morocco and Emmerson is now pursuing a US$1.215B treaty arbitration - a miss as CEOsource
  • Locke at Marimaca since 2020: took the asset from PEA to DFS (Aug 2025), EIA approval (Nov 2025), C$80M raise 2025, C$409M global offering Feb 2026 (C$136.5M treasury) - no mine built yetsource
  • Chair Bruno: ran Mantos Copper as CEO (operator of Mantos Blancos and Mantoverde; Mantoverde sulphide expansion later built under Capstone) - direct Chilean oxide/sulphide copper operating and project recordsource
  • Board refreshed Mar 2026 toward builders: Wozniak (First Quantum, Cobre Panama/Kansanshi) joined; founders Stephens and Newall retired; Haworth stepped down as chairsource

Boards today: Locke: Marimaca CEO + director of Emmerson plc (2). Bruno: Marimaca chair; other boards not verified. Haworth (director): Gunnison Copper and others (circular lists multiple). Daly: Atlantic Lithium, Gemfields.

Fit to this job
Stage: team has NOT built a mine before as a group; the CEO is a banker/corporate-development executive, not a mine builder. Mitigant: the build chain hired in 2024-26 (Watson, Valenzuela, Munoz, Wozniak, Bruno) has built and run Chilean copper heap-leach/SX-EW and sulphide projects (Mantoverde, Mantos Blancos, Cobre Panama). Deposit/method: oxide heap leach SX-EW in Antofagasta region is exactly what Bruno/Valenzuela/Munoz ran. Region: Chile - yes. New for them: executing a US$587M build and project-finance package as this company, and the first FID.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. Insider holdings per 2025 circular: Locke 32,900 sh; Haworth 38,330 (plus Greenstone affiliate stake, since reduced to 6.4%); Petterson 72,997; Bruno 47,500; Daly nil; ~101.2M shares outstanding (May 2025, before Feb 2026 offering). Mostly grant-derived; no notable open-market CEO buying found. CEO 2024 total comp C$3,027,052 (salary C$592,880, share awards C$1,989,000, bonus C$445,172). Source: 2025 MIC https://marimaca.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/Notice-of-Annual-General-Meeting-and-Information-Circular-2025.pdf

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Largest shareholder Greenstone (chair-affiliated until Mar 2026) sold down from 18.6% to 6.4% in Feb 2026, right before the FID - the insider with the most information reduced exposure.
  • CEO holds only 32,900 shares (circa 0.03%) against C$3.0M 2024 pay; exposure is via grants, not purchases.
  • Executive pay is large for a pre-construction developer: CEO C$3.03M, CFO C$2.17M, Corp Dev C$1.94M (2024), non-exec directors C$283k-510k each.
  • CEO's other company (Emmerson) lost its only project to a permit refusal and is in arbitration.
  • Financials: corporate overhead up US$6.7M in Q4 2025 and US$5.4M in H1 2026 year on year; share-based pay US$10.7M in FY25 (41% of the net loss); 2025+ statement PDFs are image-only, five quarters estimated from the MD&A.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was US$140.0M at 30 June 2026; at US$3.8M a month that covers roughly three years, but the US$590M mine build needs separate project financing.
  2. H1 2026 put US$16.6M into drilling and acid-plant work against US$5.9M of operating outflow; in 2025 overhead was almost as big as ground spend.
  3. Shares rose 34% from 101.0M to 135.0M on about US$176M of net equity, including US$94.4M from the February 2026 global offering.
  4. Overhead is growing fast with the Chile team build-out and ASX listing, and share-based pay was US$10.7M in 2025, 41% of the loss.
  5. No debt or streams; the Rayrock receivable was impaired three times, and US$18.4M of Chilean VAT credits await refund from late 2026.

Valuation Anchor

~C$750M market cap (C$1.99, 15 Oct 2026; ~US$527M) — still the priciest explorer per contained lb in this file. A grade/optionality bet, not a value bet; premium already in the price. C$141M cash at 30 Jun 2026 (the C$2.50 warrants were all exercised by Feb 2026), so no financing need before the 2H 2027 resource update.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~13% — dominated by Pierre Lassonde ~10.3% (added 1.8M sh for C$4.7M Nov 2025); Chairman Craig Nelsen ~2.1%; operating management <1% each. Strategic: Agnico Eagle ~15.5%. Funds: ASA Gold ~4.1%, Franklin Templeton ~3.9%, RWC ~2.1%.

Read: High — Lassonde and Agnico hold ~26% between them and both bought recently; management proper is small.

Jurisdiction risk

National: favourable (Chile). Local: low-to-moderate, but untested — north-central Chile, no organised opposition known, though a project this early hasn't yet faced an EIA. Contractor fatality (Apr 2026) is an operational, not licence, issue.

Watch as it advances toward a study — local risk is unpriced at this stage.

Differentiator

Grade — by a wide margin the best in the file. Indicated 0.88% CuEq / 0.58% Cu vs. Los Andes 0.36% Cu reserve, Aldebaran 0.42%, Osisko 0.32% CuEq; B2B breccia hits run 3–4% CuEq. High-grade pounds mean lower capex intensity and fatter margins if an economic study ever confirms them. Second: cap-table quality — Agnico Eagle at ~15.5% plus Pierre Lassonde as #2 holder is endorsement from people who buy assets for a living, and it's 100%-owned with no JV, so a takeout needs no partner's consent.

Caveat: the differentiator is already the reason it's the priciest name here per contained pound — you're not getting the grade cheaply.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, better tonnes · moves the needle: medium-high. B2B high-grade breccia now ~600 m of strike and still open; 20 m @ 4.10% CuEq within 78 m @ 3.03% CuEq. High grade near the core should lift the starter economics of a maiden PEA — the best 'better tonnes' story in the file. Much of it is already in the price.

Next Catalyst

Maiden PEA/economic study; permanent CEO appointment; continued B2B growth.

Fit to this job
Exploration-stage team in Chile, and that is exactly what they have been doing for five years with success. No development or build experience in the executive ranks; Agnico as a 15% holder provides a technical backstop but no operating control.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$141.0M at 30 June 2026; at about C$22M of burn a quarter that covers roughly six quarters, including the Phase VII drill programme.
  2. Nearly all money goes into the ground: H1 2026 exploration was C$37.2M against about C$4.5M of cash overhead, roughly 11% of spend.
  3. Shares rose 81% from 208.1M to 376.2M through Agnico Eagle's C$55.7M, a C$109.9M bought deal and about C$115M of warrant exercises.
  4. No debt and no revenue; the former US$15M credit facility was converted into shares in November 2024.
  5. A C$29.5M unexplained PP&E addition appeared in the September 2025 quarter, and share-based pay was C$9.8M over the 15-month period.

Valuation Anchor

~1.5–1.9¢/lb attributable (US$442M ÷ 25.4 Blb M&I+Inf × 80%; ~2.5¢/lb on the 22.0 Blb M&I alone) — among the cheapest defined pounds in the file, with the financing flag as the reason why.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~5.6% (management & directors; CEO John Black ~1.3%, CGO Kevin Heather ~1.3%, mostly via option exercises). Control: Route One ~41% (added C$5M in the Feb 2026 placement), South32 ~13.6%, Sibanye-Stillwater ~13.1% at the company level (on top of its 20% project interest).

Read: Moderate — one fund and two miners dominate the register; management's exposure is modest.

Jurisdiction risk

National: favourable and locked (Argentina RIGI, San Juan). Local: low — remote high-altitude, mining-supportive province, Centauri spun out so no Salta exposure. Risk is financing, not licence.

Differentiator

A genuine high-grade core inside a very cheap bulk deposit — 513 m @ 1.06% CuEq sits within a 0.42% average, which is the profile that lets a PFS design a high-margin starter pit and transform payback vs. the PEA's flat 20.5% IRR. Second: 48-year mine life — the longest here, and scarcity-asset duration majors pay up for. Third: Sibanye-Stillwater at 20% project level (not just a share stake) — a producing miner already carrying its share.

Counterweight: Nuton walked in Nov 2025, so the "majors validate it" case is weaker than it was. Offset: Route One (largest shareholder) wrote a cheque into the Feb 2026 raise.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, mostly conversion · moves the needle: medium. Infill (513 m @ 1.06% CuEq) confirms a high-grade core, which should shape a PFS starter pit; ~9.8 Blb Inferred still to convert.

Extra tonnes add little to a 48-year life — the core grade is what matters.

Entry plan · €1,000 as an illustration
Step 0 · written, nothing boughtThree alerts set: the updated Altar resource (guided October 2026), a price alert at C$2.50 (~15% below today), and any release containing "partner", "strategic", "financing" or "placement". Plan written 1 Oct 2026 at ~C$2.99 (18 Sep close; 52-week range C$1.93–4.20; last placement C$3.25 in Feb 2026). The €1,000 is illustrative (≈ C$1,500 ≈ ~500 shares) — the point is the 40/30/30 split and the events, not the amount; scale it.

A decision tree tied to events, not dates. Three tranches assume cheap TSXV access; at a German bank charging €25–60 per foreign order, collapse it to two (€600 now / €400 at Step 4) — at this size the fee drag beats the timing gain. Not advice; my read written down in advance so that on the day I compare numbers against thresholds I set beforehand, not against the price move.

Two things to be honest about before Step 1. First, most of the multiple is copper, not progress: progress alone is ~1–1.5× at today's ~US$442M (was ~1.3–2× at ~US$350M), the 3.7–6× column needs the market to adopt US$6 as its long-term copper price (spot is already ~US$6.5), and the PEA's 20.5% IRR at US$4.35 fails the Rule screen — if you don't hold a bullish copper view this is the wrong name. Second, the horizon event is a study plus a partner, not a mine: ~US$1.6B of capex on a ~US$442M cap (15 Oct 2026; ~US$350M when the plan was written) means heavy dilution or a partner at FID, and Nuton (Rio) walked in Nov 2025. This is also the third copper developer in the file after Hot Chili and Copper Giant — all three move on the same copper beta and the same financing cycle.

Step 1first tranche now: €400 (~40%), because the stock is under the insiders' last cheque and the best event is undated

Buy €400 (~200 shares) with a limit order at or below C$3.10 on the TSXV. Reason: C$2.99 is below the C$3.25 placement that Route One (41% holder) topped up in February, the October resource is low-downside (infill conversion, not a verdict), and the one event that can print any week — a partner replacing Rio at project level — has no date. Being partly in is the price of not missing it.

  1. Not filled and the stock runs? Don't chase above C$3.40 — that is above the placement with nothing new announced. Wait for Step 2.
  2. Falls to the C$2.50 alert with no news? Fill the €400 there and bring €150 of Step 4 forward — a no-news drawdown in a funded name with a dated study ahead is the entry the plan hopes for.
Step 2the updated Altar resource (guided October 2026): read three numbers and one sentence before doing anything
WhatGreenRed
M&I tonnage≥ 2.4 Bt (does not shrink)< 2.0 Bt, or a cut-off change that hides a shrink
The high-grade corestated as its own domain — on the order of ≥ 100 Mt at ≥ 0.8% CuEqfolded into the 0.42% average, no core quantified
Inferred → M&I conversiona meaningful share of the 9.8 Blb Inferred moves upInferred grows while M&I is flat — the drilling found tonnes, not confidence
The sentence"will form the basis of the PFS mine plan" / "starter pit""further drilling required" / no reference to the PFS

Three or four green → the starter-pit thesis is intact. Core not quantified → hold; the PFS thesis depends on that number. Two or more red → stop, do not buy the dip, re-run the card.

Step 3second tranche: €300 (~30%) — on the resource, not before it
  1. Mostly green and the stock falls ≥ 10% on the day or within the following week → buy €300 in the market. The fall is positioning, not the project.
  2. Mostly green and the stock rises → buy €300 anyway within two weeks; don't chase beyond +20%.
  3. Core not quantified or red → nothing. Wait for Step 4 or Step 5.
Step 4third tranche: €300 (~30%) — the PFS (guided Q2/Q3 2027), read against thresholds set now
WhatGreenRed
After-tax IRR≥ 25% at a copper deck ≤ US$4.50/lb — or a phased plan whose first phase shows NPV ≥ 2× its own capex< 18% at the deck
Initial capex≤ US$2.0B (PFS numbers usually rise from a PEA's US$1.6B)> US$2.3B
Payback≤ 4 years at the deck> 6 years

Three green → buy €300. Two of three → half. IRR red → stop; hold Step 1 only and reassess whether the asset is a partner's, not a shareholder's. If nothing else has triggered by the PFS and the PFS is green, deploy on it anyway — cash held for a dip that never comes is how this plan fails.

Step 5overrides — events that change the plan whatever step it is at
  1. Buy the remaining tranches that day: a producer or major takes a project-level interest or funds the PFS/FS (≥ US$100M of funding or ≥ 20% of Altar). That converts the financing gate from open to half-closed; the price on the day is irrelevant against it.
  2. Pull Step 2/4 money forward: a copper drawdown of 20%+ in the stock with the story unchanged — no company news, just the metal.
  3. Stop adding and review: an equity raise before the PFS (it means the February money was not enough); a raise below C$2.50 not tied to a partner; any sign of Argentina's RIGI being reopened.
  4. Exit regardless of the study: Route One or South32 reported selling.
Step 6once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if the PFS lands red on IRR and no partner has appeared by end-2027 — the asset then belongs to whoever funds it, at a price set by them.
  2. Sell half if the stock doubles before the PFS or a partner is signed. A double on copper alone is worth banking half of; the thesis is a study and a partner, not the metal.
  3. Otherwise hold through the PFS and the partner process into 2028. Don't trade the infill holes in between — the core grade is known; what changes the value is the mine plan built on it.
PracticalWhere to buy, currency, and the most likely outcome

Liquidity is on the TSXV (ALDE) in CAD; the OTC (ADBRF) and Frankfurt lines are thin — limit orders only, priced off the Toronto close converted to EUR, never market orders. You take CAD/EUR on top of the copper exposure and cannot hedge it at this size. Most likely single outcome: the October resource confirms the core, the stock moves ±10%, the PFS comes in with higher capex and an IRR in the low 20s at a US$4.25–4.50 deck, and the real re-rate waits for a partner in 2027–28. The money is not in the timing — it is in whether Altar's starter pit survives the PFS and who pays for the build.

Plan log: 1 Oct 2026 — plan written at ~C$2.99; Step 0, nothing bought; marked as pick in tracker and rankings.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

A real prior sale (Antares, C$650M) and plain disclosure; Regulus unresolved after 14 years, Nuton walked, and the team has never built.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
John E. Black (CEO & Director, since 2018-06): Economic geologist; founded Antares Minerals (Haquira, Peru), also CEO of Regulus Resources. · Kevin B. Heather (Chief Geological Officer & Director, since 2018): Co-founder Antares/Regulus; Haquira East discovery. · Mark Wayne (CFO & Director, since 2018): Also CFO of Regulus; investment adviser at IA Securities — part-time CFO. · Stanford Foy (VP Project Development, since unverified): Ex-Sibanye-Stillwater corporate development, 18 yrs at Stillwater.
Track record
  • Hit (2010, last cycle): Antares Minerals (Haquira) sold to First Quantum for C$650Msource
  • Unresolved: Regulus Resources (AntaKori, Peru), run by the same trio since 2012, has not been sold or built after 14 years (company site; outcome check unverified)
  • Altar: earned 80% from Sibanye-Stillwater by spending US$25M (completed 30 Jun 2024); PEA Oct 2025 NPV8 US$2.0B, IRR 20.5%, 48-yr lifesource
  • Nuton (Rio Tinto) option to JV signed Nov 2024, terminated by Nuton Nov 2025 citing a shift to later-stage projectssource
  • Financing: C$40M bought deal Feb 2026; spun out northern Argentina assets as Centauri Minerals (listed Aug 2026, C$25M raised)source

Boards today: Black: CEO/director Aldebaran and Regulus (2 public exec roles), likely Centauri involvement (unverified). Heather and Wayne: same two companies each.

Fit to this job
Same deposit type (Andean copper porphyry) and same team that found and sold Haquira; Argentina/San Juan is where they have worked since 2018. They are explorers and sellers, not builders: no mine built, and Altar is a 48-year, multi-billion-dollar project at altitude. Fit is good for the current task (define, de-risk, sell) and weak if the task becomes construction. Management runs two companies in parallel.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Black ~1.3% direct (2.4M shares, added via option exercises Dec 2024, not open-market); CEO total comp C$140k salary (Simply Wall St, year unverified) — low for the company size (~C$600M market cap, unverified). Insider open-market buying not found. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-alde/aldebaran-resources-shares/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Rio Tinto's Nuton exited after a year — a sophisticated partner passed.
  • Shareholder rights plan adopted Mar 2026.
  • Part-time CFO and shared management with Regulus; low board refreshment.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$49.4M at 31 March 2026; at the recent C$3.9M a quarter that is about 3 years, or 7 quarters at drilling-season burn of C$7M.
  2. Money went mainly into the ground: C$22.1M in FY24, C$30.5M in FY25 and C$9.9M in nine months of FY26, against C$2.2-2.5M of cash overhead a year.
  3. Shares rose from 148.2M in 2023 to 185.3M in March 2026; the February 2026 C$45.25M bought deal at C$3.25 added 9%.
  4. Rio Tinto's Nuton paid C$50.1M in FY25 then quit the option, leaving Aldebaran with 80% of Altar; no debt or streams.
  5. Argentine VAT write-downs of about C$5M a year hit reported results, and the auditor notes a going-concern uncertainty every period.

Thesis

One of the largest undeveloped copper-gold porphyries in a tier-one country, with a feasibility study, five years of cash, two strategic holders and a project now on Ottawa's investment-summit prospectus — trading at ~0.24× its stale 2022-deck NPV (US$411M, 15 Oct 2026) and under 0.07× at spot metal prices, because the market will not pay for a permit clock with no end date.

Risk score3/5A completed FS, C$128M of cash, Rio Tinto and Mitsubishi on the register and a pro-development territorial government; against that, a first-of-its-kind, open-ended panel review, a C$3.6B capex about five times the market cap, a cyanide heap leach in a post-Eagle-Gold Yukon and no signed First Nation benefit agreement.
Market cap2 Oct 2026: ~US$489M (C$3.08 · ~C$697M on ~226.2M shares). ~US$525M (Sep 2026; ~C$742M at C$3.28 on 226M shares, Sep 25; 52-wk C$2.62–5.74). Cash and short-term investments C$128.6M (Jun 30, 2026) after a C$92M bought deal at C$4.15 in Feb 2026; no debt; ~5 years of runway at the current spend.
Capex / IRRInitial capex US$2.89B (C$3.62B); after-tax IRR 18.1% @ 2022 deck (US$3.60 Cu, US$1,700 Au). Jun 2022 FS. Payback 3.3 yr. Company's Aug 2026 "consensus deck" (US$5.00 Cu, US$3,500 Au): IRR ~39%, payback 1.6 yr. No capex re-estimate since 2022.
NPVAfter-tax NPV US$1.7B (C$2.33B) @ 2022 deck, 8% discount; C$2.79B @ US$4.00 Cu; company's consensus-deck figure ~C$9.2B (US$5.00 Cu / US$3,500 Au). Broker NAVs cluster ~C$5B at US$4.50 Cu / US$2,500 Au.
DepositP&P 1.43 Bt — 5.24 Blb Cu, 10.3 Moz Au(mill 1,217 Mt @ 0.19% Cu, 0.22 g/t Au, 0.021% Mo + heap leach 210 Mt @ 0.26 g/t Au; plus 572 Mlb Mo, 78 Moz Ag); M&I 2,491 Mt (7.64 Blb Cu, 14.8 Moz Au) + Inferred 1,413 Mt (3.08 Blb Cu, 6.3 Moz Au) — the reserve is about a third of the resource. 120,000 tpd mill + 25,000 tpd heap leach, 27-year life, strip 0.43:1; years 1–4 ~241 Mlb Cu + ~333 koz Au; C1 negative net of by-products.
NPV : capex0.64x@ 2022 deck → ~0.77× @ US$4.00 Cu → ~2.5× at the consensus deck. IRR 18.1% base. Payback 3.3 yr.Fails Rule at base — the thinnest cushion in the file below Highland's; at spot metal prices it clears both tests easily. Everything about this name depends on which deck you believe.
Valuation Anchor

~0.31× NAV at the 2022 deck (US$3.60 Cu / US$1,700 Au), ~0.25× at US$4.00 Cu, under 0.1× at spot metals. EV ~US$430M / 5.24 Blb reserve Cu ≈ 8¢/lb — but that ignores 10 Moz of gold; on a CuEq basis it is among the cheapest defined pounds in the file. Market cap ~0.18× capex.

Same bucket as Los Andes: a deep, computable discount on a real study, with the permit process — not the rock — as the whole reason.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~4–5% — CEO Sandeep Singh bought in via placement on appointment (2023); directors O'Hara and Psihogios bought into the C$4.15 raise (Feb 2026); one officer sold through 2025. Strategics: Rio Tinto ~8.5% (investor-rights agreement expires Nov 30, 2026 — the standstill and lock-up fall away, board rights already removed in Sep 2025; Rio did not participate in the Feb raise) and Mitsubishi Materials ~5% (bought on-market in Jul 2026 to keep its rights to 2028). Institutions ~31%: Kopernik 5.8%, Tidal 3.7%, Konwave 3.6%.

Read: Moderate — insiders own a little and bought at the top; what matters is what Rio does on Dec 1.

Jurisdiction risk

National: favourable — Canada critical-minerals list, Major Projects Office short-list, Casino on the Sep 2026 Canada Investment Summit prospectus, Yukon–BC grid link named a federal priority transmission project (Jun 2026); Yukon Party government pro-development. Local: moderate, and raised by Eagle Gold. Victoria Gold's 2024 heap-leach failure hardened the territory: CPAWS Yukon wants the Casino heap leach reclassified to the highest hazard class and Klaza caribou is a live issue. Five First Nations; cooperation agreements with Selkirk (2014) and Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in (2015), capacity agreements with others, no IBA with any; Little Salmon/Carmacks flags the access road across settlement land. No formal opposition — and no formal support. New chair Mark E. Smith advised the Yukon government on heap-leach practice after Eagle — a deliberate signal.

Differentiator

Scale with a gold engine. 5.2 Blb Cu and 10.3 Moz Au in reserve — gold is ~45% of revenue at spot, which makes Casino the most gold-weighted NAV in the file, with a C1 copper cost that goes negative net of by-products. Second: the strategic register — Rio Tinto (~8.5%) and Mitsubishi Materials (~5%, rights and pro-rata offtake extended to 2028) are the two most credible eventual builders or buyers, and both are already inside the tent. Third: five years of cash — no dilution pressure while the panel runs.

The flip side: at C$3.6B of capex, Western will not build this alone; the value crystallises through a partner or a takeout, and the timing of that is in Rio's hands as much as YESAB's.

Exploration upside

Beyond-reserve scale · moves the needle: low–medium. The reserve is ~⅓ of M&I + Inferred; 2026 brought the first property-wide geophysics in years across 21,300 ha and oxide-cap metallurgy that could lift heap-leach gold. Scale is already the point — the multiple hinges on permits and a partner, not more tonnes.

Next Catalyst

Rio Tinto investor-rights expiry, Nov 30, 2026 (a decision point, not necessarily a re-rate); YESAB sufficiency determination and Panel terms of reference (undated — plausibly Q4 2026–H1 2027); Panel hearings later; grid and road funding decisions; any FS refresh at current metal prices.

Open Questions
  • What does Rio do when its agreement lapses on Nov 30, 2026 — renew, sell down, top up, or bid?
  • When does YESAB declare the statement sufficient, and how long is the Panel?
  • Does the heap leach survive post-Eagle scrutiny in its current class?
  • Does any First Nation sign a benefit agreement before the hearings?
  • Who funds C$3.6B?

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Sandeep Singh (President, CEO, Director, since 2024-02): Age 46. Ex-CEO Osisko Gold Royalties (2020-2023); 15 yrs banker (BMO, Dundee); co-founder Maxit Capital. No mine-building or operating record. · Mark E. Smith (Chairman (independent), since 2026-08): P.Eng., 45 yrs heap-leach/tailings; 12 yrs on Yukon projects; chaired the Eagle Gold (Victoria Gold) failure review board. Replaced Ray Threlkeld (chair since June 2024). · Bob Dirk (COO, since 2026-01): 37 yrs; Suncor Fort Hills mega-project; Kaz Minerals Peschanka - the first true large-project builder on staff. · Christian Roldan (VP Technical, since 2026-01): Ex-Newmont study lead; ex-mine GM in Central America.
Track record
  • Singh: as Osisko Gold Royalties CEO he ran a royalty company, not a mine; left 2023; no prior developer or builder rolesource
  • Founder/long-time chair Dale Corman (Western Silver sold to Glamis ~US$1.2B 2006) has left the board; the board now has no founder, three chairs in two years (Corman > Threlkeld 2024 > Smith 2026)source
  • Casino: 2022 FS; company has been in Yukon's YESAB process since the 2010s; ESE Statement finally submitted Oct 3 2025 and is still in 'sufficiency' review with supplementary information requestssource
  • Rio Tinto 8% (2021) and Mitsubishi Materials ~5% (2023, topped up on-market 2026) as strategic holders; C$92M bought deal Feb 2026; cash ~C$135Msource
  • Director Threlkeld: Rainy River sold to New Gold US$310M (2013), Newmarket to Kirkland Lake (2016) - real developer exits, but as director not CEO here.

Boards today: Singh: WRN only (as found). Smith: WRN chair plus consulting/review roles. Threlkeld: New Found Gold director. Zeitler: Amerigo exec chair, Rio2 lead director. Only 3 of 7 directors independent (Simply Wall St).

Fit to this job
Stage: permitting a C$3.6B+ (2022 FS) Yukon porphyry through a YESAB panel review - nobody on the executive has done a panel review; Smith, Shaw and Miller (ex-Yukon government) know the territory. Deposit/mining: very large open-pit porphyry with a heap leach and a major tailings facility in a cold climate - Smith's specialty is exactly heap leach/tailings and he reviewed the Eagle Gold heap failure; Dirk has mega-project (oil sands) experience. New for CEO: Singh is a capital-markets executive running a technical permitting slog; Mitsubishi/Rio relationships are his strength.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Singh owns 1.11% (~C$7.1M), mostly grants; CFO Psihogios bought C$127k at C$4.15 (Feb 2025); insiders net buyers C$1.6M over 12 months (options exercises included). Director Vitton holds 3.0%. CEO total comp C$4.0M (2024, sign-on year) and C$2.0M (2025). Rio Tinto 8%, Mitsubishi ~5%.source

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • CEO pay C$4.0M (2024) and C$2.0M (2025), 73% equity, at a ~C$640M pre-permit developer with no revenue - rich for the stage.
  • Three chairs in two years; founder gone.
  • Permitting has no company-stated end date; YESAB panel review has not formally begun 13 years after the project entered the process (entry date unverified).
  • Minority of independent directors.

Thesis

A very large, near-surface porphyry at low elevation (~1,650 m) close to highways, power, water and the ports of Matarani and Ilo — the opposite of the high-Andes builds — owned 100% and funded to keep drilling.

The Gate

Converting a large low-grade Inferred resource into economics. At 0.34% Cu, Pecoy's margin depends on scale, the by-product credits and low elevation keeping costs down, which only a PEA will show. The kilometre-long intercepts show continuity, not economics. Secondary: social licence in Arequipa.

DepositInferred 865 Mt @ 0.34% Cu (~6.5 Blb Cu)Plus gold, molybdenum and silver credits (Apr 2025 MRE, Mining Plus). Company's first holes: PEC25-065 1,014 m @ 0.37% Cu + 0.13 g/t Au from 17 m; PEC25-066 1,020.5 m @ 0.43% Cu + 0.09 g/t Au from 48 m. Sep 1, 2026: PEC26-072 804 m @ 0.34% Cu, 0.08 g/t Au from 24 m (third broad South Breccia intercept) and Northwest 42.3 m @ 1.01% Cu near surface, expanding the footprint. Under 49,000 m of historic drilling; open along strike and at depth; 2026 programme ~35,000 m. Tororume (100%, 8 km north): all nine historic holes mineralised.
NPV : capexn/a — no study.
Valuation Anchor

~3.6–3.9¢/lb Cu on EV (~US$235–255M / 6.5 Blb, 2 Oct) — still the priciest per pound among the defined-resource juniors here (Kodiak ~2.3¢, Copper Giant ~1.3¢, Aldebaran ~1.1–1.4¢), roughly level with Atex (~3.5¢) without Atex's grade. You're paying for scale, low elevation and the long intercepts.

(Corrected Sep 22 — the earlier 4.4¢ used a stale Feb market cap.)

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~20% — director Jerrold Annett ~9.1% (net buyer >C$1.7M late 2025, +280k sh at C$1.78 Jan 2026), Luis Zapata ~4.7%, CEO Vincent Metcalfe ~2.7%, CGO Vincent Cardin-Tremblay ~2.0%, Chairman Paul Matysek ~1.3% (bought Sep 2025 and again Sep 10 2026). Insiders net +C$2.3M over 12 months. Institutions ~8% (Konwave ~2.2% named); no strategic holder.

Read: Strong — high ownership plus sustained open-market buying.

Jurisdiction risk

National: mixed — Peru has world-class geology and volatile politics. Local: moderate, untested — Arequipa hosts major copper operations, but Southern Copper's Tía María in the same region was stalled for more than a decade by local opposition. No organised campaign against Pecoy is known; engagement is described as close coordination with local stakeholders.

Differentiator

Scale at low elevation, 100% owned and funded. 6.5 Blb in one near-surface system, open-pit geometry, year-round access and coastal logistics are a rare combination among Andean porphyries.

The flip side: the market already prices it like a more advanced project.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, mostly more tonnes · moves the needle: medium–high. Kilometre-long intercepts from near surface at grades slightly above the resource average; breccia centres (South and Central) as possible higher-grade zones; ~5,000 m at Tororume in 2026 for district scale.

Next Catalyst

2026 drill results (four rigs since September; several holes with assays pending); initial metallurgical testwork; Tororume drilling; updated geological model; updated MRE / PEA (undated).

Open Questions
  • Does metallurgy support good recoveries on a 0.34% Cu ore?
  • (A May 2026 Phase 1 review by GRE flagged a potential step-change in gold recovery — historic testwork optimised for copper only.) Do the breccia zones give a higher-grade starter pit?
  • When does the resource convert to Indicated, and when is a PEA?
  • How is Arequipa's social licence handled?
