Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Proven sellers of juniors at cycle tops, well funded; no porphyry or Peru record, split attention, and the founders' stake is mostly cheap founder stock.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Vincent Metcalfe (President, CEO, Director, co-founder, since 2025-06-30): Age 41. Ex-CEO/Chair Nomad Royalty (sold to Sandstorm 2022); ex-CFO Falco Resources; ex-VP IR Osisko Gold Royalties. Also CEO of Comet Lithium since Dec 2023. Finance/royalty background, not an operator. · Paul Matysek (Chairman, co-founder, since 2025): Serial company seller: says six companies sold for >C$3B since 2007 (Energy Metals, Potash One, Lithium One, Goldrock, Lithium X, Gold X). Chairs several other juniors today. · Vincent Cardin-Tremblay (Chief Geological Officer, since 2025): Runs the 40,000 m programme. · Luis Zapata (Managing Director Peru, Director, since 2025): In-country lead. Javier del Rio (Hudbay SVP US) joined board May 2026.
Track record
  • Matysek: six public companies sold since 2007 for >C$3B in aggregate per company statement, incl. Gold X to Gran Colombia (~C$365M, 2021), Lithium X to NextView (C$265M, 2018), Potash One to K+S (C$434M, 2011), Energy Metals to Uranium One (~C$1.8B, 2007)source
  • Matysek misses / open positions: Freeman Gold (exec chair), LithiumBank (exec chair), Nevada King (chair), Millennial Potash - none sold; most trade far below financing prices (price performance unverified). He has never built a mine; every win was a sale to a bigger company, mostly at cycle tops (2007 uranium, 2011 potash, 2018 lithium, 2021 gold).
  • Metcalfe: Nomad Royalty founded 2020, sold to Sandstorm Gold 2022 (~US$590M, unverified figure); CFO of Falco Resources (Horne 5, never built) to 2018source
  • Pecoy RTO Sept 2025: project consolidated from Copper X Mining, Pembrook Copper and private vendors; C$35M raise upsized to C$63.5M at $0.60source

Boards today: Matysek: 13 listed positions per TipRanks (chair of Pecoy, Freeman Gold, Nevada King, LithiumBank; director Nano One, others) - heavily overcommitted. Metcalfe: CEO of two companies at once (Pecoy and Comet Lithium).

Fit to this job
Stage: explorer with a historic 865 Mt inferred resource moving to PEA - the Matysek model (buy, drill, sell) fits this stage exactly. Deposit type: porphyry copper in southern Peru - new for both founders (Matysek's wins were uranium, potash, lithium, gold; Metcalfe is a finance/royalty executive). Jurisdiction: Peru is covered by Zapata, Luque and new director del Rio; the founders have no Peru operating history. Nobody on the team has built or permitted a porphyry mine; the exit plan is a sale, not a build.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. ~37% of 202.6M shares were escrowed insider/founder stock at the RTO (founders' seed shares, i.e. cheap paper rather than market buys); related parties put C$777k into the $0.60 placement. Matysek bought C$80k in the market Sept 2026. Options outstanding 7.5M. Management comp C$543k for nine months to Jan 2026 (all NEOs); CEO-specific pay not yet in a circular. (MD&A: https://www.pecoycopper.com/_resources/financials/Pecoy_Copper_Corp_MDA_Q3_2026.pdf?v=092502)

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Chairman holds ~13 public positions; CEO runs a second company - attention is split.
  • 'Management to subscribe up to C$8.5M' at RTO became C$777k actually subscribed.
  • No PEA date given; 'advance toward PEA' is the only timeline.
  • Promotional framing of kilometre-scale low-grade intercepts (0.3-0.4% Cu).

Partly funded to the next catalyst Funded for 2+ years at the current minimal spend, but not to a DFS or a permitting decision: any resumption of drilling or DFS work needs new equity, and the debenture interest is partly paid in shares. The company says it depends on equity markets.
Thesis

Cheap, de-risked reserves — ~2.9¢/lb reserve Cu vs. a ~US$2.8B PFS NPV (US$3.68/lb); P/NAV roughly 0.1. P&P 1.22 Bt @ 0.36% Cu / 0.41% CuEq.

The Gate

Chilean environmental permitting in the Rocín/Putaendo valley — protected-area campaign + social license. Water-source risk largely engineered away via desalination; the live risk is the protected-area push and years of SEIA + litigation. Mine EIA still not filed.

Valuation Anchor

~2.9¢/lb reserve Cu; P/NAV ~0.1. Queen's Road convertibles still being serviced (routine).

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~0.3% direct (officers & directors). Control sits with Turnbrook Corporation ~47% — the private vehicle whose mining interests Chairman Eduardo Covarrubias oversaw (ultimate owner not disclosed) — and Resource Capital Funds ~13%. Queen's Road Capital holds US$9M of convertibles (US$14M before the 2021 debenture converted in Apr 2026) (interest paid in shares; equity % undisclosed). No open-market insider buying found 2025–26.

Read: Skin in the game is very high at the controlling-shareholder level but near zero for operating management — a takeover is effectively one negotiation with Turnbrook, and minorities ride its decisions.

Jurisdiction risk

National: favourable, time-boxed. Kast (Mar 2026–Mar 2030) pro-mining — permitting acceleration, tax 27%→23%, 25-yr invariability >US$50M; but no congressional majority and no re-election. Local: the highest risk in the file. Rocín/Putaendo protected-area campaign, organised water/agricultural opposition, SEIA + environmental courts; EIA unfiled, so decisive rulings may straddle the 2030 transition. Company's litigation against the Putaendo mayor and a local scientist is a social-licence yellow flag. Precedents to fear: Dominga, Pascua-Lama — economic projects killed outright. This risk is the source of the ~0.1× NAV discount, not a reason to discount it again.

Differentiator

Cheapest P/NAV in the file (~0.1) on a reserve-stage asset in tier-one Chile — and a rare 100%-owned, unencumbered pure-play with no major, no JV partner, no stream. That means a takeover needs no one else's consent: the cleanest acquisition target here. Low strip + moderate altitude + near existing roads/power gives first-quartile early C1 ($0.93/lb) despite a modest 0.36% head grade.

The whole discount is one variable — permitting — which is unusually legible for an investor: you're underwriting one binary, not five.

Exploration upside

Geological inference · moves the needle: low. A large Inferred resource sits beyond the reserve (1.8 Bt), but there's no active step-out story — exploration isn't the thesis. Value lies in the permit or a farm-in.

Next Catalyst

Strategic partner; EIA submission; permanent CEO.

Open Questions
  • Will a mining major farm in (the key validation signal)?
  • When is the EIA filed — and can it clear SEIA before the 2030 transition?
  • Who becomes permanent CEO after the Montt debacle?
  • Does the Kast reform bill pass with the invariability regime intact?
Context & updates
3 Oct 2026 refresh

Convertibles settled: US$9M outstanding (two Queen's Road debentures, US$4M and US$5M from 2022); the 2021 US$5M debenture converted into shares in April 2026. The stock fell ~19% to C$12.31 on thin volume with no news.

CEO episode (Jan 2026) — corrected Sep 18

CEO Santiago Montt was slated to be Kast's Minister of Mines, and Los Andes announced it before the president-elect did. Kast dropped him hours later at the cabinet unveiling over that breach; Daniel Mas took Mining as bi-minister (Economy + Mining). Montt had already resigned; Antony Amberg (chief geologist) is interim CEO, search ongoing. Net negative, not a tailwind: lost the CEO, gained no ministry insider, handed the opposition a conflict-of-interest narrative about Vizcachitas, and the Valparaíso senator-elect (Frente Amplio) who attacked the appointment now sits in a 25–25 Senate.

Chilean political backdrop (Sep 2026)

Kast (Republican, 58% runoff, in office since Mar 11, 2026, term to Mar 2030, no consecutive re-election) is strongly pro-mining — day-one decree to clear 50 stalled administrative claims (~US$16B), Economy+Mining merged under Daniel Mas, Apr 22 bill: corporate tax 27%→23% by 2029, 25-yr tax invariability for projects >US$50M, permitting acceleration (approvals avg >1,000 days), Aug 30 greenfield-exploration tax credits. Record Q1 2026 SEIA submissions (US$17.3B). Constraint: no majority — Chamber right bloc 76/155 (PDG's 14 seats pivotal), Senate tied 25–25; reforms need negotiation, revisions likely; approval ~34%, economy flat Q2. Calendar: municipal/regional elections Oct 2028 (Putaendo mayor, Valparaíso region); presidential + Congress Nov 2029, new government Mar 2030. Vizcachitas' EIA is unfiled and SEIA takes years → the decisive rulings may straddle the 2030 transition.

National layer favourable but time-boxed; the gate is still regional/local.

Track record
  • PFS Feb 2023: NPV8 US$2.8B, IRR 24%source

Fit to this job
Chilean porphyry in Chile, same jurisdiction, long local presence. But this is now a chief geologist running a company that needs a feasibility study, a Supreme Court outcome, permits and a US$2B+ build; the only executive with major-company and government weight (Montt) left for cabinet. Family control and a lender on the board shape decisions more than management does.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. Turnbrook Corp (Covarrubias) ~47%, RCF ~13%; management ownership small (Amberg % not disclosed). Only one open-market insider buy in two years (Gilman C$109k, Apr 2024). Amberg comp ~C$309k (FY Sep 2024, pre-CEO role); FY2025 related-party fees C$1.95M. Red flags
  • Lender's CEO sits on the board (Queen's Road Capital / Warren Gilman) — related-party flavour to the debenture financing.
  • 47% family control via Turnbrook; board average tenure 15 years, no refreshment.
  • Silence on project progress in 2026; related-party fees C$1.95M in FY2025 (management/consulting via private companies).
  • Ex-CEO Montt was named for Mines (Jan 2026) and dropped by Kast hours later over the early disclosure; he never took office. The episode cost the company its CEO and gave opponents a conflict narrative.
  • Financials: related-party charges C$1.1M in 9M FY26; US$9M of debentures mature Apr and Sep 2027 against C$17.6M cash; a Q1 FY26 cash-flow line (debenture interest) contradicts the note.

  1. Cash was C$17.6M at 30 June 2026, burning C$1.9M a quarter, about 9 quarters; US$9M of debentures due 2027 would cut that to C$5M if repaid in cash.
  2. About 70-75% of spend goes into Vizcachitas studies and permitting, C$4.3M in nine months of FY26, with cash G&A about C$2.2M a year offset by interest income.

  4. Reported results are driven by non-cash items: deferred-tax recoveries, debenture mark-to-market swings and a C$3.7M loss in Q2 FY26.
  5. Related parties charged C$1.1M in nine months, the CEO resigned in January 2026, and the project has a completed PFS with US$2.8B NPV awaiting permits.

Risk score4/5A real, drill-confirmed porphyry discovery, 100% owned, Barrick-backed, funded, and since 1 Sep 2026 (announced 30 Jul) run by the team that just sold Arizona Sonoran to Hudbay — but there's no resource, the system is deep and partly under leached cover, and the price already reflects the discovery.
Market cap15 Oct 2026: ~US$259M (C$1.06 · ~C$373M on 350.4M shares). 2 Oct 2026: ~US$298M (C$1.21). May 2026: ~US$150M (~C$205M at ~C$0.60 on ~345M shares after the C$31.5M raise). Incoming management is personally investing a further C$4.5M at C$0.62 (closing ~Sep 1, 2026).
Capex / IRRNo economic study — no resource yet.
NPVNo NPV — pre-resource.
DepositNo resource yet.Leviathan porphyry (Cu-Mo-Ag), traced >1 km along strike, up to 750 m wide and 500 m vertically, with only ~20% of the target footprint tested: 670.44 m @ 0.45% Cu incl. 212.81 m @ 0.67% (HER-25-18); 420.62 m @ 0.60% Cu incl. 113 m @ 1.38% (HER-25-15); 788 m @ 0.54% CuEq and 802 m @ 0.40% CuEq (2026); discovery hole 185 m @ 0.84% Cu incl. 45 m @ 1.94%. HER-25-25 hit the margins of a new blind porphyry at Southern Flats. Northern holes ended in increasing grade at depth.
NPV : capexn/a — no study.
Valuation Anchor

~US$300M (2 Oct) for a 100%-owned, Barrick-backed US porphyry discovery with no resource. Pricier than Gladiator and Kodiak, cheaper than NGEx — same bucket as Gladiator, with a bigger system and a major on board, but less grade.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~8% (est.) — founder Chris Paul ~2.8%; George Ogilvie and six ex-Arizona Sonoran colleagues bought 7.26M sh at C$0.62 (C$4.5M, Aug 31 2026), ~2.2%, at a premium to market; small officer buys May–Jun 2026. Strategic: Barrick ~11% (12.8% Jul 2025, diluted; pro-rata rights). Funds: Jupiter ~8%, Konwave ~1%.

Read: Meaningful — an incoming team paying cash at a premium is a strong tell; Barrick anchors.

Jurisdiction risk

National: excellent — United States, with a strong critical-minerals push for domestic copper. Local: low known opposition — Idaho is mining-literate; the 404.7 km² property has surface mining rights, road access, three 260 kV transmission lines crossing it, and sits ~2 hours from Boise. The permitting path is untested at this stage.

Differentiator

A genuine new porphyry district in the US, 100% owned, with a major already on the register. Barrick invested ~C$35M (2023) to build its position; competition among majors across the belt raises takeout odds. Unlike Amarc, Kincora or Latin Metals, Hercules keeps 100% of the discovery — and it now has a management team with a fresh, proven US-copper exit (Cactus → Hudbay), backing that with C$4.5M of their own money.

Read honestly: ~US$259M (15 Oct 2026) for no resource means the discovery premium is already paid — the multiple needs the system to prove genuinely large.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, district-scale · moves the needle: high. Long intervals, higher grade in potassic cores, holes ending in mineralisation, and MT conductors along trend not yet drilled. This is the core of the thesis rather than a bonus.

Next Catalyst

2026 drill results (Southern Flats blind porphyry, Hook IP target, HER-25-18 extension, step-outs); order-of-magnitude study; maiden resource (undated); any Barrick or major-company move.

Open Questions
  • How large does Leviathan get along strike and at depth?
  • Does the high-grade (~1%+) core have tonnage?
  • At what depth does it sit, and does that point to open-pit or underground mining?
  • Does Barrick move beyond an investor stake?
Context & updates

Market cap corrected to ~US$298M (C$1.21 × 350.4M shares) — the card's US$150M was a May estimate, and the stock has roughly doubled. 30 Sep: the porphyry is traced 1.35 km along strike, up to 750 m wide and open; Southern Flats is a second centre. At this price the discovery is largely priced.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 4/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 4/5

The Arizona Sonoran team (Cactus → C$2B Hudbay exit) took over in September and bought C$4.5M of stock at market — the same porphyry play. Five weeks in; A if it delivers a resource on time.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 28% → 31%, odds of a 3× 6% → 6%.

People
George Ogilvie (President, CEO, Director, since 2026-09-01): Age 59. P.Eng. Ex-CEO Arizona Sonoran (sold to Hudbay C$2B 2026), Battle North (sold to Evolution C$343M 2021), Kirkland Lake Gold (2013-16), Rambler Metals (built Ming mine, NL). · Chris Paul (SVP Exploration, Director (CEO until 2026-08-31), since founder): Geologist; founded company around a geological concept that led to the 2023 Leviathan porphyry discovery; moved aside for the operator team. · Matthieu Bos (Chairman (non-exec), since 2025-12-19): Appointed chair late 2025; background not verified. · Nicholas Nikolakakis (SVP Finance & CFO, since 2026-09-01): Ex-CFO Arizona Sonoran, Battle North, Rainy River; ex-VP Barrick corporate finance. · Anthony Bottrill (Senior Resource Geologist, since 2026-09-01): Modelled Cactus (Arizona Sonoran), Klondex, BHP Olympic Dam - the person who will build the maiden resource.
Track record
  • Ogilvie: Arizona Sonoran Copper CEO 2021-2026; Cactus (Arizona) taken from C$125M equity value (2021) to C$2B Hudbay takeover (2026)source
  • Ogilvie: hired Oct 2016 to restructure Rubicon Minerals after its Phoenix mine failed (reserve cut 88%, stock $6 to 5c); renamed Battle North, sold to Evolution Mining for C$343M May 2021 - a clean-up and exit, not a buildsource
  • Ogilvie: CEO Kirkland Lake Gold 2013-2016 (operating turnaround; ended June 2016 ahead of the Newmarket merger); CEO Rambler Metals to Jan 2014 (small Ming copper-gold mine, Newfoundland)source
  • Misses: none of Ogilvie's exits was a mine he built from an explorer; Rambler later failed under successors (unverified). No bankruptcy or sanction found under his watch.
  • Wins came in 2021 (gold bull) and 2026 (copper bull); Kirkland turnaround in 2013-16 gold bear.
  • Chris Paul: Leviathan discovery drilled 2023 (hole HER-23-05 era); Barrick took a strategic stake Oct 2023 (~C$23M) and signed a 73 km claim-belt consolidation dealsource

Boards today: Ogilvie: Hercules CEO/director plus Chairman of Barksdale Resources (appointed Sept 2026) - 2 public roles. Left Rupert Resources board 2024. Paul: Hercules only (as far as found).

Fit to this job
Same stage? Partly. Ogilvie's team took Cactus (Arizona porphyry/oxide copper) from early resource to PEA/PFS and a sale - exactly the explorer-to-developer-to-exit path Leviathan needs. Same deposit type (porphyry copper) and same US western jurisdiction (Arizona vs Idaho; Idaho is US Forest Service land - Hercules drills under USFS categorical exclusions, more federal process than Cactus private/state land). New for them: no maiden resource yet, so this is the earliest stage the team has run as a unit; Idaho has no modern large porphyry mine permitting precedent. Paul is the discoverer, now subordinate - the risk is founder friction, not competence.
Skin & pay
4/5 — meaningful stake with real market buying. Insider ownership was ~0.7% before the Aug 2026 placement (Simply Wall St); incoming Arizona Sonoran team then bought 7.26M shares (C$4.5M) at C$0.62 cash - a real market-price buy, plus 18.65M options. Barrick holds a strategic stake (~12% at 2023 entry; current % unverified). Net insider buying C$142k in prior 12 months. CEO pay: Ogilvie's Hercules package not yet disclosed; Chris Paul's 2025 pay not found (circular not fetched).source

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Large option grant (18.65M at $0.59) to the incoming team on day one - partly offset by C$4.5M cash buy.
  • Board flagged for low continuity: 5 new directors in 3 years, chair appointed Dec 2025.
  • No maiden resource or timeline for one stated yet; promotion ('America's newest copper belt') runs ahead of the resource.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash plus investments were C$33.2M at 30 June 2026 after a C$31.5M raise at C$0.59, roughly 22-26 months; the company guides funding to August 2027.
  2. Money goes into the ground: FY2025 exploration was C$17.7M against C$1.6M of overhead, about 8% of spend; H1 2026 was C$6.3M versus C$0.8M.
  3. Shares rose 52% from 231.1M in 2023 to 350.4M in September 2026, with each raise priced lower than the last.
  4. No debt and nothing capitalised; the accumulated deficit reached C$67M by June 2026.
  5. New management received 21.0M options in mid-2026, so overhead will rise; related-party fees were C$0.8M in FY2025.

Thesis

Cheap, de-risked coastal Atacama project — ~3.8¢/lb reserve CuEq; low elevation, own water (Huasco 80%), port access. La Verde discovery (30 km south) could roughly double NPV toward ~US$2B via a high-grade starter pit.

The Gate

The funding gap — ~A$160–285M market cap vs. ~US$1.27B start-up capex. Needs a strategic partner; asset-level partnering process live (BMO-led) with non-binding proposals received and multiple parties in due diligence. A$40M raised Feb 2026 at A$1.65; cash ~A$46M pro forma (A$25M at 30 Jun 2026 plus the US$15M non-dilutive OR Royalties amendment announced Aug 2026) — runway adequate for the La Verde MRE and PFS work, not for construction.

Partly offset by the Huasco Water lever below — less severe than the raw numbers suggest, but not solved.

NPV : capex0.94x@ PFS base → 1.73x @ US$5.30/lb. IRR 19% base / 30% @ $5.30.Fails Rule at base — this is the "IRR concern" Rule voiced on Hot Chili (Mar 2026); IRR passes at $5.30, NPV test doesn't. La Verde restated PFS is what could change this.
Valuation Anchor

~3.8¢/lb reserve CuEq (~4.7¢/lb on the 4.2 Blb of contained reserve copper alone); ~2.4¢/lb CuEq on total resource (~3.1¢/lb Cu-only). Stock re-rated 4–5x over ~15 months — partly priced. ~0.17× PFS NAV at ~US$198M (A$1.40, 15 Oct 2026; was ~0.19× at ~US$230M).

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~6% (directors & officers; MD Christian Easterday ~0.9%, buying on-market Aug 2026; director de Andraca +180k sh Apr 2026). Strategic: Glencore ~6.6% (diluted from 9.96% in 2022, but took part in the Feb 2026 placement). Other: GS Group ~4.1%, Blue Spec (drilling contractor) ~4.8%.

Read: Moderate — insiders own a little and add in small amounts; Glencore's continued participation is the more meaningful signal.

Jurisdiction risk

National: favourable (same Chilean reforms as Los Andes). Local: among the lowest in the file. Coastal Atacama, low elevation, established mining district, Huasco Water 80% with the only granted maritime concession — the water question that sinks Chilean projects is already answered. EIA submission due ~Q2 2027 but on a site with no exclusion campaign.

Contrast with Los Andes: same country, opposite local risk.

Differentiator — Huasco Water (80%-owned)

The one genuinely distinct asset in this file. Holds the only granted maritime concession + permits to supply the water-constrained Huasco Valley. Plan: vend the water rights into a private vehicle and sell down Hot Chili's stake (retaining enough to guarantee own supply), using proceeds to fund "a large chunk" of Costa Fuego's equity portion — i.e. non-dilutive at the HCH share level. Template: Antofagasta sold Centinela's water rights for US$600M, cutting capex US$380M, with a 20-yr offtake back. Staged design (Stage 1 seawater to Costa Fuego; Stages 2–3 desalinated supply deeper into the valley, which hosts six undeveloped copper projects + two greenfield discoveries) means it's sellable on third-party demand — a regional utility, not a captive pipe.

  • Why this differentiates: other names have water solutions (Los Andes' desal LOI answers a permitting objection); Hot Chili has a water business that answers a financing problem. Different function.
  • Caveats: nothing signed — optionality, not committed funding. No hard % of capex disclosed; scale it yourself (equity slice of US$1.27B ≈ US$400–500M). Centinela was a producing major's expansion, so the read-across flatters a junior greenfield. Value depends on neighbouring valley projects actually advancing. Addresses the equity side only — debt still raised against a junior balance sheet. Timing must land before FID (2029).
Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, better tonnes · moves the needle: high. La Verde, 30 km south: 398 m @ 0.45% CuEq from surface, mineralised to 765 m, maiden MRE (~500 Mt guided) pending, 22 holes' assays outstanding. A near-surface satellite starter pit that could roughly double NPV —

and the most direct fix for its thin 0.94× NPV/capex.

Entry plan · €1,000 as an illustration
Step 0 · waitingNothing bought. Three alerts set: the La Verde maiden resource (guided late 2026), a price alert at A$1.45 (~15% below today), and any ASX announcement containing "placement", "strategic" or "Huasco Water". Plan written 26 Sep 2026 at ~A$1.72; restructured 27 Sep. The €1,000 is illustrative (≈ A$1,650 ≈ ~950 shares) — the point is the 40/30/30 split and the events, not the amount; scale it.

A decision tree tied to events, not dates. Three tranches assume cheap ASX access (Interactive Brokers, ~A$6 an order); at a German bank charging €25–60 per foreign order, collapse it to two (€600 now / €400 at Step 2) or one — at this size the fee drag beats the timing gain. Not advice; my read written down in advance so that on the day I compare numbers against thresholds I set beforehand, not against the price move.

Step 1first tranche now: €400 (~40%), because the two best events are undated

Buy €400 (~230 shares) with a limit order at or below A$1.75 on the ASX. Reason: the two things most likely to re-rate the stock — an asset-level partner out of the BMO process (non-binding proposals in, parties in due diligence) and a Huasco Water transaction — have no date, and either can print any week. Being partly in is the price of not missing them. The stock is ~20% off its A$2.19 high and at the Feb 2026 placement level (A$1.65), so there is no obvious "wait for" level below.

  1. Not filled and the stock runs? Don't chase above A$1.95 — that puts it back near the high with nothing new announced. Wait for Step 2.
  2. Falls to the A$1.45 alert with no news? Fill the €400 there and consider bringing €150 of Step 3 forward — a no-news drawdown in a name with two undated positives pending is the entry the plan is hoping for.
Step 2the La Verde maiden resource (guided late 2026, most likely Nov–Dec): read three numbers and one sentence before doing anything
WhatGreenRed
Tonnage≥ 500 Mt (management's guided figure)< 350 Mt
Grade of the open-pit portion≥ 0.45% CuEq, with a starter zone broken out at ≥ 0.6%< 0.35% CuEq, no starter zone stated
Near-surface enrichment blanketquantified as its own domain (the ~70 m blanket, tens of Mt)folded into the bulk average, not separated
The sentence"to be incorporated into the revised PFS" / "open-pit starter""further drilling required to define" / no mention of the PFS

Three or four green → the starter-pit thesis is intact; any sell-the-news dip is a discount. Two or more red → the project got smaller, not cheaper. Stop. Do not buy the dip. Re-run the card — the roughly-doubled NPV the market is pricing rests on this resource.

Step 3second tranche: €300 (~30%) — on the resource, not before it
  1. Mostly green and the stock falls ≥ 10% on the day or within the following week → buy €300 in the market. A resource at guidance after a 325% run is a classic sell-the-news setup; the fall is positioning, not the project.
  2. Mostly green and the stock rises → buy €300 anyway within two weeks. The dip is not coming; a confirmed starter pit is worth more than the 10% saved. Don't chase beyond +20%.
  3. Red → nothing. Hold the cash and wait for Step 4 or Step 5 to change the picture.
Step 4third tranche: €300 (~30%) — the first of three triggers, whichever comes first
  1. A placement. Hot Chili raises roughly every 12–18 months (A$0.9x in 2025, A$1.65 in Feb 2026). Buy on the announcement day or the next morning, at or near the placement price — the institutions' price without the hold. Read the use of proceeds: PFS, EIA, La Verde drilling = fine; "general working capital" with no programme attached = caution, halve it.
  2. A copper drawdown of 25%+ in the stock with the story unchanged (no partner news, no permit news — just the metal). Buy the €300 into it.
  3. The revised PFS (2027) if neither has triggered. Green: after-tax NPV ≥ US$2.0B at a copper deck ≤ US$4.50, NPV/capex ≥ 1.5×, initial capex ≤ US$1.6B. Red: capex > US$1.8B or NPV/capex < 1.1× → don't; the financing gap just got wider than the market cap can carry.

If none of the three has triggered by the PFS and the PFS is green, deploy on the PFS anyway. Cash held for a dip that never comes is how this plan fails.

Step 5overrides — events that change the plan whatever step it is at
  1. Buy the remaining tranches that day: an asset-level partner deal with a producer or major (≥ 25% of Costa Fuego for ≥ US$200M of funding), or a Huasco Water sale/JV printing ≥ US$150M. Either one converts the financing gate from open to mostly closed; the price on the day is irrelevant against that.
  2. Stop adding and review: the company announces the partnering process has concluded without a transaction; or an equity raise below A$1.50 that is not tied to a partner. Both say the non-dilutive levers failed.
Step 6once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if, by mid-2027, the partnering process has ended empty and no water transaction has printed and the company has raised equity below A$1.50 — three misses is the thesis failing, not bad luck.
  2. Sell half if the stock doubles before a partner or water deal is signed. Developers re-rate fastest around the financing event; a double on hope alone is worth banking half of.
  3. Otherwise hold through the partner/water transaction and the revised PFS. The thesis is a de-risked coastal Chilean project finding its financing; don't trade the drill results in between.
PracticalWhere to buy, currency, and the most likely outcome

Liquidity is on the ASX (HCH) in AUD; the TSXV line (HCH) and the Frankfurt/Tradegate line are thin — if you must use them, limit orders only, priced off the ASX close converted to EUR, never market orders. The stock moves 5–8% on drill results. You take AUD/EUR exposure on top of the copper exposure and cannot hedge it at this size. Most likely single outcome: the resource lands near 500 Mt, the stock moves ±10% and drifts, no partner deal until well into 2027, and the plan's average entry ends near A$1.65–1.75. The money was never in the timing — it is in whether Costa Fuego finds its partner.

Plan log: 26 Sep 2026 — plan written at ~A$1.72; Step 0, nothing bought. 26 Sep — marked as pick in tracker and rankings. 27 Sep — restructured as an event tree with thresholds. 15 Oct — A$1.40, below the A$1.45 alert with no adverse news (no release since 29 Sep; La Verde MRE and the partner process both still pending) — Step 1 condition met (€400 at or below A$1.75; the no-news-drawdown case). Decision: owner to decide; nothing bought yet.

Next Catalyst

A Huasco Water transaction printing at a real number — arguably a bigger re-rate than another drill hole. Also: La Verde maiden MRE (later 2026; 21 holes' assays pending); revised PFS (commenced May 2026) — now also assessing a large open-pit at Cortadera as an alternative to the block cave, which could change capex materially; EIA split into two filings (Huasco Water intake; Costa Fuego), submission targeted late 2026–2027; strategic partner. FID targeted 2029, first production 2031. Community perception study (Jun 2026): 93% positive.

Open Questions
  • What does Huasco Water actually fetch, and what % of capex does it cover? Does the La Verde maiden MRE land near the ~500 Mt guidance?
  • Who partners, and at what terms?
  • ~40% of concentrate offtake still uncommitted (Glencore 7.5% holder can take up to 60% for 8 years while it maintains that stake).

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 2/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

Candid and insiders buy, but the EIA slipped from mid-2024 to 2027, the PFS is being redone and the 17-year CEO has never built a mine.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 41% → 38%, odds of a 3× 21% → 20%.

People
Christian Easterday (Managing Director & CEO, since 2009 (~17 yrs)): Geologist; has run Hot Chili through the whole Productora/Cortadera/Costa Fuego history including the 2013-2019 downturn. · Stuart Mathews (Independent Non-Exec Chairman, since 2025-05): Ex-Gold Fields EVP (Australia/Americas operations), 32 yrs. · David Bayona (Project Director (new development team), since 2026 (H1)): Background not verified. · Grant King (COO (listed by MarketScreener), since 2008 (unverified)): Long-tenured; role in current build-out unclear.
Track record
  • Easterday has built no mine; Hot Chili has been a Chilean explorer/developer since ~2010 and has not previously reached a construction decisionsource
  • Delivered: 2024 PEA, Mar 2025 PFS and maiden reserve for Costa Fuego (capex US$1.27B, NPV8 US$1.2B, IRR 19%) and Mar 2025 Huasco Water PFSsource
  • Glencore is ~6.6% holder; OR Royalties royalty deal provided ~US$15M in 2026; A$40M placement Feb 2026source
  • Chairman Mathews bought 200k shares (A$252k) Dec 2024; Easterday net buyer A$168k in last 12 monthssource

Boards today: Easterday: 1 public role (HCH). Mathews: chair HCH, other seats unverified.

Fit to this job
Same region and deposit type (Chilean coastal IOCG/porphyry, open pit, conventional concentrator) and the team has been in the Huasco valley for 15 years. New for them: a definitive study, EIA approval, a US$1.1B+ financing and construction — none of the executives has delivered a mine build; the new chairman brings operating credibility but joined in 2025.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Easterday ~0.9% of shares, net open-market buyer (A$168k last 12 months, incl. a purchase at A$0.66 — the source dates it Sep 2026, but the stock traded A$1.5–1.7 then and the 52-week low is A$0.76, so it is probably Sep 2025; date unverified); chairman and director de Andraca also bought in 2024-25. CEO total remuneration ~A$707k (FY2025) vs market cap roughly A$150-250M — proportionate. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/au/materials/asx-hch/hot-chili-shares/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Permitting timeline has slipped roughly three years and the project scope keeps changing (La Verde added, PFS redone).
  • Partner process running since 2024 with BMO, 'non-binding proposals' only.
  • Very long CEO tenure with no mine built; same leadership through a decade of share-price decline.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was A$24.9M at 30 June 2026 plus US$15M from a July royalty sale, about A$46M; at A$9.9M a quarter that is around 4.5 quarters.
  2. About 70% of cash spend goes into the ground, but overhead has grown from A$5.6M to A$8.9M a year, about A$2.2-2.5M a quarter.
  3. Shares rose 34% from 151.3M to 202.9M, almost all from the A$14.1M rights issue at A$0.60 and A$40M placement at A$1.65.
  4. No debt or convertibles; exploration is capitalised, so the A$10.1M FY26 loss is essentially overhead plus share-based pay.
  5. Two royalty sales to OR Royalties have funded the company alongside equity, and the December 2025 quarterly showed only 0.58 quarters of funding left.

Thesis

Andina has hit long porphyry intercepts at two separate systems in one year: 468 m @ 0.50% Cu + 0.30 g/t Au at Piuquenes North (PIU13, Jul 2026) and 504 m @ 0.48% Cu (CDH010, Aug 2026) inside a ~1.3 km × 0.55–0.7 km footprint at Cobrasco. If either grows into a 500 Mt-class resource the market has a new Andean porphyry developer; the ground sits in the Altar–Los Azules cluster (Piuquenes) and next to Rio Tinto's Comita (Cobrasco). The price (~US$206M) already assumes both keep delivering.

Valuation Anchor

~US$206M for two unresourced porphyry discoveries, about US$100M each. Aldebaran's neighbouring Altar carries 2.40 Bt M&I @ 0.42% Cu, which shows the scale this cluster can reach, but Piuquenes has three good holes and Cobrasco thirteen. The market is paying for the second discovery and the pedigree of the board; a maiden resource at Cobrasco is the first thing that can anchor the price.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~10%: Chair Tony Manini and associates 15.2M shares (5.5%), CEO Joseph van den Elsen 6.26M (2.4%), director Bryce Roxburgh ~2.3% (Rugby paper). Institutions: 1832 Asset Management (Dynamic Funds) 26.25M shares (~10%). No major or strategic mining company on the register as far as disclosed. Insider trades on record are option exercises and holds (Manini Mar 2026, CEO Oct 2025), no sales found.

Read: Real money from the chair and a serious fund; no major yet — a strategic placement would be the next validation.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Argentina (San Juan) is currently the friendliest Andean copper province (Altar, Los Azules, Josemaría neighbours; RIGI incentive regime) but policy swings with Buenos Aires. Colombia is the weak leg: Cobrasco sits in a Chocó forest reserve (Ley 2 de 1959); a rule change in Dec 2024 stopped Rugby's drilling, drilling resumed in 2025 under a 10-year community agreement and water permits, and the company's own MD&A flags draft mining-code Bill 340 and the 2026 election cycle as risks. Chocó also has a security record. Local: Piuquenes is high-altitude Andean ground with a short drilling season; no community issue reported. Chile (Mantau) is undrilled and immaterial.

Two very different jurisdictions in one company: Argentina sets the upside, Colombia sets the tail risk.

Differentiator

Two discoveries, a board that has sold porphyries before, and a neighbour that proves the cluster. Manini co-founded EMR Capital and Tigers Realm (NexGen incubator); Roxburgh founded Exeter/Extorre (Caspiche sold to Goldcorp, Cerro Moro to Yamana); Zulliger worked Altar, Los Azules and Taca Taca. Piuquenes North starts 700 m down, which is deep for a junior but normal for this cluster.

Shallow Cobrasco (from ~30 m) balances deep Piuquenes — but Cobrasco is the harder jurisdiction.

Exploration upside

Two open porphyry systems · moves the needle: high Cobrasco's footprint is ~1.3 km × 0.7 km inside a >3 km² soil anomaly and is open; a second rig is coming. Piuquenes North has only two holes into an 800 m × 700 m MT anomaly, with a ~20,000 m program planned and results guided for Q1–H1 2027. Either could add scale quickly; neither has shown a high-grade core yet.

Next Catalyst

Cobrasco assays for three completed holes plus the hole in progress (pending since 23 Sep 2026) and the second rig; Piuquenes North follow-up drilling with results from Q1 2027. The US$250k third-anniversary option payment falls due ~30 Nov 2026.

Open Questions
  • Does Piuquenes North hold a higher-grade core, and at what depth — can a junior fund 20,000 m of 1,000 m+ holes?
  • What does Cobrasco look like as a maiden resource, and does the Chocó forest-reserve permitting hold through a new Colombian government?
  • How will the C$14.75M Piuquenes exercise payment (due by ~Nov 2027) be funded — equity, a major, or a renegotiation?

Fit to this job
Stage: drill-stage discovery, pre-resource — fits Roxburgh (serial discoverer/seller) and Zulliger (Andean porphyry QP who worked the neighbours). Deposit: porphyry Cu-Au/Cu-Mo — yes. Regions: Argentina — Roxburgh (Cerro Moro, Don Sixto) and Zulliger (Altar, Los Azules) have done it; Colombia — CEO is a dual citizen, Brewster a former Colombian diplomat, Roxburgh ran Cobrasco. New for them: the CEO is a banker-turned-explorer in his first CEO job and has not yet financed a C$15M option exercise or a resource.

  • Releases and MD&A never disclose the Piuquenes option economics (C$14.75M exercise payment, four-year clock to ~Nov 2027); only the FS notes do — investors reading headlines do not see the clock.

  • Deck headline '$1B+ value-creation opportunity' with no basis shown.
  • Promised ASX dual listing (Mar 2025) dropped without comment.
  • Chair holds three chairmanships; CFO is a part-time serial CFO; management fees C$250k per half-year are modest, so no pay issue found.

The company capitalises all exploration: there is no exploration expense line, so `is.exp` is null and the money into the ground appears as `cf.exp_cap` ('Expenditures on mineral properties'). `bs.ee` = 'Mineral property interests' (acquisition + capitalised exploration); `bs.ppe` = equipment. `ga` = total operating expenses ex share-based compensation (consulting, depreciation, director/management fees, G&A, IR, professional, transfer agent). `cf.oth` = 'exploration expenditures held in deposits' and minor equipment lines so that cfo+exp_cap+capex+acq+oth+fin = net. spend.overhead uses `ga` (cash G&A ex-SBC).

Vicuña-belt explorer next door to Filo del Sol with two first-season discoveries (Albor, Cruz del Sur), Rio Tinto at ~5% and ~C$77M cash for a 20,000 m season.

Gate Turning one 180 m breccia hole into a body, and finding the porphyry beneath it Albor is a single hole (FS_DDH_016); the offset hole FS_DDH_019 only clipped it (14 m @ 0.82% CuEq) because it crossed the fault at an oblique angle. Funding & next catalyst
Cash
C$43.8M cash at 31 May 2026 (last filed statements); ~C$77M at 21 Sep 2026 after Rio Tinto's C$21.3M, C$5.6M of pre-emptive units and CD Capital's C$19.2M rights exercise (company figure via Crux Investor; the company says the treasury funds the next 12 months)
Debt
None (total liabilities C$2.9M at 31 May 2026). Off-balance-sheet: Beskauga option payments — US$24.7M in total (US$17.2M cash + up to US$7.5M cash-or-shares, 27 Feb 2026 release): US$2.5M paid at signing (US$1.5M cash), US$1.0M on each of 1 Jan 2027/2028/2029 (half cash), US$19.2M by 8 Feb 2029 (US$14.2M cash + US$5.0M cash-or-shares) and Copper Cliff earn-in (US$4M in year 1, US$16M by year 3).
Burn · runway
FY2026–27 plan: ~C$40M for up to 20,000 m at Filo Sur (Crux, 17 Sep 2026), ~C$8M for Beskauga, ~US$5.5M for Copper Cliff this year, plus overhead — roughly C$55–65M over 12 months, i.e. ~C$14–16M per quarter if all three programmes run.
Next catalyst
Filo Sur drilling restart Nov 2026 (first assays likely Q1 2027); Beskauga first assays Q4 2026; Copper Cliff drilling earliest Nov 2026 if permits arrive.
Funded to the next catalyst Funded through the whole 2026–27 season on all three projects, by the company's own statement, with the next raise likely in H2 2027 — possibly from Rio Tinto's top-up or the 199M warrants (C$0.47 average, 15.2M at C$1.00 expire Feb 2028) if the price runs. Not funded for the US$19.2M Beskauga balloon payment in Feb 2029 or the Copper Cliff stage-3 spend.
Thesis

Filo Sur is 100%-owned ground adjoining Lundin/BHP's Filo del Sol, and the first drill season (6,208 m) produced two discoveries: Albor, 180 m @ 0.98% CuEq from 108 m incl. 58 m @ 1.77% CuEq, and Cruz del Sur, 258 m @ 0.36 g/t Au and 328 m @ 0.32 g/t Au with ~0.1% Cu. Rio Tinto bought ~5% at a premium in Aug 2026 and holds a 15-month exclusivity over Filo Sur; CD Capital (an early Filo Corp backer) has gone to 19.9%. With ~C$77M in cash the company can drill up to 20,000 m at Filo Sur from Nov 2026, 50,000 m at Beskauga (Kazakhstan, optioned) and 8–9,000 m at Copper Cliff (Montana, Rio Tinto option) in the same 12 months.

The Gate

Turning one 180 m breccia hole into a body, and finding the porphyry beneath it Albor is a single hole (FS_DDH_016); the offset hole FS_DDH_019 only clipped it (14 m @ 0.82% CuEq) because it crossed the fault at an oblique angle. The 2026–27 season must show strike and depth continuity at Albor and test the IP chargeability high the company interprets as a deeper porphyry. The drill window is short (roughly Nov–May at ~4,500 m elevation), ground conditions already stopped several 2025–26 holes, and the market is paying ~US$200M for two holes. Rio Tinto's exclusivity runs to ~Nov 2027 (extendable 6 months): it has a right to match and a top-up to 9.99%, which is both validation and a cap on who else can bid.

Albor (breccia, FS_DDH_016): 180 m @ 0.98% CuEq from 108 m (0.51% Cu, 0.37 g/t Au, 2.8 g/t Ag, 119 ppm Mo) incl. 58 m @ 1.77% CuEq and 9 m @ 2.84% CuEq; CuEq at US$4.69/lb Cu, US$3,321/oz Au, 80% recoveries assumed, true widths unknown. Cruz del Sur (porphyry, 4 km south): FS_DDH_006 258 m @ 0.36 g/t Au + 744 ppm Cu and 328 m @ 0.32 g/t Au + 962 ppm Cu; FS_DDH_007 120 m @ 0.52 g/t Au + 0.18% Zn from 24 m. Cuenca road-cut channels 153 m @ 0.31 g/t Au + 0.11% Cu. The Macho Muerto Fault Zone runs ~10 km through the property, mostly undrilled. Beskauga (Kazakhstan, option to 100%): historical Feb 2022 estimate 111.2 Mt Indicated @ 0.30% Cu, 0.49 g/t Au, 1.34 g/t Ag and 92.6 Mt Inferred @ 0.24% Cu, 0.50 g/t Au (at US$3.50 Cu, US$1,750 Au; not current, not to be relied on), ~68,000 m drilled historically. Copper Cliff (Montana, option to 51–60% from Kennecott/Rio Tinto): best historical hole 14CC0013 1,252.5 m @ 0.41 g/t Au + 0.34% Cu from 665 m — deep.
NPV : capexn/a — no study.
Valuation Anchor

~US$200M for two discovery holes on Filo del Sol's doorstep, ~C$77M of cash (~27% of the cap) and a cheap option on a 1.8 Moz Au / 334 kt Cu (historical) Kazakh porphyry. The market is paying for the address and for Rio Tinto's endorsement, not for pounds: NGEx's Lunahuasi re-rated to multiples of this on holes of similar width but higher grade. If Albor becomes a 50–100 Mt body at ~1% CuEq the price is cheap; if it stays a narrow fault-breccia, US$120M of the cap is sentiment.

Shareholder structure

CD Capital Fund IV ~19.9% partially diluted after Aug 2026 (director Carmel Daniele; investor rights agreement Jan 2026: board seat, pre-emptive and top-up rights). Rio Tinto ~5.0% (30.4M shares, Aug 2026) with a top-up right to 9.99% at a 20% premium during exclusivity. Aster Blue Ltd ~11.7% and Syndicate Minerals Pty Ltd ~6.7% (the CEO's former private prospecting group; link to Sabet family unverified) per simplywall.st. Named individual insiders ~1.1% (chair Mullens 0.55%, Williams 0.31%, A. Sabet 0.18%). Institutions ~4.6% (Rothschild & Cie Gestion 2.2%, Euro Pacific 1.5%, Konwave). Insiders took 5.5M shares at C$0.70 in the Rio Tinto placement (Sep 22 clarification).

Read: Two strategic anchors (CD Capital at the cap, Rio Tinto with a cheap look) and a loyal register; management's own direct stake is small.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Argentina (San Juan) — improving. The RIGI incentive regime and Vicuña (Filo del Sol / Josemaría) being advanced by BHP-Lundin set the precedent; San Juan is Argentina's most mining-friendly province, but the country's macro and FX rules remain volatile and the 2027 election is a risk. Chile claims (1,303 ha) sit in a stable regime. Local: the property is at ~4,000–5,000 m with a Nov–May season and no communities on site; logistics and weather, not social licence, set the pace. Kazakhstan: Beskauga is near Bozshakol with rail, road and power; mining licence application submitted (management, Oct 2026), but the licence and the US$19.2M balloon payment are the real tests. Montana: permits for Copper Cliff drilling still pending in Oct 2026.

Argentina risk is mostly macro and political; the Vicuña district has the best precedent in the country.

Differentiator

Two discoveries in the first season, next door to the biggest copper find of the decade, with Rio Tinto paying a premium to look. Unlike most Vicuña juniors it owns the Argentine ground outright (1.5% NSR to Golden Arrow), has ~C$77M to drill, and has added two large porphyry options (Beskauga, Copper Cliff) that give it something to show if Filo Sur stalls.

The flip side: three projects on three continents for a ten-person team, and the chair sold into the Rio Tinto news.

Exploration upside

District-scale, two open discoveries, porphyry untested · moves the needle: high Albor is open along the fault and at depth, with potassic alteration increasing downward next to an IP high; Cruz del Sur is open in all directions over a 4 × 0.5 km footprint; Luz del Sol, Cuenca and Meseta are undrilled or barely drilled porphyry targets along 10 km of structure. A 20,000 m season is enough to answer the question either way.

Next Catalyst

Filo Sur drilling restarts Nov 2026 (up to 20,000 m), with first Albor offset assays likely Q1 2027; Beskauga first assays Q4 2026; Copper Cliff drilling once Montana permits arrive.

Open Questions
  • Does the Albor breccia have width and continuity beyond one hole, and is there a porphyry under it?
  • What does Rio Tinto do at the end of its 15-month exclusivity (Nov 2027): top up, offer a JV, or walk?
  • Can a small team actually run 78,000 m across Argentina, Kazakhstan and Montana in one year without the Filo Sur programme slipping?
  • Who is Aster Blue Ltd (11.7%), and is Syndicate Minerals (6.7%) the CEO's family stake?

  • 09 JulMogotes Metals Drills 180 m at 0.98% Copper Equivalent, Expanding the Albor Copper-Gold-Silver-Molybdenum Discovery at Filo SurMatters most: the full Albor hole — 180 m @ 0.98% CuEq incl. 58 m @ 1.77% CuEq; offset hole 019 clipped it; porphyry target below.

Links go to the company's own site · all releases · grey notes are my read of whether a release changes this card.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Unproven CEO who nevertheless delivered two discoveries and C$65M of financing at rising prices in his first season; strong board/advisors for the Andes; Rio Tinto and CD Capital endorse it. Offset by a chair selling into news, a small executive stake, family on the board and a shared CFO. Solid but clean, not tier 1.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Allen Sabet (President, CEO & Director, since CEO since 2022 (company incorporated Sep 2022, listed 12 Jun 2024)): Ex-McKinsey consultant to mining/energy clients (Woodside, South32, Shell); previously operated Syndicate Minerals, a private prospecting group. First public-company CEO role. Direct holding ~1.06M shares (0.18%); exercised 1M options at ~C$0.23 in Sep 2026. · Peter Mullens (Non-executive Chairman, since n/a (founding board, 2022–24)): 35+ years, 25 in Argentina; ex-exploration manager Mt Isa Mines Argentina, chief geologist Aquiline Resources (Navidad, sold to Pan American 2010), co-founder/director Lydian International (Amulsar; went into CCAA/receivership 2019–20 after permits were blocked). Also chair of Unico Silver and exec chair of Greenshift Commodities. Holds ~3.3M shares (0.55%); sold ~1.1M shares on market at ~C$0.52 in Jul 2026 after exercising 1M options at ~C$0.16. · Carmel Daniele (Director (CD Capital nominee), since Jan/Feb 2026): Founder/CEO CD Capital (four PE funds, >US$1B raised); early strategic investor in Filo Corp (2020). CD Capital Fund IV holds ~19.9% partially diluted. · Philip Williams (Director, since n/a): Co-founder/ex-CEO Uranium Royalty Corp; chair & CEO IsoEnergy (TSX: ISO); ex-Dundee Capital Markets, Pinetree Capital. Holds ~1.9M shares (0.31%). · Carlos Braun (Director, since n/a): Represents the Braun family (Argentine agribusiness, related to a Bunge founding family); Latin American agriculture and hospitality investor. Holding not disclosed. · Anees Sabet (Director & VP Corporate Development, since n/a): Brother of the CEO (same surname; relationship unverified). Ex-Catch eCommerce executive; NED Peregrine Gold (ASX: PGD). Holds ~0.35M shares (0.06%). · Eric Myung (CFO, since n/a): Part-time via Marelli; CFO of several juniors at once (Arizona Metals, Labrador Gold, Sokoman, Madison Metals, Goldseek, Melkior). · Carl Schnell (Head of Geology (QP for Filo Sur, not independent), since n/a): Signed off the 2026 Filo Sur releases. · Stephen Nano (Technical Advisor (resigned as director 7 Aug 2026), since Founding director 2022–Aug 2026): 38 years exploration; principal technical architect of Filo Sur, Beskauga and Copper Cliff evaluations. Left the board without a stated reason, stays as advisor. · Ray Nadarajah / Raymond Jannas (Advisors, since n/a): Nadarajah: ex-chief of staff to Rio Tinto CEO, partner at Global Infrastructure Partners, NED Kincora Copper. Jannas: discovery teams behind Pascua-Lama, El Morro, Choco 10; director ATEX Resources.
Track record
  • Sabet: no prior public-company record; Mogotes is his first listed vehicle (CEO since 2022). Delivered two discovery holes in the first drill season (May–Jul 2026) and raised ~C$65M in 2026 at rising prices (C$0.265 → C$0.49 → C$0.70)source
  • Sabet: assembled Filo Sur from a Golden Arrow earn-in into 100% ownership for ~C$1M cash plus ~15.4M shares and a 1.5% NSR, Feb–Oct 2025 — cheap entry for the addresssource
  • Mullens: Aquiline Resources (Navidad) sold to Pan American Silver 2010 — win; Lydian International (Amulsar) lost shareholders essentially everything in 2019–20 receivership after the mine was blockaded — loss (role: co-founder/director). Chair of Unico Silver and Greenshift Commodities concurrentlysource
  • Daniele/CD Capital: backed Filo Corp early (2020) ahead of the Filo del Sol discovery and BHP-Lundin bid — a relevant winsource
  • Williams: co-founded Uranium Royalty Corp (listed, grew to a multi-hundred-million royalty company) — winsource
  • Company: Rio Tinto paid a 50–70% premium (C$0.70) for ~5% and a 15-month look in Aug 2026; Kennecott optioned Copper Cliff to Mogotes in Apr 2026 — two Rio Tinto endorsements in four monthssource

Boards today: Sabet: Mogotes only (as far as found). Mullens: chair of Unico Silver and executive chair of Greenshift Commodities plus Mogotes — three chairs. Williams: chair & CEO of IsoEnergy. Daniele: runs CD Capital. CFO Myung: six or more junior CFO roles via Marelli.

Fit to this job
Stage: early explorer with two discovery holes — the board (Mullens, Jannas, Nano as advisor) has the Andean discovery background; the CEO is a consultant-turned-promoter who has not run a drill programme before this one. Deposit: Vicuña-style breccia/porphyry — Jannas (Pascua-Lama, El Morro) and Mullens (25 years Argentina) fit. Region: Argentina — Mullens and Braun are the local anchors. New for them: running three programmes in Argentina, Kazakhstan and Montana at once with a part-time CFO; Beskauga's PEA/PFS is a development task nobody on the executive team has done.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small direct executive stake (~1% named insiders), chair sold into strength; founder block via a private vehicle does not count; some insider buying at C$0.70 in Aug 2026. Named individual insiders ~1.1% (Mullens 0.55%, Williams 0.31%, A. Sabet 0.18%, An. Sabet 0.06%); Syndicate Minerals Pty Ltd 6.7% (CEO's former private group — beneficial link unverified). Insiders subscribed for 5.5M shares at C$0.70 in the Rio Tinto placement (Sep 2026) and were among buyers at C$0.49 in Aug 2026 (36.7M 'insider' shares, mostly CD Capital). Mullens net seller (~C$440k sold Jul 2026); simplywall.st shows insiders net sold ~C$347k over 12 months. Pay not found. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-mog/mogotes-metals-shares/ownership ; https://www.mogotesmetals.com/news/mogotes-update-on-exploration-plans-in-2026-2027

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Chair Peter Mullens exercised 1M options at ~C$0.16 and sold ~1.1M shares on market at ~C$0.52 in Jul 2026, days after the Rio Tinto term sheet — selling into the best news the company has had.
  • CEO's direct stake is ~0.18%; the larger 'Syndicate Minerals' 6.7% block is his former private vehicle (link and beneficial owners unverified) — founder paper, not bought at market.
  • CEO's brother on the board as VP Corporate Development; part-time CFO shared with six other juniors; QPs are all non-independent consultants.
  • Founding technical director Stephen Nano left the board in Aug 2026 with no reason given, just before the biggest season.
  • Three projects on three continents (~78,000 m planned) for a small team — risk that Filo Sur, the only thing the market pays for, is under-managed.
  • Rio Tinto's exclusivity, right to match and standstill until ~Nov 2027 reduce competitive tension if Filo Sur works; top-up at a 20% premium is cheap for a major.
  • Beskauga balloon payment of US$19.2M by Feb 2029 and Copper Cliff's US$16M earn-in are not covered by current cash.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$43.8M at 31 May 2026 and about C$77M by 21 Sep 2026 after Rio Tinto's US$15M (C$21.3M), C$5.6M of pre-emptive subscriptions and CD Capital's C$19.2M rights exercise; at the Q2 operating outflow of C$9.1M that is roughly eight quarters, but the 2026–27 plan (20,000 m at Filo Sur, up to 50,000 m at Beskauga, 8–9,000 m at Copper Cliff) and US$17.2M of Beskauga cash option payments imply a much higher run-rate.
  2. Spending has stepped up sharply: expensed exploration went from C$5.2M in FY2024 to C$11.8M in FY2025 and C$19.8M in the first half of FY2026 alone (C$12.5M in the May quarter).
  3. Overhead is small and stable at about C$0.5–0.8M a quarter (C$2.5M in FY2025 ex-SBC); it was 29% of cash spend in FY2024 but under 10% in H1 FY2026 as drilling ramped up.
  4. The share count rose from 113M (Nov 2023) to 523M (May 2026) and 609M (Sep 2026) — a 5.4x increase — through roughly C$105M of placements since January 2024, plus about C$9M of shares issued for property option payments; 199M warrants (mostly $0.40–$0.53, Rio's at $1.00) are outstanding.
  5. No debt, no revenue, no capitalised assets: the balance sheet is essentially cash plus C$2.7M of Argentine VAT recoverable. The FY2025 audit carried a going-concern material uncertainty, since removed in substance by the 2026 raises.

No economic study yet — PEA due Q4 2026

Cheap (~1.1¢/lb CuEq) but early

Gate Local environmental and community licence in the Mocoa Andes–Amazon transition — not national politics. The binding actors are (1) Corpoamazonia, the autonomous regional environmental authority, which sanctioned the company in 2022 for unauthorised forest use and issued Resolution 1015 (Jul 9, 2026) restricting mining in ecologically sensitive Mocoa areas — community groups were protesting at the ANM for its enforcement on Jul 28, after the election; (2) the courts — indigenous tutelas have already suspended administrative acts pending consultation questions, and constitutional jurisprudence on prior consultation doesn't move with the executive; (3) the site — upper Mocoa river basin, wetlands, the Doña Juana–Chimayoy páramo complex, a protective forest reserve, and the memory of the 2017 mudflow; talk of new Amazon exclusion zones. Structurally the same situation as Los Andes' Rocín valley: a sensitive watershed with an organised exclusion campaign, where a pro-mining national government helps at the margin but doesn't decide the outcome. Secondary: mostly Inferred (first 290 Mt Indicated in Oct 2026), pre-economic; backers are traders/financiers (Denarius 15.3% / Giustra ~16%, Trafigura offtake), not a mining major.

Deposit 290 Mt Ind @ 0.54% CuEq + 1.60 Bt Inf @ 0.40% CuEq (11.5 Blb Cu, eff. 24 Sep 2026; 0.15% cut-off)

The Gate (revised Sep 2026)

Local environmental and community licence in the Mocoa Andes–Amazon transition — not national politics. The binding actors are (1) Corpoamazonia, the autonomous regional environmental authority, which sanctioned the company in 2022 for unauthorised forest use and issued Resolution 1015 (Jul 9, 2026) restricting mining in ecologically sensitive Mocoa areas — community groups were protesting at the ANM for its enforcement on Jul 28, after the election; (2) the courts — indigenous tutelas have already suspended administrative acts pending consultation questions, and constitutional jurisprudence on prior consultation doesn't move with the executive; (3) the site — upper Mocoa river basin, wetlands, the Doña Juana–Chimayoy páramo complex, a protective forest reserve, and the memory of the 2017 mudflow; talk of new Amazon exclusion zones. Structurally the same situation as Los Andes' Rocín valley: a sensitive watershed with an organised exclusion campaign, where a pro-mining national government helps at the margin but doesn't decide the outcome. Secondary: mostly Inferred (first 290 Mt Indicated in Oct 2026), pre-economic; backers are traders/financiers (Denarius 15.3% / Giustra ~16%, Trafigura offtake), not a mining major.

Shareholder structure

Management ~1% — CEO Ian Harris ~1% (~C$2.7M at C$1.00, bought mostly in placements). Frank Giustra personally ~15.8% (bought ~3M sh on-market Jul 2025, added again in the Aug 2026 financing) — an investor, not an officer, so not counted as skin. Strategic: Denarius Metals 15.3% (2-yr lock-up; Giustra + Denarius ≈ 31%, figures per the Aug 2026 closing / Simply Wall St register). Trafigura holds no equity (offtake only). Insiders net buyers ~C$3.7M over 12 months.

Read: Strong, but concentrated in one financier — Giustra is the bet.

Jurisdiction risk

National: materially improved. De la Espriella (Aug 2026) reverses the Petro-era closure — faster permitting, strategic-minerals push. Term to 2030 only; Colombia swung Duque→Petro→de la Espriella in eight years. Local: high, and unchanged by the election. Corpoamazonia (autonomous regional authority) issued Resolution 1015 restricting mining in sensitive Mocoa areas; Indigenous tutelas have already suspended acts; Andes–Amazon transition zone, páramo complex, memory of the 2017 mudflow. Offset: binding Inga Condagua prior-consultation agreement (Sep 2025) and the Apr 2026 title carve-out. The election de-risked the layer that wasn't the problem.

Differentiator

De-risked metallurgy ahead of the economics — 92% Cu / 97% Mo recoveries, above the resource-model assumptions, which is unusual for a pre-PEA name and removes one of the two things that most often kills a PEA (the other being capex). Second: the molybdenum. At Mo prices well above historical norms, a 0.039% Mo grade turns a mediocre 0.31% Cu deposit into a 0.51% CuEq one — the credit is the thesis, not a footnote. Third: Trafigura offtake secured pre-PEA, i.e. a route to market before a mine plan exists. Fourth, and previously missed: a legally binding Prior Consultation (Consulta Previa) agreement with the Inga Condagua Indigenous Nation, protocolised Sep 20, 2025 after ten official sessions, with the community representing itself — one of the hardest hurdles in Colombian mining, done. Plus the April 2026 title consolidation (ANM-approved unified concession, term reset to a new exploration stage) with no forestry-reserve or protected-area overlap per the company, which resolved the overlap that started the conflict and let exploration formally resume; three rigs turning. Note: that is the national title — Corpoamazonia's July 2026 Resolution 1015 still sits on top at the regional level.

Caveat: trader/financier backing (Denarius/Giustra, Trafigura) is validation of the metal flow, not of the mine — no miner has put its name on this. And local sentiment is contested, not settled: residents worry about the environment, but many in Putumayo say they need the work.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, mostly confidence · moves the needle: low–medium. Recent drilling is largely infill reproducing the model (771 m @ 0.54% CuEq), which de-risks the PEA. The genuine step-out test is La Estrella, assays pending, within a funded 23,000 m programme.

At 1.1 Bt it needs economics more than tonnes.

Entry plan · €1,000 as an illustration — the mirror of Hot Chili's
Step 0 · waitingNothing bought. Alerts set: the PEA release (guided Q4 2026); any headline containing "Corpoamazonia", "tutela", "Resolution 1015" or "suspension"; the La Estrella step-out assays; a price alert at C$0.85. Plan written 28 Sep 2026 at ~C$1.10 (52-wk high C$1.48; Aug placement C$0.72). The €1,000 is illustrative (≈ C$1,500 ≈ ~1,350 shares); in a portfolio that gives Hot Chili €1,000, this name gets €500–700 of the same money — it is a Risk 4, and a licence loss in Putumayo is a −70% event, not a −50% one.

Most of the money goes in after the event, not before it. The PEA is the first NPV this company will ever have — until it lands, ~1.3–1.6¢/lb is faith, not arithmetic — and the undated event here is a negative (a court or regional-authority ruling), where Hot Chili's undated events are positives. Same logic, opposite conclusion: wait, make the PEA prove it, then buy the licence resolution. Not advice; thresholds written down now so that on the day I read numbers against them, not against the price move.

Step 1optional starter, ≤ 20% (€200) — only on a no-news drawdown

Buy €200 only if the stock trades at or below C$0.85 with no adverse news (roughly the post-placement floor; Giustra and Denarius paid C$0.72 in August). Otherwise nothing before the PEA. If the stock runs into the release, let it run — you are not paying up ahead of the first NPV on a stock already +124% year-to-date.

Step 2the PEA (Q4 2026): read five numbers and one paragraph before doing anything
WhatGreenRed
After-tax NPV (8%) at a copper deck ≤ US$4.25/lb≥ US$1.5B< US$0.8B
Initial capex≤ US$2.0B> US$2.5B
After-tax IRR≥ 20%< 15%
Molybdenum price assumed≤ US$20/lb> US$25/lb — the Mo credit is the grade (0.31% Cu → 0.51% CuEq); an inflated deck fakes the NPV
Starter phasebuilt on the 190 Mt @ 0.94% CuEq core; payback ≤ 4 yrsbulk average from day one; payback > 6 yrs
The permitting paragraph & footprintpit, waste and tailings all outside the Resolution 1015 zones; tailings out of the upper Mocoa basin (or filtered/dry-stack); starter footprint confined to the 190 Mt core; consulta previa referencedany part of the footprint on restricted ground, tailings upstream of Mocoa, or silence on the question

Four or more green → a computable discount exists for the first time: ~US$207M against ≥ US$1.5B is ~0.14× NAV, the deepest in the file after Oroco. Two or more red → the pounds were cheap for a reason. Stop. Re-run the card.

Step 2bthe three PEA scenarios — name the one you are looking at before acting
  1. Goldilocks (~20% likely): four-plus green on the numbers and the whole footprint clean — pit, waste and tailings outside the Resolution 1015 zones, tailings out of the upper Mocoa basin or dry-stack, first decade confined to the 190 Mt @ 0.94% core. Licence odds within five years move from ~25–35% to ~40–50%, not because a court has ruled but because the opposition loses its best exhibit and the pro-mining national government and the Inga get a defensible story. Action: deploy Step 3 and Step 4 on the PEA (€800 total); keep only the starter allocation for a placement. Expect the market to pay for the NPV first and the footprint later — the footprint is the part you are buying.
  2. Base (~55% likely): numbers green but the footprint only partly clean — pit outside 1015 but tailings in the watershed, or the permitting paragraph silent. A computable discount now exists (~0.14× NAV) but the licence question is unchanged. Action: Step 3 only (€500); Step 4 waits for the ruling, a placement or a miner.
  3. Bad (~25% likely): two or more red — NPV under US$0.8B, capex over US$2.5B, an inflated moly deck, or a footprint that needs restricted ground. The cheap pounds were cheap for a reason and the licence fight now has a mine plan to point at. Action: nothing; sell any starter if the footprint is the problem, hold it if only the economics disappointed and a PFS could fix them.

The probabilities are mine and rough; the point is to have decided before the release which scenario earns €800, which earns €500 and which earns nothing, so that the price move on the day doesn't decide it for you.

Step 3main tranche: 50% (€500) — on the PEA
  1. Green and the stock falls or is flat in the following week → buy €500 in the market.
  2. Green and the stock gaps up 20%+ → buy €250, hold the other €250 for Step 4. A PEA re-rate on a stock that has already more than doubled this year typically gives back a third within two months.
  3. Red → nothing. Hold the cash; Step 4's licence event can still change the picture, but only after the PEA has been re-read.
Step 4final 30% (€300) — the first of three triggers
  1. The local-licence question resolves in the company's favour — Resolution 1015 narrowed or annulled, or the tutelas dismissed. This is the single largest re-rate available and it is binary, so it is bought after, not anticipated. Buy within a week of the ruling.
  2. The goldilocks PEA (Step 2b) — deploy the €300 on the PEA alongside Step 3. A clean map alone is not this: hydrology and the tutela process survive a clean map.
  3. A placement. Buy at or near the placement price. With this register it will be priced by Giustra/Denarius, which is a fair proxy for fair value.
  4. A producer or major takes a stake or farm-in — the first miner validation this company would ever have (its backers today are a financier and a trader). Buy that day regardless of price; deploy any Step 3 remainder as well.
Step 5overrides — events that change the plan whatever step it is at
  1. A court order suspending exploration, or an ANLA/ANM exclusion of the Mocoa ground → stop; sell any starter; do not average down. In Colombia these resolve in years, not quarters, and the discount becomes permanent.
  2. Denarius or Giustra selling (an insider filing, a block trade) → the smartest money on the register leaving. Stop adding until you understand why.
  3. PEA slips out of Q4 2026 with no reason given → not a sell, but no starter and no buying until it lands.
Step 6once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if the PFS (2027–28) cuts the PEA NPV by more than a third, or the licence fight escalates from Corpoamazonia to the national level with the executive siding against the project.
  2. Sell half on a double before the PFS — a doubling on a pre-PFS Colombian developer is worth banking half of.
  3. Otherwise hold through the PFS and the first real permitting decision. The thesis is cheap, metallurgically de-risked pounds waiting for economics and a licence; don't trade the infill holes.
PracticalWhere to buy, and the most likely outcome

Liquidity is on the TSXV (CGNT) in CAD; OTCQX (upgraded Sep 2026) is usable; the Frankfurt line is thin — limit orders only. CAD/EUR exposure unhedged at this size. Most likely single outcome: the PEA lands with an NPV around US$1–1.5B on capex around US$2B, the stock moves +15% then drifts back, and the licence question stays unresolved into 2027. The plan then has €500 in at roughly today's price with €500 still waiting — which is the right posture for a name whose biggest event is a court, not a drill.

Plan log: 28 Sep 2026 — plan written at ~C$1.10; Step 0, nothing bought; market cap refreshed to ~US$207M. 28 Sep (later) — three PEA scenarios (goldilocks / base / bad) written out as Step 2b with their allocations; footprint test sharpened: pit/waste/tailings outside 1015 and tailings out of the upper Mocoa basin; a fully clean PEA added as a Step 4 trigger.

No release since 22 Sep (PEA reaffirmed for Q4). No ruling found on Resolution 1015 or the tutelas. A 27 Sep La Silla Vacía investigation links the August Denarius financing to President de la Espriella's circle (a campaign strategist was named a director on 6 Aug and withdrawn on 21 Aug) — a reputational flag on the local licence.

National politics (updated Aug 2026)

Risk down materially. Abelardo de la Espriella won the presidency — faster environmental permitting, strategic-minerals push, "subsoil as a driver of growth" — reversing the Petro-era closure of the frontier to new large-scale metal mining. Tailwind for the eventual national (ANLA) licence. Two caveats: a hardline pro-extraction push can inflame the local layer (Colombia is the deadliest country for environmental defenders); and the term runs only to 2030 — Colombia swung Duque → Petro → de la Espriella in eight years, and Copper Giant's exploitation licence/FID likely lands late in or after this term. The election de-risked the layer that wasn't the problem.

New (late Aug 2026)

MD-070 infill 771 m @ 0.54% CuEq incl. 102 m @ 0.87% CuEq — reproduces the resource model at infill spacing. 23,000 m fully funded 2026 program; La Estrella target drilling, assays pending.

Thesis

A Hunter Dickinson–group explorer whose discovery at AuRORA was good enough for Freeport to earn 60% and elect a further C$75M for another 10% — with Boliden funding a second district and a third held 100%.

The Gate

A maiden AuRORA resource that justifies a ~US$185M valuation for a 30% interest. Freeport completes Stage 2 after ~C$35.9M more spending (post-2026), taking JOY to 70/30. After that, Amarc would typically fund its 30% share or be diluted further. The 2026 programme is C$20M, fully Freeport-funded.

Valuation Anchor

~US$185M for ~30–40% of an undefined discovery plus two other districts — not cheap on any computable measure. You're paying for Freeport's validation and a possible buyout. Same bucket as Gladiator, but with a major at the table and less of the asset.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~19–20% — Robert Dickinson (HDI) ~17%, CEO Diane Nicolson ~1.6%; a private "Sutton Group" holds a further ~18% (likely HDI-affiliated; unverified). Freeport and Boliden are project-level partners with no company equity. Konwave ~2%, Mackenzie ~1.5%. 2026 insider flow: only small selling by minor officers; no insider participation disclosed in the Sep 2026 C$20M placement.

Read: Strong at the Dickinson level (~17%, possibly ~35%); the operating team's exposure is modest.

Jurisdiction risk

National: excellent — BC, Canada. Local: moderate — Toodoggone is remote but developing (next to Centerra's Kemess district and near Thesis Gold's Lawyers), with infrastructure nearby; BC First Nations consultation applies.

The local risk is remoteness and permitting pace, not opposition.

Differentiator

Major-company validation that nothing else in the file can match at this size. Freeport operating, funding C$110M in total, and already studying pre-development at AuRORA; Boliden funding DUKE. Two majors have written real cheques.

The flip side: each earn-in shrinks what Amarc keeps — ~30% of JOY once Stage 2 completes.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed discovery plus a new one · moves the needle: high geologically, diluted for shareholders. AuRORA expansion drilling continues; TWINS is a second discovery in the same district; multiple other targets being surveyed. Freeport's budget increase for 2026 (C$15M → C$20M) is itself a signal.

Next Catalyst

2026 JOY results (AuRORA, TWINS); Freeport completing its Stage 2 earn-in; DUKE programme update (Boliden); AuRORA maiden resource (undated).

Open Questions
  • When does AuRORA get a resource, and how big?
  • Does Freeport eventually buy out Amarc's 30% — at what price?
  • Is Amarc's value driven by copper or gold, given the TWINS gold-copper emphasis?

People
Diane Nicolson (President & CEO, since Nov 2014): PhD economic geology; 20+ yrs exploration. 12 years as CEO. · Robert Dickinson (Chairman, since Founder-era (HDI)): Co-founder Hunter Dickinson Inc.; director/officer of multiple HDI companies (Northern Dynasty, Taseko history). · Gavin Titley (VP Exploration, since n/a): 15+ yrs porphyry Cu exploration in north-central BC. · Braden Jensen (Interim CFO, since 15 Sep 2026): Replaced Carol Li (appointed Jul 2025) who left for 'personal reasons' after ~14 months.
Track record
  • Chair Dickinson / HDI group: Taseko (Gibraltar restart, Prosperity blocked), Northern Dynasty (Pebble - 20+ years, EPA veto 2023, no mine), Curis (Florence, sold to Taseko 2014), Northcliff (Sisson, stalled), Rathdowney (sold) - mixed: operator win at Taseko, long capital-heavy misses at Pebble; general knowledge, not re-fetched
  • CEO Nicolson: 12 years at Amarc; no prior CEO exit found; under her the company signed Freeport (JOY, up to C$110M earn-in) and Boliden (DUKE) deals and made the Aurora Cu-Au-Ag discovery (Jan 2025) with Freeport fundingsource
  • Freeport elected to proceed to C$75M Stage 2 earn-in at JOY in Sep 2025 after Aurora - the partner voted with moneysource
  • First hard-dollar raise in two years: C$20M at C$1.00 in Sep 2026, after share price re-rate; market cap ~C$248Msource

Boards today: Dickinson: chair/director across several HDI companies (Northern Dynasty, Amarc, others - count unverified, likely 3+). Nicolson: Amarc only (unverified).

Fit to this job
Stage: explorer with partner-funded discovery - fits; HDI has decades in BC porphyry Cu-Au (same region, same deposit type). The group has operated (Taseko) and permitted (with difficulty). New for them: nothing at this stage; the risk is the HDI pattern of very long holds without a transaction.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. CEO ownership ~1.46% (~C$3.6M at C$248M cap); CEO total comp C$252,550 (100% salary) - modest. Insiders net sellers ~C$206k in 12 months. Related-party overhead: Hunter Dickinson Services billed C$564k in the June 2026 quarter (C$719k a year earlier) for services, IT, rent and pass-through costs, plus a C$1.08M loan at 10% from a director and significant shareholder (Q1 FY27 statements, SEC 6-K). HDI/Dickinson group holding % not verified.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • HDI structure: management services are provided through Hunter Dickinson Inc. (related party); fees not quantified here (unverified) - a known pattern across HDI companies.
  • Two CFOs in 14 months.
  • Insiders net sellers (~C$206k) over 12 months; director Coughlan sold.
  • Board of only 4, average tenure 24 years - no independent refresh.
  • Financials: negative equity at Mar 2025, Jun 2025 and Mar 2026 before the Sep 2026 raise; C$1.0M director's loan at 10% (R. Dickinson) due Jan 2027; most overhead paid to related-party Hunter Dickinson Services.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$4.5M at 30 June 2026, then a C$20M placement closed in September 2026; overhead of about C$0.6M a quarter gives multi-year runway.
  2. Almost all ground spend is partner money: Freeport funds up to C$75M at JOY and Boliden funds DUKE, so Amarc's own exploration spend is near zero.
  3. Overhead is the real burn, rising from C$1.2M in FY24 to C$1.8M in FY26, most of it paid to related-party Hunter Dickinson Services.
  4. Shares grew only 5% to 225.6M by June 2026, then to about 245.6M after the C$20M placement at C$1.00.
  5. Equity was negative before the raise, the auditor flagged going concern, and a C$1.0M director loan at 10% is due January 2027.

No economic study yet — scoping study due Q1 2027 (originally 'internal scoping study H2 2026'); PFS targeted H2 2027

Zambian copper developer 30 km from First Quantum's Sentinel, 877 kt Cu resource at 0.42%, A$41.6M cash, FQM ~12.5% holder; scoping study due Q1 2027.

Gate A scoping study that shows a low-grade, shallow deposit pays at a capex a junior can fund — or that FQM will pay for. At 0.42% Cu the project only works as a large, shallow open pit with cheap processing. Metallurgy is good (94–95% Cu recovery into 25–32% concentrate at Kabikupa) and recent infill holes (18 m @ 1.31% Cu) are better than the resource average, but no economics exist yet. The scoping study, first promised as an 'internal scoping study in H2 2026', is now 'Q1 2027'. The exit most likely to pay is a First Quantum deal; the risk is that FQM waits and buys cheaply.
