Thesis

Prospect owns 90% of Mumbezhi, a 356 km² land package with 208 Mt @ 0.42% Cu (877 kt Cu) across three deposits, about 30 km from First Quantum's Sentinel mine. First Quantum paid a 36% premium for 15% in Apr 2025 and has said Mumbezhi could extend Sentinel's life. The company is cashed up (A$41.6M, no debt) through a 32,000 m Phase 3 programme and a scoping study in Q1 2027, run by the team that sold Arcadia for US$378M.

The Gate

A scoping study that shows a low-grade, shallow deposit pays at a capex a junior can fund — or that FQM will pay for. At 0.42% Cu the project only works as a large, shallow open pit with cheap processing. Metallurgy is good (94–95% Cu recovery into 25–32% concentrate at Kabikupa) and recent infill holes (18 m @ 1.31% Cu) are better than the resource average, but no economics exist yet. The scoping study, first promised as an 'internal scoping study in H2 2026', is now 'Q1 2027'. The exit most likely to pay is a First Quantum deal; the risk is that FQM waits and buys cheaply.

Valuation Anchor

EV ~A$210M (~US$145M) after cash, for ~790 kt attributable Cu: roughly US$0.08/lb or ~US$185/t of resource copper, all open-pit, Indicated+Inferred. That is a developer price for what is still a pre-PEA resource, paid for because First Quantum sits 30 km away and on the register. The market is paying for the FQM option and for resource growth, not for economics that exist yet.

Shareholder structure

Eagle Eye Asset Holdings (Gaurav Gupta, director) ~12.7–15.1%; First Quantum (FQMA Holdings) ~12.5% (15% at Apr 2025, board nominee right, technical working group, right to participate in raises); institutions ~14% (Morgan Stanley 3.8%, Konwave 3.0%, MBM 2.6%, 1832 1.2%); directors ~4% (Hosack 21.2M shares ~2.5%, Goldberg 8.1M ~1%, Wheatley 5.9M ~0.7%). Hosack is a repeat on-market buyer: A$201k at A$0.24 on 6 Oct 2026, A$201k at A$0.20 in Dec 2025, A$504k in Apr 2024, A$391k in Oct 2022. No insider sales found.

Read: A major with a 30 km-away mine on the register and a CEO who keeps buying with his own money — the register is the thesis.

Jurisdiction risk

National: good for Africa — Zambia under Hichilema (re-elected Aug 2026 with >50%, opposition disputed the count) has kept a stable royalty regime and a 3 Mtpa-by-2031 copper target; FQM, Barrick and KoBold are all investing. Watch the kwacha, power supply and the new Minerals Regulation Commission, whose consent was needed for the 5% transfer. Local: two granted Large Scale Mining Licences, no community dispute reported; North-Western Province already hosts Sentinel and Kansanshi so mining is the local economy.

One of the easier African addresses for copper; the licences are mining licences, not exploration permits.

Differentiator

First Quantum's Sentinel is 30 km away and FQM owns ~12.5% of the company. FQM's country head has said Mumbezhi 'could have a significant impact on the mine life of Sentinel'; the grades are similar to Sentinel's. The CEO (12 years at FQM) and a director (FQM founding director Matt Pascall) know the buyer.

The obvious exit is a trade sale or toll-treatment deal with FQM, which caps the upside as much as it underwrites the downside.

Exploration upside

356 km² with three deposits and a pipeline of targets · moves the needle: medium–high Phase 3 (four rigs) is infilling Nyungu Central, stepping out to the south-east where a new zone sits under a shallow EM anomaly, and testing Sharamba, Kabikupa, Chipimpa and Kamafamba. Resource grew 63% in Feb 2026 and 20% in May 2026. The first infill hole returned 18 m @ 1.31% Cu, better than the resource grade, which matters more for economics than more tonnes at 0.4%.

Next Catalyst

Infill and extensional assays from Nyungu Central through Q4 2026 (20 holes pending at 1 Oct 2026), then the scoping study in Q1 2027. A resource update before the study is likely but the company has not given a date.

Open Questions
  • Does the scoping study show a capex and strip ratio a junior can finance at 0.42% Cu, or only a project that works inside FQM's Sentinel complex?
  • Do the infill holes lift the grade of the Indicated core (NCDD040 suggests yes) or just confirm 0.4%?
  • What are GDC's rights on its 10% — free carry or contributing — and will FQM top up or wait?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 4/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 4/5

One clean exit (Arcadia, US$378M) and a major brought in at a premium; the right people for a Zambian copper sale to FQM. Held at B rather than A because the team has never studied or built a copper mine, the study date is already sliding, and the headlines run ahead of the assays.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Sam Hosack (Managing Director & CEO, since MD since Jul 2018): 12+ years at First Quantum before Prospect; led the 2022 sale of 87% of Arcadia (Zimbabwe lithium) to Huayou Cobalt for US$377.8M. Paid A$633k in FY2026 (A$674k FY2025). · Ian Goldberg (Executive Director Finance & CFO, since Director since Jul 2024; company secretary from Mar 2021): Chartered accountant, ~28 years mining finance. Paid A$498k FY2026. · Mark Wheatley (Non-Executive Chair, since n/a): Resources director since 2003; ex-Peninsula Energy director (to Jul 2025). · Matt Pascall (Non-Executive Director, since ~2025): Mining engineer; founding director and senior executive of First Quantum, Zambia experience. Appears to be the FQM-era link though not stated as FQM's nominee. · Gaurav Gupta (Non-Executive Director, since n/a): Represents Eagle Eye Asset Holdings, the largest holder (~15% at the Feb 2026 placement). · Doug Jones (Non-Executive Director, since Oct 2025): Geologist, 45+ years; ex-GM Exploration Perseus Mining. Track record
  • Hosack: Prospect sold 87% of Arcadia to Huayou Cobalt for US$377.8M in 2022, ~A$1.23/share implied, a ~78% premium to the 10-day VWAP — a clean win for shareholderssource
  • Hosack/Goldberg: bought 85% of Mumbezhi from GDC for US$6.5M (May 2024), then 5% more for US$4.25M (Mar 2026); resource went from nothing to 877 kt Cu in two yearssource
  • First Quantum paid A$0.15 (36% premium) for 15% in Apr 2025; A$45M placement at A$0.38 in Feb 2026 with institutional demand — the team can raise money at good pricessource
  • Namibian lithium (Omaruru) was wound down after the lithium price fell; non-binding offers received Jul 2026 — a loss owned plainlysource

Boards today: Hosack: Prospect only (no other listed roles found). Wheatley: chair here, stepped off Peninsula Energy in 2025. Pascall and Jones each hold one other-company background but no competing listed executive role found.

Fit to this job
Stage: resource-to-study developer in Zambia — fits exactly: Hosack spent 12 years at FQM, Pascall was an FQM founding director, and the likely buyer is FQM. Deposit: Copperbelt sediment-hosted copper at Sentinel-type grades — FQM is the world's specialist in exactly this. New for them: Prospect has never built or studied a copper mine itself; Arcadia was sold before construction.
Skin & pay
4/5 — ~2.5% stake largely bought at market over four years, still adding (Oct 2026); pay modest against the cap. Hosack 21.2M shares (~2.5%, ~A$6.4M at A$0.30) plus 6.0M options and 1.8M rights; repeat on-market buyer — A$391k Oct 2022, A$201k Jun 2023, A$504k Apr 2024, A$60k Sep 2024, A$201k at A$0.20 Dec 2025, A$201k at A$0.24 on 6 Oct 2026. Goldberg 8.1M shares (~1%), bought 200,000 on 6 Oct 2026. Jones bought 465,116 in Dec 2025. No insider sales found. Hosack's pay A$633k ≈ 0.25% of market cap, flat to down year on year. Red flags
  • Scoping study date drifted from 'H2 2026' to 'Q1 2027' without being called a slip.
  • Two clarifications in a month (Jul and Aug 2026) after assay-light, strongly worded headlines.
  • The largest shareholder's principal (Gupta) sits on the board; the second largest (FQM) is the natural buyer — minority holders' interests may not set the exit price.
  • Annual report gives Phase 3 as both ~26,000 m and ~32,000 m in different sections; the number keeps moving (now ~32,000 m incl. RC/AC).

What the numbers say
  1. Cash went from A$8.3M at 30 Jun 2024 to A$36.6M at 30 Jun 2026 plus a A$5.0M 12-month term deposit (A$41.6M in total, no debt); at the June-2026 quarter's outflow of A$3.8M (A$1.5M operating + A$2.3M exploration) that is about 11 quarters, but the 26,000m Phase 3 programme that started in May 2026 will lift the burn (the September-2025 quarter, mid-Phase 2, cost A$8.0M).
  2. Over FY25-FY26 about A$18.5M was paid into capitalised exploration and A$12.9M into staff and admin (Appendix 5B), so overhead is roughly 40% of cash spend; overhead is flat at A$6.1M (FY25) to A$6.8M (FY26) a year, A$1.2-2.1M a quarter, and in FY25 it exceeded the money put in the ground (A$7.1M vs A$6.1M).
  3. Funding is 100% equity: A$9.1M placement/SPP at A$0.10 (Aug 2024), A$18.5M from First Quantum Minerals and Eagle Eye at A$0.15 (Apr-Jun 2025), A$45.0M placement at A$0.38 (Feb/Apr 2026, A$42.4M net) and A$1.4M of option exercises; shares rose 74% from 478.7M to 832.7M in two years.
  4. Non-exploration uses: A$6.1M (US$4.25M) in March 2026 to lift the Mumbezhi interest from 85% to 90%, A$1.3M received from selling the Step Aside lithium project (Nov 2025), and a A$1.9M FY26 loss on discontinued (Zimbabwe lithium) operations.
  5. Net loss A$7.9M in FY26 vs A$8.1M in FY25 and A$7.0M in FY24 is essentially overhead plus A$1.3M a year of share-based pay because exploration is capitalised; the E&E asset grew from A$14.0M to A$39.2M and equity from A$26.3M to A$82.7M.

Thesis

High-grade Cu-Au-Ag-Mo skarn on the historic Whitehorse Copper Belt. Near-surface, tier-1 jurisdiction, fully funded; 2026 drilling expanded to 50,000 m+. Cowley hits: 40 m @ 1.98% Cu (Aug 2026), 8.3 m @ 4.99% Cu; Cub East high-grade continuity over 300 m+ strike. Moly is a real by-product credit.

The Gate

No NI 43-101 resource yet — the maiden inferred resource at Cowley is the re-rate event. Slipped: originally guided Q2 2026, now "2026" — and with the Cowley delineation programme expanded to 10,000 m+ and a second phase on the Southern Limb still to run, a slip into 2027 is plausible. Plus an unusual social-license risk: the project sits within Whitehorse city limits amid local zoning opposition (Class 3 permit held; First Nations consultation positive).

Valuation Anchor

Not a value bet. Pre-resource → no EV/lb possible, so it screens "infinitely expensive" vs. Hot Chili/Copper Giant. Stock up ~200%+ over 6 months; premium already priced. Same bucket as Atex.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~4.6% (CEO Jason Bontempo ~1.6%; others <1.2% each; largely option/RSU-derived). Largest holder is the drilling contractor Kluane Drilling ~10–11% (paid in shares). Funds: 1832 / Dynamic ~8.1%, Mackenzie ~3.6%, IG ~1.7%; BlackRock World Mining led the C$35M Jul 2026 placement (stake undisclosed). Macquarie/Orimco: no evidence as shareholders. Minimal insider open-market buying.

Read: Modest — the anchor is institutional money, not management.

Jurisdiction risk

National: among the best — Yukon, Canada; tier-one rule of law, Class 3 permit held, First Nations consultation positive. Local: unusual and unpriced. The project sits within Whitehorse city limits — municipal zoning and mining-plan opposition in a territorial capital is politically fraught in a way remote Yukon ground never is.

The same proximity that gives free infrastructure creates the fight. And with no resource, none of this is in the price yet.

Differentiator

Skarn grade — 1.5–2% Cu, four to five times the porphyry names here (Hot Chili 0.37%, Copper Giant 0.31%, Osisko 0.32% CuEq), and near-surface. High grade + shallow = small footprint, low strip, modest capex if it ever gets built — a fundamentally different cost equation from a billion-tonne bulk-tonnage porphyry. Second, and genuinely unusual: infrastructure is already there — the project sits beside a territorial capital, with roads, grid power, an airport and a workforce, so there's effectively no infrastructure capex, the single biggest burden on Los Azules. Third: brownfield pedigree — Hudson Bay mined 10.5 Mt @ 1.5% Cu + 0.75 g/t Au from this belt (1967–82), so the system is proven to host economic grades.

The same proximity that gives free infrastructure is also the social-licence risk: mining inside city limits. The differentiator and the gate are the same fact.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, critical for scale · moves the needle: very high. Cowley delineation (40 m @ 1.98% Cu; 8.3 m @ 4.99% Cu), Cub East continuity over 300 m+ of strike, the Great Southern / Chiefs trend, 50,000 m+ programme.

Tonnage is the gate, so every step-out that holds grade de-risks the maiden resource directly — here exploration isn't a bonus, it's the thesis.

Next Catalyst

Maiden Cowley resource (2026); continued Cub East growth; Great Southern / Chiefs-trend drilling.

Open Questions
  • How much tonnage does the maiden resource show?
  • (Skarns run high-grade but often small — historic belt production ~10.5 Mt.) Why the slip, and does the in-city friction escalate?
Context & updates
15 Oct 2026 update

Whitehorse City Council voted down the company's OCP amendment on 13 Oct (reported 15 Oct by Yukon News and CBC), so the three green-space tracts inside city limits stay closed to drilling for now. This narrows where Gladiator can expand on the belt; the Cowley programme under the existing Class 3 permit continues as far as reported. Chance it works 33% → 30%; odds of a 3× stay ~9% because the shares are 12% lower than at the 10 Oct assessment.

3 Oct 2026 refresh

28 Sep: 24.0 m @ 2.37% Cu from 8 m at Cowley. Cowley drilling doubled to >16,000 m with most assays pending; the company still guides the maiden resource for 2026, but a slip into 2027 looks likely.

A kilometre-scale copper-gold porphyry discovery in BC's Babine district, with South32 (19.9%), Teck (12.9%) and Eric Sprott on the register and ~C$50M cash for an 80-hole programme.

Gate Turning long, mostly low-grade intercepts into a resource the market will pay for. Headline holes are 1,001 m @ 0.46% CuEq, but the copper inside them is 0.25% Cu; the CuEq leans on gold at US$3,375/oz and an assumed 80% recovery for every metal. True widths are unknown and no resource exists after ~90,000 m of drilling since 2022. The 2027 maiden resource and PEA (PEA start H2 2027) must show a core of 0.8–1% CuEq big enough to carry a low-strip open pit, and metallurgy (ten-sample test programme under way) must confirm the recoveries. The nearby Morrison deposit (Pacific Booker) was refused an environmental certificate in 2012 and never recovered, so BC permitting is a real second gate even with a signed Lake Babine Nation agreement.

Deposit No resource. Footprint ~1.5 × 1.7 km, South Zone 700 × 600 m to >800 m depth.

Thesis

NAK has produced some of the longest mineralised intercepts in Canada (1,001 m @ 0.46% CuEq; 802 m @ 0.71% CuEq, both from near surface) in a road-accessible district next to the former Bell and Granisle mines. Two majors fund it without warrants, and a 55,000 m programme through April 2027 is meant to turn the South Zone into a maiden resource and PEA in 2027. The bet is that bulk tonnage at ~0.4–0.5% CuEq, with a gold-rich higher-grade core, is worth a lot more than US$155M once it has a number on it.

The Gate

Turning long, mostly low-grade intercepts into a resource the market will pay for. Headline holes are 1,001 m @ 0.46% CuEq, but the copper inside them is 0.25% Cu; the CuEq leans on gold at US$3,375/oz and an assumed 80% recovery for every metal. True widths are unknown and no resource exists after ~90,000 m of drilling since 2022. The 2027 maiden resource and PEA (PEA start H2 2027) must show a core of 0.8–1% CuEq big enough to carry a low-strip open pit, and metallurgy (ten-sample test programme under way) must confirm the recoveries. The nearby Morrison deposit (Pacific Booker) was refused an environmental certificate in 2012 and never recovered, so BC permitting is a real second gate even with a signed Lake Babine Nation agreement.

Valuation Anchor

~US$155M for a drilled-out porphyry footprint with no resource, two majors at 32.8% combined and ~C$50M cash (cash is roughly a quarter of the cap). The market is paying ~US$120M for the ground. A plausible maiden resource of 500 Mt–1 Bt at ~0.4–0.5% CuEq would be 4–10 Blb CuEq; BC bulk-tonnage developers with PEAs have traded at roughly US$0.02–0.05/lb, which brackets the current price rather than sitting far above it. Pacific Booker's board argued in Apr 2026 that AE would need a Morrison-sized resource just to justify its cap.

Shareholder structure

Strategics ~42%: South32 19.9% (40.99M shares, board nominee right, top-up and information rights while >5%), Teck ~12.9% (first strategic, May 2023; did not follow the Nov 2024 South32 round and diluted from 19.9%), Eric Sprott ~9.3% (19.2M shares, Mar 2026). Orecap Invest (chaired by AE chair Stephen Stewart) held 11.8M shares / 8.9% in Nov 2024, ~5.7% today if unchanged (unverified). Insiders: Stewart ~10.2M shares (~5.0%), CEO Moreau 2.3M (~1.1%). Institutions otherwise small; free float ~121M shares.

Read: Two majors and Sprott bought without warrants and have not sold; Teck's decision not to keep pace in 2024 is the one soft spot.

Jurisdiction risk

National: low — British Columbia, Canada; road, rail (CN), Highway 16 and hydro nearby; 85 km from Smithers. Local: moderate — NAK sits in Lake Babine Nation territory under an expanded five-year exploration agreement (Aug 2023) with consent for drilling and Nation participation in baseline work; many field staff are Lake Babine members. The district precedent is poor: Pacific Booker's Morrison copper-gold porphyry, ~30 km away in the same Nation's territory, was denied an EA certificate in 2012 over Morrison Lake sockeye concerns and has been dormant since; BC's 2024–26 mine permitting pace is slow.

Exploration consent is in hand; mine consent is a different, later question, and Morrison shows it can be refused.

Differentiator

Intercept length and major-company money. Kilometre-long mineralised holes from surface are rare anywhere; South32 and Teck have together put in ~C$44M with no warrants and keep topping up. The treasury (~C$50M) is larger than most peers' market caps.

The flip side: 0.25% Cu bulk grade needs a big pit and a strong gold price to work.

Exploration upside

Open at depth and east · district ground added · moves the needle: medium–high The South Zone is open to the east near surface and to the northwest at depth, and the southern margin of the Babine stock is lightly drilled. Hearne Hill South (4.5 km away, no modern drilling) and the staked Morrison-area ground give the company district targets, but the next 12 months are about density at NAK, not new discoveries.

Next Catalyst

Continuous assays from the three-rig programme into Q2 2027 (first Phase 2 infill results Q4 2026–Q1 2027), metallurgical results, then the maiden resource in 2027 and PEA start in H2 2027. A first drill test of Hearne Hill South is possible in 2027.

Open Questions
  • What is the tonnage and grade of the ≥0.8% CuEq core, and how much of the 1 km intercepts is sub-0.3% Cu halo that a pit cannot pay for?
  • Do metallurgical tests support the flat 80% recovery assumed for copper, gold, silver and molybdenum in CuEq?
  • Will the 2027 resource and PEA dates hold, and does either major move to a bid or a JV rather than another top-up?
  • Can a new open-pit copper mine be permitted in Lake Babine territory after Morrison's 2012 refusal?

Track record
  • Moreau/Stewart: pivoted the shell to NAK in 2022 (acquired after no work since 1996), hit 125 m @ 1.02% CuEq in the maiden hole (Nov 2022) and have drilled ~90,000 m since — a real discovery, delivered (https://americaneaglegold.ca/news/; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/306848)
  • Brought in Teck (May 2023, topped up Nov 2023 at C$0.215), South32 (C$29.2M at C$0.875, Nov 2024, 15% premium to VWAP) and Eric Sprott (C$23M, Mar 2026), all without warrants — strong financing record for a junior (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/187979; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/229610; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/289306)
  • 2025 programme: planned ~30,000 m from May 2025 on a C$12–15M budget (Feb 2025); completed 31,500 m (Jan 2026) — delivered (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/239864; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/281589)
  • Market cap C$23.5M (Nov 2023) → C$78.5M (Jul 2024) → C$222M (Sep 2026): shareholders who held through the discovery have done wellsource
  • Moreau and Stewart: no prior mine built or company sold that could be found; the Ore Group stable (Orecap, XXIX Metal, Mistango, Awalé etc.) is a set of small explorers rather than exits — unverified for outcomes
  • Hostile all-share bid for Pacific Booker (Apr 2026, 1.41 AE per BKM share, ~C$31M) rejected by the target board as 'highly opportunistic' and valuing Morrison at ~US$0.01/lb; AE terminated it on 5 Jun 2026 without a stated reason, then optioned and staked ground around (not including) the Morrison deposit (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/292376; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/295128/; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/300311)

Boards today: Stewart chairs eight listed juniors and a private consortium; Moreau sits on five other Ore Group boards besides AE. South32 has a board-nominee right (nominee not identified on the company's board page). Stothart is the one independent with operating depth.

Fit to this job
Stage: discovery heading for a maiden resource — the team has done exactly this part well (drilling, financing, majors). Deposit: bulk-tonnage Cu-Au porphyry in BC; Prowse and Greig are BC porphyry geologists, Stothart worked at Bell next door. Region: Canada, Lake Babine territory — agreement in place. New for them: resource estimation, a PEA and BC mine permitting; no executive has taken a project through a study or a permit. Hired Pierre-Luc Richard (May 2026) to steer the resource work.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stakes (chair ~5%, CEO ~1%), mostly founder stock and exercised options; no selling found. Chair Stephen Stewart ~10.2M shares (~5.0%, ~C$11M); exercised 1M options at ~C$0.20 in May 2026 and kept the shares; the only insider transaction in 12 months, no sales found. CEO Moreau 2.3M shares (~1.1%, ~C$2.5M). CEO total pay ~C$265k (81% salary) against a ~C$220M cap — modest. Origin of Stewart's stake (founder paper vs purchases) not verified. Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Headline CuEq numbers (1,001 m @ 0.46% CuEq) carry only 0.25% Cu; gold at US$3,375/oz and a flat 80% recovery do a lot of work. Metallurgy is untested.
  • The 2026 flow-through structure gave Sprott, Teck and South32 shares at an effective C$0.77 back-end price while the stock traded C$1.1–1.4; ordinary holders bore the discount.
  • Chair spread across eight listed juniors and a private group; CEO on five other related boards. Orecap (chaired by Stewart) is a ~6% holder — a related-party shareholder, though no fees to Ore Group were found (unverified).
  • A hostile bid launched and dropped within eight weeks with no reason given, and a CEO quoted calling AE 'a $260 million company' when the basic cap was ~C$230M.
  • 'From surface' language for NAK25-78 where the interval starts at 54 m.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash went from C$35.9M (Dec 2024) to C$22.9M (Dec 2025) to C$44.0M (Mar 2026) and C$53.3M at 30 Jun 2026 after two flow-through placements of C$34.0M gross (19.2M shares at C$1.20 in March, 9.65M at C$1.13 in April). 2025 operating burn was about C$15M and the 2026 programme (>50,000 m, 3-5 rigs, May 2026-Apr 2027, C$23M of flow-through money to spend by 31 Dec 2026) is bigger, so C$53M covers roughly the current drill season; expect another raise before the 2027 season.
  2. Nearly all money goes into the ground: exploration expensed was C$8.0M in 2024 against C$1.4M of cash overhead (15% of spend) and C$7.3M in the first nine months of 2025 against C$0.8M (10%). Overhead is flat at about C$0.3-0.4M a quarter.
  3. Share count rose from 114.8M (Dec 2023) to 167.8M (Dec 2024), 192.6M (Mar 2026) and about 206M (Sep 2026), +79%. South32 paid C$29.2M at C$0.875 in Nov 2024 and keeps topping up to 19.9% (C$0.8M Jun 2025, C$0.7M at C$1.09 Sep 2026); Teck holds 12.9%, Eric Sprott 9.5%.
  4. No debt, no revenue, no capitalised assets. Flow-through premium recoveries (C$2.4M in 2024, C$1.1M in 9M 2025) flatter the net loss; the C$3.8M premium liability at Mar 2026 will unwind as the 2026 money is spent. Share-based pay was C$1.5M in 2024 and C$1.3M in 9M 2025.
  5. Unusual: the derived Oct-Dec 2025 quarter shows a C$4.9M net loss (FY2025 C$12.3M from the deficit roll-forward vs C$7.3M for 9M) and about C$7.6M of cash outflow with no shares issued, well above earlier quarters; and the company spent April-June 2026 on a hostile bid for Pacific Booker Minerals (F-10 filed 14 Apr 2026, terminated 5 Jun 2026) whose costs will sit in Q2 2026. PEA Feb 2026 (eff. 22 Feb 2026): NPV8 US$1.95B, IRR 22.7%, payback 3.9 yrs at US$4.60/lb; NPV8 US$3.22B / IRR 32% at US$5.75; initial capex US$1.54B; 174 Mlb/yr Y1–15; AISC US$2.06/lb; 21-yr life

Arizona copper developer with a 5.2 Blb M&I oxide deposit (PEA NPV8 US$2.0B, capex US$1.5B) and a small Rio Tinto-funded cathode mine next door; ~US$165M cap.

Gate Financing a US$1.5B open-pit build from a US$165M base, with a stream and royalties already on the ground. The deposit is proven and the mine plan is conventional (open pit, heap leach, SX-EW), so the gate is money and partners, not geology. The 2026 PEA is Class 5 (-25%/+30%) and includes a US$300M acid plant, a material sorter, an I-10 highway relocation and a cement co-product; the PFS (budget US$29.7M, ~18 months, targeted H1 2028) must hold those numbers. Triple Flag holds a US$65M copper stream (16.5% of refined copper at 25% of spot on the first stage, sliding to 5.75% and 3.5%) plus a 3% GRR, and Altius a GRR, so a builder's economics are thinner than the headline. Johnson Camp cathode revenue first repays Nuton's Stage 2 costs (deferred revenue balance US$200M at 30 Jun 2026), so the mine does not yet fund the company. The May 2026 buyback option (US$65M, exercisable only with a change of control announced by 31 Mar 2028) tells you how management expects this to end.

Funding & next catalyst

US$33.2M at 30 Jun 2026, of which US$25.1M non-Nuton and US$8.2M Nuton-related (after the C$34.5M bought deal closed 3 Jun 2026); US$5.3M paid out 7 Jul 2026 to cash-settle the Greenstone debentures; US$8M due from Nuton in Q4 2026 for the optimized Stage 2 plan
Debt
None after 1 Oct 2026 (Triple Flag converted the last US$1.5M debenture at US$0.19 into 7.9M shares plus 1.6M for interest; ~US$15M secured legacy debt retired Jan 2026, US$5.3M Greenstone convertibles cash-settled Jul 2026). But: Triple Flag stream derivative liability US$94.8M fair value, Nuton deferred revenue US$204.5M, total liabilities US$387.5M, equity negative US$17.8M at 30 Jun 2026
Burn · runway
Operating cash flow is NOT positive: H1 2026 net cash used in operations US$35.3M (H1 2025: US$8.3M), investing US$22.0M, financing +US$69.8M. The Q2 net income of US$13.1M comes from recognising US$9.8M of deferred Nuton demonstration-service revenue; cathode sales were US$13.7M against US$7.4M production cost in Q2, but that revenue repays Nuton first. Non-Nuton spend ahead: ~US$15M drill program (2026–27) and US$29.7M PFS budget over ~18 months
Next catalyst
NYSE American listing (ticker GUNN, expected late Oct 2026); preliminary drill results Q4 2026; MLRP permit amendment approval before end-2026; Johnson Camp at nameplate by end-2026
Partly funded to the next catalyst Non-Nuton cash of ~US$20M after the July debenture settlement covers corporate costs and the first year of drilling, and the company says it is funded for 12 months. It does not cover the full US$45M of drilling plus PFS to H1 2028; a US$200M shelf is in place and the NYSE listing is the obvious venue, so expect an equity raise or a strategic placement in 2027.
Thesis

Gunnison owns one of the largest undeveloped oxide copper deposits in the US (846M short tons M&I @ 0.33% Cu, 5.19 Blb) in a state-permit-only jurisdiction, next to its own operating SX-EW plant at Johnson Camp, which Nuton (Rio Tinto) is funding as a sulfide-leach demonstration and which reached commercial production in Sep 2026. The 2026 PEA shows NPV8 US$1.95B and 22.7% IRR at US$4.60/lb (US$3.2B at US$5.75), but initial capex is US$1.54B, roughly nine times the market cap, and a Triple Flag stream plus two gross revenue royalties sit on the project. The market pays ~8% of PEA NPV; the re-rate case is a PFS (H1 2028), state permits by mid-2028 and a strategic partner or takeover, for which a US$65M stream/royalty buyback option tied to a change of control before 31 Mar 2028 has already been arranged.

The Gate

Financing a US$1.5B open-pit build from a US$165M base, with a stream and royalties already on the ground. The deposit is proven and the mine plan is conventional (open pit, heap leach, SX-EW), so the gate is money and partners, not geology. The 2026 PEA is Class 5 (-25%/+30%) and includes a US$300M acid plant, a material sorter, an I-10 highway relocation and a cement co-product; the PFS (budget US$29.7M, ~18 months, targeted H1 2028) must hold those numbers. Triple Flag holds a US$65M copper stream (16.5% of refined copper at 25% of spot on the first stage, sliding to 5.75% and 3.5%) plus a 3% GRR, and Altius a GRR, so a builder's economics are thinner than the headline. Johnson Camp cathode revenue first repays Nuton's Stage 2 costs (deferred revenue balance US$200M at 30 Jun 2026), so the mine does not yet fund the company. The May 2026 buyback option (US$65M, exercisable only with a change of control announced by 31 Mar 2028) tells you how management expects this to end.

Valuation Anchor

~US$165M for 5.19 Blb M&I of oxide copper in Arizona, i.e. ~US$0.03/lb M&I and ~8% of PEA NPV8, with a 25 Mlb/yr SX-EW plant and a Rio Tinto technology partner on site. Against that the project carries a US$95M stream liability, two GRRs and US$204M of Nuton deferred revenue, and needs US$1.5B. Peers the market uses: Arizona Sonoran (Cactus, PFS) and Faraday/other US oxide developers; the CEO says GCU trades at about a quarter of the peer group on contained copper (Crux interview, undated).

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~2.5% (Stephen Twyerould, ex-CEO, 1.57%; Roland Goodgame 0.5%; CEO Craig Hallworth 0.17%). No strategic shareholder on the register: Nuton/Rio Tinto funds Johnson Camp under an option agreement (may form a 49/51 JV after Stage 2) but holds no equity. Institutions per Simply Wall St 3.3% (ALPS 0.86%, RBC GAM 0.49%, Aegis 0.49%, CI 0.44%, US Global, Ninepoint); management claims ~60% institutional across 40–50 holders after Greenstone's 33.9% block was placed in Feb–Apr 2026 (unverified). Insider buys 2026: Hallworth 150,000 at C$0.45 (May) and 32,500 at C$0.44 (Jan); Winton 94,750 at C$0.44 (Apr); Bingham 33,500 at C$0.42 (Jun); Chair DuVal 31,799 at C$0.43 (Sep). No insider sales found.

Read: Tiny insider stakes but steady small open-market buying; the register is now widely held with no anchor holder, which cuts both ways for a takeover.

Jurisdiction risk

National: low — Arizona, USA; the company states there is no federal nexus (private/state land), so permitting is State of Arizona only: Mined Land Reclamation Plan amendment (submitted Sep 2026, approval expected before end-2026), Aquifer Protection Permit amendment (ADEQ, submit Q1 2027, decision ~Q1 2028) and Air Quality Permit amendment (submit mid-2027, decision mid-2028). Copper cathode sold domestically (to AWS per management). Local: low–moderate — Johnson Camp is a historic mine site with an operating plant; Governor Hobbs publicly recognised the company for job creation (Sep 2026); the open-pit plan needs a portion of Interstate 10 relocated (ADOT), a Union Pacific rail spur, and a 1 Mt/yr cement plant, which widens the stakeholder set. Water: the earlier ISR operation held an EPA UIC permit; the heap-leach plan changes the water footprint and goes through ADEQ.

One of the easiest copper jurisdictions on the tracker on paper; the I-10 relocation is the item most likely to add years.

Differentiator

Scale plus an operating plant plus Rio Tinto money, in Arizona. 5.2 Blb of M&I oxide copper is a rare US asset; the SX-EW plant and workforce already exist; Nuton pays for the demonstration mine and gets a JV option, not equity. The flip side is the structure: a stream, two royalties and ~US$200M of Nuton cost recovery stand ahead of shareholders, and the deposit's first life (in-situ recovery, 2019–2022) failed.

The change-of-control buyback option (by 31 Mar 2028) makes this a cleaner takeover target than most PEA-stage peers.

Exploration upside

District with nine satellite targets · moves the needle: medium The company targets +1.2 Blb of added resource from the 2026–27 program (120 holes, ~US$15M), mainly conversion and expansion at Gunnison and Strong & Harris plus eight holes of district exploration; preliminary results are due Q4 2026 and full results mid-2027. With 5.2 Blb already in M&I the market will pay more for metallurgy (405 column tests, 63 flotation tests under way) and a higher-grade starter pit than for more pounds.

Next Catalyst

NYSE American listing (GUNN) expected late Oct 2026, then preliminary drill and column-leach results in Q4 2026 and the MLRP permit amendment decision before end-2026. Johnson Camp nameplate (25 Mlb/yr) is guided for end-2026.

Open Questions
  • Who writes the US$1.5B cheque: does Nuton/Rio Tinto exercise its 49% JV option, or does the May 2026 buyback option signal a sale before Mar 2028?
  • Do the PFS numbers survive the Class 5 to Class 4 step, including the acid plant, sorter, cement plant and I-10 relocation?
  • When does Johnson Camp cash reach shareholders rather than Nuton's US$200M cost-recovery account?
  • How much equity is raised in 2027 to fund the PFS, and at what price after the NYSE listing?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 2/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

The company's record for shareholders is one large failure (the ISR mine) under the man who still sits on the board, with the loss re-dated into a new plan; the new CEO is five months in with a clean, delivered-on-time record so far (JCM, debt, PEA) and an Arizona-fit team, which keeps this at C rather than D and could become B with a delivered PFS.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Craig Hallworth (President & CEO (and director), since CEO since 15 May 2026; SVP & CFO from Sep 2024): CPA, CFA. Ex-CFO of Hudbay's Arizona business unit (Copper World, Mason financial lead); says he has helped finance and build four mines (USA, Canada, Peru). As CFO he retired ~US$15M of legacy secured debt (Jan 2026), cash-settled the Greenstone convertibles (Jul 2026) and ran the C$34.5M bought deal. · Stephen Twyerould (Director; ex-President & CEO (2010 – May 2026), 'planned retirement', since CEO 2010–2026): Built the Gunnison in-situ recovery mine (first copper late 2020) which never approached nameplate because of CO2 blockage in the wellfield; pivoted the company to Johnson Camp heap leach with Nuton (2023) and to an open-pit plan for Gunnison (2024 PEA). Largest individual holder at 1.57%. · Fred DuVal (Chair of the Board, since unverified): Former Arizona Democratic gubernatorial candidate and Arizona Board of Regents member (background not verified from company pages); bought 31,799 shares at C$0.43 on 2 Sep 2026. Re-elected with 85.7% support at the Jun 2026 AGM, the lowest of the six. · Bjorn Meyer (Chief Operating Officer, since Jun 2026): Ex-Grupo Mexico, SSR Mining, Panasonic Energy; University of Arizona mining engineer. · Matt Bingham (SVP Permitting & External Affairs, since May 2026): Mining/environmental lawyer; led legal, permitting and public affairs for Hudbay's Copper World. Bought 33,500 shares at C$0.42 in Jun 2026. · Roland Goodgame (SVP Projects / Project Development (QP), since unverified): 35+ years at large miners; holds ~0.5%. · Jennifer Hays (CFO, since 12 Oct 2026): Ex-CFO of PacSci EMC (US defense, Ralliant Corp), ~17 years at Intel finance. No mining background; replaces interim CFO Fabio Rocha. · Andre Lauzon (Director, since 1 Oct 2026): Ex-COO Hudbay (ran Arizona unit: Rosemont/Copper World; Copper Mountain turnaround); director of Rupert Resources 2023–26 (sold to Agnico Eagle). · Brian Penney (Director (nominated for the Jun 2026 AGM), since Jun 2026 (unverified)): CEO Tacora Resources, ex-CEO Baffinland Iron Mines.
Track record
  • Gunnison ISR (Twyerould era): 2016 FS/2022 PFS promised 25→75→125 Mlb/yr; first cathode late 2020; CO2 bubbles blocked injection, ramp-up never reached nameplate; by Sep 2021 the company proposed US$13M raffinate-neutralisation capex and later abandoned ISR for an open-pit plan (Dec 2024 PEA) – a loss for shareholders carried through a 33.9% holder (Greenstone) exiting at C$0.40–0.45 in 2026 (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/95969; https://www.mining.com/?p=1087045; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/282806)
  • Johnson Camp restart: Sep 2021 release guided cathode from H2 2022; actual first cathode Aug 2025, under a different (Nuton-funded) plan – ~3-year slip, though the funding model changed (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/95969; https://www.gunnisoncopper.com/news/news-2026/gunnison-copper-achieves-commercial-production-at-johnson-ca2026-09-22-030502)
  • Nuton option (Jul 2023 agreement, Stage 2 elected May 2024): Nuton funds all Stage 2 costs and paid US$5M for infrastructure use; revenue repays Nuton first; Nuton may form a 49/51 JV after Stage 2source
  • Hallworth era (Sep 2024–): JCM from construction decision to production in under 18 months; commercial production declared Sep 2026 in the guided quarter; PEA updated Feb 2026 (NPV8 US$1.26B → US$1.95B); legacy secured debt, Greenstone convertibles and Triple Flag debentures all cleared by Oct 2026; C$34.5M bought deal oversubscribed (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/285349; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/299937)
  • Triple Flag stream (Oct 2018, US$65M + US$10M placement): 16.5%/5.75%/3.5% sliding-scale copper stream at 25% of spot plus 3% GRR; May 2026 buyback option for US$65M, only with a change of control announced by 31 Mar 2028source

Boards today: Hallworth: CEO and director of Gunnison only (no other public boards found). Twyerould stays on the board after retiring as CEO. Lauzon joined Oct 2026 after Rupert Resources was sold. Six directors elected Jun 2026; full list not verified from company pages (board page did not load).

Fit to this job
Stage: PEA-stage developer with a small Nuton-funded mine; the next job is a PFS, three Arizona state permits, an I-10 relocation and a US$1.5B financing. The Hudbay-Arizona trio (Hallworth finance, Bingham permitting, Lauzon operations/board) is a close fit for Arizona permitting and project work. Nobody on the executive has financed a build of this size as principal; the new CFO comes from defence contracting, which fits a US-government-funding strategy more than a mining capital raise. Deposit type (oxide heap leach, SX-EW) is well understood and the plant exists.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stakes (CEO ~0.2%), but repeated small open-market buys by the CEO, chair and officers in 2026 and no selling; pay moderate against the cap. Insiders ~2.5% in total. Hallworth ~0.17% (~882,500 shares, ~C$0.4M) after open-market buys of 150,000 at C$0.45 (22 May 2026) and 32,500 at C$0.44 (2 Jan 2026); Chair DuVal bought 31,799 at C$0.43 (2 Sep 2026); Bingham 33,500 at C$0.42 (Jun 2026); Winton 94,750 at C$0.44 (Apr 2026). Twyerould 1.57% (7.95M shares), no 2026 trades found. No insider sales found. Hallworth total comp US$583K (2025, as CFO) vs ~US$165M cap. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-gcu/gunnison-copper-shares/ownership

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • The deposit's first mine (ISR, 2019–22) failed under the founder-CEO, who stayed 16 years and leaves with 1.57%; the loss was re-framed as a new plan rather than owned in a release.
  • Q2 2026 'net income US$13.1M' headline while H1 operating cash flow was -US$35.3M and equity is negative; the profit is recognised Nuton deferred revenue.
  • The 48C tax-credit reversal (Jul 'key milestone' → Sep 'decided not to claim') was disclosed inside an unrelated release.
  • Stream and royalty structure (Triple Flag 16.5% sliding stream + 3% GRR, Altius GRR) sold in 2018 for US$65M now burdens a US$2B NPV project; the buyback costs US$65M and only works in a takeover.
  • Press releases quote the PEA as 'US$2 billion NPV, 23% IRR' without the US$4.60 price or the US$1.54B capex in the same breath.
  • CEO pay US$583K in 2025 (as CFO) on a company that was ~US$100M at the time – not extreme, but rising fast (US$358K in 2024).

What the numbers say
  1. Cash rose from US$8.2M (Dec 2024) to US$33.2M at 30 Jun 2026, but only US$25.1M is non-Nuton and working capital is -US$40.9M; H1 2026 operating outflow was US$35.3M (US$24.2M in Q2 alone), so at that pace the non-Nuton cash covers roughly two to three quarters and the company itself says the PFS programme needs more financing.
  2. Johnson Camp is producing (4.1 Mlb cathode in H1 2026, ~2.0-2.3 Mlb a quarter at US$5.7-6.1/lb; record revenue US$23.6M in Q2 2026 of which US$13.7M cathode sales and US$9.8M non-cash Nuton deferred-revenue amortisation) yet operating cash flow is negative because cathode proceeds go to Nuton cost recovery first; ~US$204M of Nuton deferred revenue plus a US$36M Stage 2 payable sit on the balance sheet, total liabilities are US$387.5M and equity is -US$17.8M.
  3. Nearly all money goes into Johnson Camp construction funded by Nuton: Nuton advanced US$141.7M in 2025 and US$45.8M in H1 2026 against US$104.7M and US$21.0M of Stage 2 spend; the company's own exploration/permitting spend is small (US$3.3M in 2025, US$2.0M in H1 2026) while overhead has grown to about US$4.3M a quarter (S&A Gunnison + Johnson Camp) from under US$1M a quarter in 2024.
  4. Share count rose 60% from 315.4M (Mar 2025) to 505.5M (Jun 2026) and 515.1M at 30 Sep 2026 through four unit placements (US$18.2M net in 2025), the C$34.5M June 2026 bought deal (US$23.3M net), the January 2026 conversion of the remaining Nebari loan and the autumn 2026 conversion of the last US$1.5M debenture; the Greenstone debentures were cash-settled for US$5.3M in July 2026, leaving the Triple Flag copper stream (derivative liability US$94.8M) as the only remaining financial debt besides leases.
  5. Reported earnings are driven by non-cash fair-value swings (stream derivative -US$21.2M and Nuton payable -US$23.3M in 2025; +US$56.7M derivative gain and -US$38.8M impairment in 2024), so the FY2025 loss of US$56.4M and H1 2026 profit of US$14.8M say little about cash generation.

Thesis

100% of Berg, a Cu-Mo-Ag-Au porphyry in the Tahtsa Ranges of central BC, 116 km by forest road from Houston and 4 km from Imperial's Huckleberry mine (on care and maintenance since 2016). The June 2026 PFS (Ausenco / MMTS) sized a 120 ktpd open pit over 28 years: initial capex C$4.68B (incl. C$574M contingency), sustaining C$1.73B, after-tax NPV8% C$4.59B / IRR 24% / payback 2.9 yrs at US$4.75 Cu, US$20 Mo, US$45 Ag, US$3,500 Au; at the June spot deck (US$6.45 Cu, US$30 Mo) C$9.4B / 36%. Years 1–5 average 270 Mlb Cu + 21 Mlb Mo + 4 Moz Ag (416 Mlb CuEq) off a supergene cap; LOM 176 Mlb Cu (308 Mlb CuEq); C1 US$1.95/lb CuEq co-product, strip 2.0:1, revenue 57% Cu / 30% Mo. Reserve P&P 1.21 Bt @ 0.22% Cu (5.8 Blb Cu, 687 Mlb Mo). The 2023 PEA was C$2.0B capex / C$2.1B NPV / 20% IRR — the PFS doubled both the plant and the value.

The Ootsa property (Seel, Ox; M&I 439 Mt @ 0.18% Cu, 2022) sits next to Huckleberry and is not in the Berg plan. Infrastructure: a new 230 kV line to BC Hydro's Telkwa substation, road from Houston — no reliance on Huckleberry or Rio Tinto's Kemano. Permitting: BC Critical Minerals Office acceptance (Feb 2026); IPD accepted by the BC EAO and IAAC on 16 Sep 2026; six Nations engaged (Wet'suwet'en hereditary chiefs via the Office of the Wet'suwet'en, Witset, Wet'suwet'en FN, Nee Tahi Buhn, Skin Tyee, Cheslatta) with supportive quotes and a Wet'suwet'en-led parallel assessment in design. Money: C$20M raised at C$0.50 in Feb–Apr 2026 (units with a C$1.00 warrant), C$4M of it from African Rainbow Minerals, which holds ~19.9%; Centerra Gold ~8.5% from its lapsed 2021 option. Cash ~C$21M, no debt.

CEO Leif Nilsson (ex-Macquarie banker, since 2021), President/QP Shane Ebert, VP Projects Mark Wheeler (ex-Thompson Creek at Berg); board rebuilt in Sep 2026 for permitting and M&A — Tony Scott (Artemis), Nalaine Morin (Skeena, BC Hydro, ex-Tahltan), David Farrell (Fortuna). At C$0.51 (30 Sep) the market cap is ~C$198M / US$145M: 0.043× PFS NAV, ~US$0.01/lb CuEq on M&I. The stock is up ~3× in a year and −40% from the June high; thin — 70k–960k shares a day.

The Gate

A major or strategic partner has to underwrite Berg — C$4.68B of initial capex against a ~C$200M market cap means Surge cannot build it; value is realised in a transaction, not in production.

The June PFS more than doubled the NAV and the market gave it back within three months: the stock is −40% from the PFS-day high. The number the market is pricing is not the NPV, it is the ratio of capex to market cap. Everything on this card is about whether someone with C$5B wants a 28-year, 0.22% Cu, 30%-Mo asset in a BC EA — and when.

Sub-gates
  1. The EA: IPD accepted by BC EAO and IAAC on 16 Sep 2026; Early Engagement (BC) and Planning (federal) now; federal substitution to BC being sought. Watch the Wet'suwet'en-led assessment framework — hereditary and elected governance in the same Yintah as the Coastal GasLink conflict.
  2. Feasibility work: 2026 program is geotech, ARD, hydrogeology and condemnation (6,330 m), not discovery — the capex and payback have to survive it.
  3. Metal deck: Cu ≥ US$4.75 and Mo ≥ US$20; by-product C1 is negative (−US$0.17/lb Cu) only because Mo and Ag pay for it.
  4. A partner before the money runs out: ~C$21M cash, C$12–18M/yr burn → a raise in 2027 unless ARM or a second strategic moves first; a full FS alone is C$30–50M.
  5. Royalties: Royal Gold 1% on eight core claims, vendor 3.5% on the optioned west claims — keep them from compounding in a financing.

Valuation Anchor

~US$0.011/lb CuEq across Berg M&I (EV ~US$129M ÷ ~12 Blb CuEq), ~US$0.02/lb on copper alone, and 0.043× the PFS NAV — among the cheapest pounds in the file, with the reason printed next to it: capex is ~24× the market cap and the reserve grade is 0.22%. A developer multiple of 0.3–0.5× NAV does not apply to a company that cannot fund its own feasibility study; the right anchor is what a major pays for a large, low-grade, long-life BC porphyry it will build on its own balance sheet — historically 0.1–0.25× NAV, or ~US$0.02–0.05/lb CuEq — which on the base deck is roughly C$0.5–1.1B, 2–5× today, before the 2027 dilution.

Read it against the peers: Los Andes at 0.12× NAV has reserves, a PFS and a permit binary; Western at ~0.3× stale NAV has an FS, five years of cash and two strategics; Surge has reserves, a PFS, an EA that has just started, 12–18 months of cash and one 19.9% holder who calls itself an investor. The discount is deeper because the dependence is total. What it has that the others don't is a Mo credit worth 30% of revenue and a BC government putting it in federal dealbooks.

Bucket: cheap defined pounds — the extreme end: defined, reserve-backed, and unbuildable by the owner.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
Insiders ~9%, mostly legacy: former chair Patrick Glazier ~10.2M (2.6%, left the board at the 29 Sep AGM); CEO Leif Nilsson ~6.4M (1.65%). Board after the AGM: chair Christian Kargl-Simard (ex-Adventus, sold to Silvercorp 2024), Nilsson, Ebert, Colterjohn, West-Sells, and the three new: Tony Scott (Artemis, ex-Gatos corp dev), Nalaine Morin (Skeena, BC Hydro director, ex-Tahltan lands), David Farrell (Fortuna, ex-Endeavour Financial M&A).
Insider activity (12 mo)
Sellers, no buyers. Kargl-Simard sold 200,000 at ~C$0.63 (Jan 2026); Ebert sold 100,000 at C$0.59 and 60,000 at C$0.61 on 19 Jun — four days after the PFS — plus ~26,500 on 22 Jun (third-party SEDI summaries). Mark Wheeler's Sep 2026 entries show implausible prices (C$100+) — an RSU/data artefact, not relied on. ARM bought 7.96M units at C$0.50 (C$3.98M) on 27 Apr 2026 as a related party. No open-market insider buying found.
Strategic & prominent
African Rainbow Minerals (Motsepe) ~76.7M shares / ~19.9% — in at C$0.175 (Aug 2025) and C$0.50 (Apr 2026) with participation rights under a May 2024 agreement, capped at 19.9%, 'for investment purposes'. Centerra Gold ~33M / 8.5%, passive, from the 2021 Berg option. A shareholder rights plan with a 20% trigger (May 2026) fences ARM where it is and forces any suitor to bid for all. Konwave ~2.3%.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~2%; corporate holders ~28%; retail ~60%. ~389M shares; 40M warrants at C$1.00 (accelerate at a C$1.50 VWAP), 17.6M RSUs, 16.7M DSUs → FD ~464M.

Read: The register is built for a negotiated transaction, not a hostile one: two corporates at 28% and a 20% rights plan. ARM has been a disciplined price-taker (C$0.175 → C$0.50) and can be the acquirer or the blocker. Management owns a few percent, largely legacy, and the people closest to the PFS sold into its pop — that is the yellow flag on near-term conviction, and it sits beside a board that was just rebuilt for exactly the transaction the thesis needs.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Canada / BC, Tier-1, with a slow clock. BC major-mine permitting typically runs 5–8 years from Initial Project Description to a Mines Act permit. Berg's IPD was accepted by the BC EAO and IAAC on 16 Sep 2026 — Early Engagement (BC) and Planning (federal) phases now, with Surge seeking substitution so BC runs a single process. The BC Critical Minerals Office accepted the project in Feb 2026; Premier Eby and the mines minister were quoted in the PFS release; the federal Canada Investment Summit put it in its Dealbook (Sep 2026). Infrastructure: 116 km of forest service road from Houston plus 17 km new, and a new 230 kV line to the Telkwa substation — no dependence on Huckleberry's line or Rio Tinto's Kemano.

Local: the Wet'suwet'en Yintah. The project sits in the territory where the Coastal GasLink conflict played out between hereditary and elected governance. Engagement is formal and, so far, supportive — the Office of the Wet'suwet'en (Chief Casbit, Gilseyhu Clan) and Cheslatta's Chief Whitford are quoted; six Nations are named (Wet'suwet'en hereditary chiefs, Witset, Wet'suwet'en FN, Nee Tahi Buhn, Skin Tyee, Cheslatta); a Wet'suwet'en-led assessment grounded in hereditary governance is being designed to run alongside the EA. That is the right structure and also the structural risk: there is no precedent for it at this scale, and BC's DRIPA consent standard gives it weight. Surge hired a VP Environment & Regulatory (Jan 2026), an ex-Rio Tinto Indigenous-relations manager (Aug 2026) and put an ex-Tahltan lands director on the board (Sep 2026) for this layer specifically.

District: Imperial Metals drilled 7,047 m at Huckleberry in 2026 and is costing a restart (plan due Dec 2026) — a reopening would validate the Tahtsa Ranges and could give Ootsa a mill.

Differentiator

Scale and a molybdenum credit no one else in this file has. 5.8 Blb of copper reserves plus 687 Mlb of Mo — one of the largest undeveloped Cu-Mo porphyries in Canada — and by-products that make the C1 cost negative on a copper-only basis.

  1. Infrastructure solved on paper — grid hydro via a new 230 kV line, road from Houston, no third-party dependency.
  2. A government that wants it — Critical Minerals Office acceptance, a Premier's quote, a federal Dealbook slot, and an IPD accepted within a week of filing.
  3. A defined negotiating structure — ARM at 19.9% with participation rights, Centerra at 8.5%, a 20% rights plan: any transaction is a negotiation, not a raid.
  4. A board built for the exit — Artemis, Skeena/BC Hydro and Fortuna/Endeavour directors added in one AGM.

Counterweight: 0.22% Cu and C$4.68B put Berg in the back half of any major's build queue; the Wet'suwet'en hereditary-governance process has no precedent at this scale; the directors sold into the PFS and nobody inside bought; Ootsa is stranded unless Huckleberry restarts; and the thin register means the stock trades on sentiment between releases. The differentiators are things a buyer values; the counterweights are why the buyer can wait.

Exploration upside

Already defined — moves the needle: low. 2.4 Bt of M&I plus Inferred is the resource; the 2026 program (6,330 m) is geotechnical, ARD, hydrogeological and condemnation drilling for the EA and the FS, not discovery. ~202 Mt of Inferred inside the pit shell is treated as waste and could convert; Ootsa (Seel/Ox) is a modest add with no mill. Nothing a drill rig does here changes the valuation — a partner and a permit do.

Next Catalyst

Q4 2026: field-program results (geotech, ARD, hydro), the EA Early Engagement / federal-substitution decision, and Imperial's Huckleberry reopening plan (Dec) as the district read-across; H1 2027: Wet'suwet'en assessment framework, EA Process Planning, FS scoping; 2027: a raise (12–18 months of cash) or a strategic process — the real catalyst, undated; 2028–29: feasibility study; 2029: C$1.00 warrants expire; EA certificate realistically 2029–31; production not before ~2034.

  • Will IAAC agree to a BC-led single assessment, and what decision-making weight does the Wet'suwet'en-led assessment carry?

  • Is there a toll-milling or consolidation conversation with Imperial ahead of its December Huckleberry decision?

15 Oct 2026 update

The IAAC/EAO public notice of 8 Oct starts the clock on Berg's Initial Project Description: comments to 9 Nov 2026, and a federal decision pending on BC's request to substitute its own process for the federal one. A substitution would simplify the path; a refusal means two assessments. Odds unchanged.

3 Oct 2026 refresh

2 Oct AGM results (housekeeping). Field results and the EA / federal-substitution decision are still pending.

EA formally started (16 Sep 2026)

IPD submitted 9 Sep, accepted by the BC EAO and IAAC within a week; BC Early Engagement and federal Planning phases underway; substitution to BC being explored; Wet'suwet'en-led assessment in development; all six Nations named; Chief Casbit quoted.

Board rebuilt for permitting and M&A (Jul–Sep 2026)

Tony Scott (Artemis, ex-Gatos corp dev), Nalaine Morin (Skeena, BC Hydro director, ex-Tahltan) and David Farrell (Fortuna, ex-Endeavour Financial) in; Glazier, Pettit and Dorward out at the 29 Sep AGM. Aman Parhar (ex-Rio Tinto) hired for Indigenous relations in August.

PFS more than doubled the NAV (15 Jun 2026)

After-tax NPV8% C$4.59B / 24% IRR / 2.9-yr payback at US$4.75 Cu — vs the Jun 2023 PEA's C$2.1B / 20%; plant 120 ktpd vs 32.4 Mtpa; capex C$4.68B vs C$2.0B; LOM Cu +32% to 4.9 Blb, Mo +50% to 602 Mlb; maiden reserve 1.2 Bt @ 0.22% Cu. Spot case C$9.4B / 36%. Stock spiked to C$0.83 and has since halved the gain.

C$20M at C$0.50 and a rights plan (Feb–May 2026)

32.04M units on 26 Feb (C$16M) + 7.96M units to ARM on 27 Apr (C$3.98M); each unit a share plus a three-year C$1.00 warrant (acceleration at C$1.50). ARM at ~19.9%; a shareholder rights plan with a 20% trigger adopted 29 May.

District: Huckleberry reopening plan due Dec 2026

Imperial Metals drilled 7,047 m at Huckleberry in 2026 (e.g. 240 m @ 0.29% Cu) and is costing a restart of the mine 4 km from Ootsa.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

PFS delivered on time, ARM as funder, clean disclosure; a first-time CEO and a chair who sold rather than built. Skin re-scored 2 → 1 on 16 Oct (quality review): the card's sellers-no-buyers reading is right; the "net buying" in the earlier source was option exercises.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Leif Nilsson (CEO, Director, since 2021-01): Ex-investment banker (Macquarie, Stifel, CIBC); ex-director Adventus Mining (sold to Silvercorp ~C$200M 2024). First CEO job. · Christian Kargl-Simard (Chairman (non-exec), since 2021-09): Age 41. CEO of Adventus Mining through its 2024 sale to Silvercorp. Net seller of Surge stock (C$72k) in past 12 months. · Mark Wheeler (VP Projects, since 2021-12): Ran the PFS; prior background (Teck/large-project engineering) unverified. · Paul West-Sells (Director, since 2026-01): Ex-CEO Western Copper and Gold (Casino) - adds BC/Yukon porphyry permitting experience.
Track record
  • Nilsson: no prior CEO or mine-building role; banking career then Adventus board (Curipamba, Ecuador - sold before construction)source
  • Kargl-Simard: built Adventus from exploration to permitted Curipamba project and sold to Silvercorp for ~C$200M in 2024 - a developer exit in a copper up-cyclesource
  • Surge under Nilsson: Berg PEA 2023, PFS delivered June 15 2026 (after-tax NPV8 C$4.6B, 24% IRR), EA process started Sept 2026source
  • Financing: African Rainbow Minerals strategic placements 2024-2026 to 19.9%; Centerra 8.5% - funded without broker bought dealssource
  • Misses: none found; no sanctions, CTOs or lawsuits found.

Boards today: Nilsson: Surge only (as found). Kargl-Simard: Surge chair plus other roles post-Adventus (unverified count). Board renewal July 2026: Glazier, Pettit, Dorward left.

Fit to this job
Stage match: same as Adventus (develop a copper project to PFS/permits, then sell or partner) - yes for the chair, first time as CEO for Nilsson. Deposit/mining: large low-grade BC porphyry (open pit, 28-year life, multi-billion capex) - neither has built one; the PFS and EA are consultant-led. Jurisdiction: BC EA with First Nations (Ootsa/Berg) - new to the executives; West-Sells (Casino) brings relevant northern permitting experience. ARM (South African producer) as 19.9% holder is the likely builder/buyer.
Skin & pay
1/5 — net sellers while promoting: the only 12-month insider trades on the open market are sales, including one four days after the PFS. CEO Nilsson 1.65% (~C$3.6M), built largely via options; on the open market the 12-month record is sellers, no buyers — chair Kargl-Simard sold 200k at ~C$0.63 (Jan 2026), Ebert ~186k at C$0.59–0.61 four days after the PFS (SEDI); the Simply Wall St "net buying C$286k" is option exercises, not open-market purchases. ARM 19.8%, Centerra 8.5% are corporate blocks, not skin

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Chair sold C$72k of stock on-market in past year while promoting the PFS.
  • CEO's stake is mostly options (exercised 500k at $0.42 June 2026); ownership 1.65%.
  • Nobody on the executive team has built or operated a mine.

Thesis

One of the largest undeveloped porphyry copper projects in the Americas, at low elevation with a port, highway, rail, grid power and gas nearby — trading at under a tenth of attributable PEA NPV.

The Gate

Permitting a new open-pit mine in Mexico. Sheinbaum withdrew AMLO's proposed open-pit ban but has said no new mining concessions will be granted and that open-pit projects face stricter, case-by-case environmental scrutiny; the 2023 mining law shortened concessions and tightened water permits. Santo Tomás sits on existing concessions and is part of Plan Sinaloa (a regional hub of Plan México), and federal and state officials have publicly backed it — but its environmental approval is untested under this regime. Secondary: US$1.1B capex against a ~US$120M market cap. PFS now targeted Q2/Q3 2027 (Phase 2 drilling is converting South Zone Inferred to Indicated and collecting PFS-level geotech, hydro and metallurgy data). New CEO Charles Cryer (capital-markets background, effective Jun 16, 2026) — the company frames his appointment as a shift toward a transaction-based objective for Santo Tomás. Land package rationalised to ~6,121 ha.

Payable copper over life of mine ~4.77 Blb; 0.51% CuEq in the first seven years from near-surface higher-grade material. Staged 60,000 → 120,000 t/d open pit; C1 ~US$1.54/lb (by-product).
NPV : capex1.34x@ PEA deck. IRR 22.2%. Payback 3.8 yr.The highest NPV-to-capex ratio in the file at study deck — still short of Rick Rule's 2–3×, and the IRR is below his 25–30%.
Valuation Anchor

~0.07× attributable NAV (US$96M at 15 Oct 2026 vs ~US$1.29B) and ~2.3¢/lb on attributable payable copper — as deep a discount as Los Andes, for a mirror-image reason: Los Andes' risk is a local campaign in a pro-mining country; Oroco's is national policy with local support.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~11% — Executive Chairman Craig Dalziel ~5.4%, director Faysal Rodriguez ~1.5% (bought C$1.4M of units Nov 2025), Ian Graham ~0.3%; new CEO Charles Cryer holds options only. Institutions <1% despite the C$23M Canaccord bought deal (Jan 2026; no named participants).

Read: Moderate — the chairman has real exposure; the new CEO has none yet, and there is essentially no institutional register.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the sharpest policy risk in the file — no new concessions, open-pit scrutiny, shorter concession terms, water-permit tightening, and judicial reform adding uncertainty. Local: supportive per the company — the local community and Sinaloa's state government back the project. Sinaloa also carries state-level security risk.

Unlike Los Andes and Copper Giant, the gate here is national policy rather than a local campaign.

Differentiator

Scale, infrastructure and capital efficiency at the deepest discount in the file. ~170 km to the Topolobampo deep-water port; highway, rail, trunk power and gas along the corridor; low elevation; a front-loaded 0.51% CuEq starter phase; NPV/capex 1.34× — the best in the file. Neighbour: Jinchuan's Bahuerachi, ~14 km away. The discount is Mexico, not the rock.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, mostly conversion with some better tonnes · moves the needle: medium. Phase 2 infill in the South Zone is upgrading resource classification (e.g. 26.48 m @ 1.18% CuEq, Aug 2026); the Brasiles zone and surrounding 80%-owned concessions add district optionality.

Next Catalyst

Phase 2 assays (fifth South Zone batch 8 Oct 2026; resource drilling complete); updated MRE targeted Q1 2027; PFS Q2/Q3 2027 (card estimate; the company gives no PFS date); a transaction (sale or partner) is the stated objective; Mexican environmental permitting after that — probably at or beyond the horizon.

Open Questions
  • Would Mexico permit a new open-pit copper mine of this size under current policy — and on what timeline?
  • Who partners or funds US$1.1B?
  • Does the PFS hold the PEA's capital efficiency?
  • Who buys or partners, now that the stated objective is a transaction?

Management review

The mine-builder CEO quit mid-PFS and a banker replaced him; a US$1.1B build with undated next steps, insider selling and a financier chair. Skin re-scored 1 → 3 on 16 Oct (quality review): the earlier "n/a" ignored the ~11% insider holding.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 28% → 23%, odds of a 3× 18% → 15%.

People
Charles (Charlie) Cryer (CEO, since 16 Jun 2026): 30 yrs capital markets (RFC Ambrian Head of London, Nomura, BofA Merrill); mining engineering degree; early field roles at Schlumberger and WMC. No prior CEO role; no mine-building record. · Craig Dalziel (Executive Chairman, since Founder (via ATM Mining)): 35 yrs finance; founded Sunda Mining (became Southern Arc Minerals). Oroco's long-time controlling figure through the Santo Tomas title fight. · Ian Graham (President, since n/a): Ex-Rio Tinto Chief Geologist Project Generation (Resolution Copper, Diavik), Anglo American. · Richard Lock (Former CEO (Apr 2022 - 30 Apr 2026), since resigned): Mine builder (ex-Rio Tinto/Oyu Tolgoi, Rosemont per general knowledge); left for 'personal reasons' mid-PFS, 2-month CEO gap.
Track record
  • Dalziel: Southern Arc Minerals (Indonesia) - no mine, no sale of note; Oroco spent roughly a decade in Mexican title litigation over Santo Tomas before consolidating it (general knowledge; litigation history not re-fetched)source
  • Under Lock (2022-26): Phase 1 drilling, 2024 MRE, PEA Aug 2024 (US$1.1B capex, US$1.48B post-tax NPV8, 22.2% IRR at US$4.00 Cu), SEMARNAT informe preventivo positive Aug 2025; then Lock resigned Apr 2026source

Boards today: Cryer: Oroco only (verified none other). Dalziel: Oroco exec chair; others not verified.

Fit to this job
Stage: developer with PEA moving to PFS on a US$1.1B-capex open-pit porphyry in Sinaloa. Team fit is thin: the chairman is a financier who spent years on title, the new CEO is a capital-markets banker, and the only builder (Lock) has left; consulting engineers (Thornton, ex-Gammon Ocampo) supply the construction experience. Region: Mexico - yes (Rodriguez ex-Torex Mexico on board). New for them: PFS, permitting, and financing a billion-dollar build.

3/5 — meaningful stake (~11% held by insiders, incl. a ~C$1.4M director buy in Nov 2025); no sales found. Insiders ~11%: Exec Chairman Dalziel ~5.4%; director Rodriguez bought ~C$1.4M of units Nov 2025; no sales found

Thesis

The nearest North American analogue to Hot Chili — a fully permitted, feasibility-stage copper project trading at ~0.5× a stale-deck NPV and ~0.09× at today's ~US$6.5 copper, where the gate is a financing transaction rather than a permit or a discovery. Add a US$250M EXIM letter of interest, a US$50M Michigan grant and White House acknowledgement, and the US critical-minerals machinery is pointed at it.

The remaining equity slice, ~US$100–125M, is larger than the company — Orion (28%) and Condire (20%) will set the terms. Timeline has slipped ~12 months: construction decision H2 2027 (was YE 2026), first production H2 2030 (was 2029).

Risk score3/5The only fully permitted, feasibility-stage project in the file besides Marimaca and Ivanhoe, debt-free with ~US$20M cash — but it is a single, small, 10-year asset whose equity gap exceeds its market cap, whose timeline has just slipped a year, and whose state grant is being litigated.
Market cap2 Oct 2026: ~US$78M (C$0.15 · ~C$111M on 738.2M shares). ~US$88M (Sep 2026; ~C$122M at C$0.165 on 738M shares, Sep 25). Cash ~US$24M pro forma after the Mar 2026 White Pine sale (US$30M, US$18M net), now likely high-teens (est.); no debt; no equity issued in 2026. The Dec 2025 accounts carried going-concern language — resolved by the sale, not by a raise.
Capex / IRRInitial capex US$425M gross (US$391M net of pre-production revenue); after-tax IRR 17.6% @ US$4.02/lb (33.4% @ US$5.00/lb; 47.6% @ US$6.00/lb). Mar 2023 FS (G Mining). Payback 3.5 yr (2.0 yr @ $5). Updated FS due H1 2027 at a ~US$4.80/lb planning price, with ore sorting, a lower cut-off and a simplified plant under study.
NPVAfter-tax NPV US$168M @ US$4.02/lb (US$507M @ US$5.00/lb; US$855M @ US$6.00/lb). 2023 FS, 8% discount.
DepositP&P 25.7 Mt @ 1.45% Cu, 3.9 g/t Ag — 820 Mlb Cu, 3.2 Moz AgM&I 54.2 Mt @ 1.49% Cu (1.78 Blb), Inferred 79.1 Mt @ 1.09% Cu (1.9 Blb). Sediment-hosted, flat-lying, room-and-pillar underground at ~6,800 tpd; ~29 kt/yr (64.6 Mlb) payable Cu; C1 US$1.68/lb years 1–5, US$1.99/lb LOM. White Pine North (the larger neighbour) is now 100% Kinterra — gone from the story.
NPV : capex0.40x@ base US$4.02/lb → 1.19× @ US$5.00 → 2.0× @ US$6.00. IRR 17.6% base / 33% @ $5. Payback 3.5 yr.Fails Rule at base by the widest margin in the file; passes both tests only from ~US$5.50 copper. The 2027 FS at US$4.80 is what re-bases this.
Valuation Anchor

~0.52× NAV at the 2023 deck (US$4.02), ~0.17× at US$5.00, ~0.10× at US$6.00, ~0.09× at today's ~US$6.5. On reserve pounds it is not cheap — EV ~US$68M / 820 Mlb ≈ 8¢/lb, more than Los Andes (2.9¢) — because the grade is four times higher; per unit of NPV it is among the cheapest permitted assets anywhere. Market cap is ~0.21× capex — the dilution to build is the whole story of the multiple.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~0.3% (~US$0.2M; Simply Wall St, 2026) — CEO Barry O'Shea has bought on-market steadily through 2025 at C$0.08–0.13, and Chair Stephen Hicks and director Iain Farmer bought in Nov–Dec 2025, but the amounts are small. Register: Orion Mine Finance ~28%, Condire Investors ~20% (added in 2026), OR Royalties ~6% (also holds a 1.5% Cu / 11.5% Ag NSR); Greenstone sold its entire 16% in a block at C$0.125 (Nov 2025). New project director Trace Arlaud (ex-Rio Tinto Resolution GM, Apr 2026).

Read: Weak on management ownership; the alignment that matters is Orion's, because Orion's cheque decides the equity terms.

Jurisdiction risk

National: strong — United States, copper on the critical-minerals list, EXIM and White House engagement. Local: moderate and active. Private land, seven state permits in hand and in good standing, unanimous support resolutions from Ironwood, Wakefield, Erwin and Gogebic County. Against that, Protect the Porkies — the project abuts the Porcupine Mountains Wilderness and sits near Lake Superior — filed an appeal in Ingham County Circuit Court (Sep 15, 2026) against the grant, arguing the funds were reallocated without legislative approval; a former Strategic Fund board member publicly agrees.

The permits themselves are not the target; the money is.

Differentiator

Permits done, high grade, and a sovereign lender at the table — at a microcap price. 1.45% Cu reserve grade is four times the porphyry names here; every state permit is issued; and EXIM's US$250M LOI makes it, with Ivanhoe, one of only two names in the file with US government financing in view. Unlike Ivanhoe, none of that is in the price yet.

Read honestly: it is a small, 10-year mine — the prize is a few hundred million of NAV, not a district — and the market has watched this project miss timelines for a decade.

Exploration upside

Conversion, not discovery · moves the needle: low–medium. The deposit is open along strike and down-dip; ~1.9 Blb Inferred sits outside the reserve, including satellite zones that the ore-sorting and lower cut-off work (US$4.80/lb) could pull into the 2027 mine plan. No greenfield story — this is a mine-life question.

Next Catalyst

Ingham County ruling on the grant appeal (undated, likely months); MEDC definitive grant agreement; DoD/DOE decision; FY results ~Oct 2026; updated FS H1 2027 → EXIM binding facility → construction decision H2 2027 → construction 2028 → first copper H2 2030.

Open Questions
  • What does the H1 2027 FS show at US$4.80 — capex, mine life, NPV?
  • Does the Ingham County appeal delay or kill the grant, and does it matter to EXIM?
  • Who provides the ~US$100–125M of equity, at what price, and does Orion lead?
  • Does a stream or offtake (Orion, Glencore assessed) replace part of the equity?
  • Does DoD award anything?

Track record
  • O'Shea: Fiore Gold CFO - Pan mine bought from bankruptcy, restarted, sold to Calibre Mining (2021) - a small heap-leach restart, the one build-adjacent winsource
  • Copperwood: fully permitted since 2018 FS era; construction never started under three management teams; Highland pitched the US$425M project to Michigan in 2023source
  • Jan 2024: Michigan Strategic Fund postponed grant vote after the CEO admitted the company lacked investors and capitalsource
  • 2025 delivered: US EXIM US$250M letter of interest (~60% of capex), FEED contracts to DRA, White Pine divestment, Greenstone (16%) exited via block tradesource
  • Aug 2026: Michigan US$50M grant finally approved (7-2) after three years; opponents sued Sept 2026 to block itsource

Boards today: O'Shea: Highland only (as found). Hemstead: Fireweed Metals, Sanu Gold boards plus interim CFO here. Directors Jon Cherry (Perpetua CEO) and Melanie Miller sit on the technical committee.

Fit to this job
Stage: builder-in-waiting with permits in hand - the team has never taken a construction decision; O'Shea's only build-adjacent experience is a Nevada heap-leach restart as CFO. Deposit/mining: underground room-and-pillar (now drift-and-fill under review) sediment-hosted copper with a flotation plant - Arlaud (Resolution, Eagle Mine) is the first person on the team who has run a US underground copper build. Jurisdiction: Michigan UP - Arlaud and the Eagle Mine link fit; but the project has drawn organised opposition, lawsuits over the grant, and a Lake Superior narrative the team has not neutralised in three years.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. Insider ownership 0.3% (~US$233k) - essentially nil; no notable open-market buying found. CEO total pay US$447k (FY to June 2025), 57% salary - modest for the role and proportionate to a ~US$80M company. Orion Mine Finance ~28% (as of mid-2025), Greenstone exited 2025.source

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Construction decision has moved from H1 2026 to 2027, construction start to 2028, within 14 months - and this is the third management team unable to start a permitted mine.
  • Both the project director and the CFO changed in early 2026.
  • 738M shares outstanding; market cap ~US$80M vs ~US$425M+ capex (capex now likely higher at a 2027 FS) - the equity cannot fund even the EXIM equity requirement.
  • Michigan grant under litigation; sustained local opposition.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was US$20.8M at 31 March 2026 after selling the last 34% of White Pine North; at about US$2.1M a quarter that is roughly 2.5 years.
  2. Spending is mostly Copperwood engineering and permitting, US$4.1M in nine months, with lean overhead of US$0.4-0.8M a quarter.
  3. No equity raised since 2023; shares have stayed at about 737M for three years.
  4. The US$30.1M White Pine sale repaid the US$11.7M Kinterra loan, so Highland is now debt-free after a going-concern note in December 2025.
  5. The US$50M Michigan grant depends on securing US$150M of project financing by 31 March 2028; the FY2026 audited accounts are not yet published.

Thesis

A funded portfolio of shots on goal rather than one advancing story. Spinout of Vizsla Silver (Inventa Capital stable; Craig Parry exec chair/CEO; ex-Cantor CEO Shawn Matthews as strategic advisor). BC porphyries — Woodjam (flagship, ~90,000 ha, Quesnel Terrane near Mount Polley), Poplar (Thira discovery: 435 m @ 0.49% CuEq, 237 m @ 0.51%), Copperview, Redgold — plus the Palmer Cu-Zn VMS in Alaska acquired early 2026 (US$13.7M 2026 budget; Alaska governor letter of support). C$44M private placement closed alongside Palmer → well funded.

The Gate

Prove a compliant, economic resource at one target. Woodjam carries only a historical, non-NI-43-101 inferred estimate (~1.7 Blb Cu + ~968 koz Au) that cannot be leaned on. Sub-risk is diffusion — capital spread across 5+ early properties in two jurisdictions with no single flagship being driven to a maiden resource. Inventa is a promotion/deal machine — read the narrative with appropriate skepticism.

Valuation Anchor

~4¢/lb CuEq on Palmer's ~1.2 Blb CuEq resource (EV ~US$50M: US$66M cap less ~US$16M cash, 15 Oct 2026) — but Palmer is partly zinc and too small to carry the company, and the BC porphyries have no compliant pounds. Small-cap ~C$93M (C$1.04, ~90M shares; 52-wk C$0.75–2.68; cash C$22.5M at 31 Jul → ~C$70M EV). Same bucket as Gladiator/Atex but earlier and more scattered than Gladiator, which at least has one target in systematic delineation. Recent price ran ~25% off the June low into results — a "sell the news" pullback is the classic pattern, not a verdict on the holes. Verify live.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~7.4% — CEO/Chair Craig Parry ~6.1% (bought 2.0M sh at C$1.24 Dec 2025; further director buys Dec 2025–Jan 2026). Largest holder: American Pacific Mining ~15.4% (vendor of Palmer). Inventa Capital: incubator/backer, no disclosed %. Institutions ~5%.

Read: Meaningful — the CEO is the largest individual holder and paid cash for it; the rest of the board is small.

Jurisdiction risk

National: excellent — BC (Quesnel Terrane) and Alaska; letter of support from Alaska's governor for Palmer. Local: moderate and diffuse — BC First Nations consultation is substantive and slow, and Mount Polley's 2014 tailings failure shapes regional sentiment in the Woodjam area.

Spread across two jurisdictions, so no single licence decision is terminal.

Differentiator

Optionality breadth — five-plus independent shots on goal, fully funded, in two tier-one jurisdictions. Every other explorer here is a single-asset bet where a bad maiden resource is terminal; Vizsla can fail at Poplar and still re-rate on Palmer or Deerhorn. Second: asset diversity of type — a Cu-Zn VMS in Alaska alongside BC porphyries and a gold-rich Deerhorn zone, so it isn't a single geological wager. Third: the Inventa/Vizsla machine — a group with a demonstrated record of financing, promoting and monetising juniors, with a C$44M placement and government-level Alaskan support already secured.

Read it honestly, though: breadth is the differentiator and diffusion is the gate — the same fact seen from two sides. Optionality only pays if one target is actually driven to a compliant resource.

Exploration upside

High-grade hits, not yet systematic · moves the needle: high if one target is stepped out. Palmer VMS 49.2 m @ 4.7% CuEq; Deerhorn 48.5 m @ 3.32% Cu; Thira (Poplar) 435 m @ 0.49% CuEq. Still closer to 'finding good holes' than extending a defined body.

Next Catalyst

Palmer 2026 drill results; Deerhorn/Woodjam follow-up; any first compliant resource.

Open Questions
  • Which target gets pushed to a maiden resource — Palmer VMS or Deerhorn?
  • Does the Woodjam historical resource get modernised?
  • Is the Alaska pivot strategy or distraction?
