Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

Parry's wins are real but in uranium as a founder-financier; chair-and-CEO plus Skeena and Vizsla Silver roles is overcommitted. Delivered what it announced so far.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Craig Parry (Chair & CEO, since CEO 2024-05 (chair earlier)): Co-founder Inventa Capital; chairman Skeena Resources; founder/ex-CEO IsoEnergy; founding director NexGen Energy; 10 yrs Rio Tinto. · Steve Blower (SVP Exploration, since unverified): Ex-VP Exploration Denison and IsoEnergy; ex-mine geologist Huckleberry and Similco (BC copper). · Peter Mercer (SVP Exploration, Alaska (Palmer), since 2025-26): 20 yrs; permitting/JV governance background. · Simon Cmrlec (Director, since unverified): COO Vizsla Silver, ex-COO Ausenco — the only builder in the group.
Track record
  • Hits (uranium cycle 2016-2024): founding director of NexGen (Arrow, multi-billion valuation); founded IsoEnergy (Hurricane discovery; merged with Consolidated Uranium 2023 — outcome details unverified)source
  • In progress: chairman of Skeena (Eskay Creek build) and executive at Vizsla Silver (Panuco) — neither yet in production; Inventa Capital group has raised >C$800M since 2017source
  • Vizsla Copper: Thira Cu-Mo discovery at Poplar Jul 2025 (345 m @ 0.43% CuEq); Palmer VMS acquired Dec 2025 with C$44M placement (upsized from C$25M) and a share consolidation; 2026 Palmer drilling 49.2 m @ 4.7% CuEq; Sep 2026 deal to buy Delta and Helm Bay from Agnicosource
  • Parry holds ~6.1% of VCUsource

Boards today: Parry: chair & CEO Vizsla Copper, chairman Skeena Resources, chairman Inventa Capital (private), roles at Vizsla Silver/EMR advisory — at least 2 public chair roles plus a CEO seat. Director Donaldson: CEO Outback Goldfields, exec chair TinOne. Konnert (advisor/director): CEO Vizsla Silver, exec chair Vizsla Royalties.

Fit to this job
Explorer/asset aggregator in BC and Alaska; Blower's BC copper mine geology and Parry's capital-markets reach fit a discovery-and-financing strategy. Palmer is a VMS project with a long permitting history under prior owners — new ground for this team in Alaska. No executive has built a mine; Parry runs several companies at once, and the rapid acquisition cadence (Palmer, Delta, Helm Bay, Miller in 10 months) is a portfolio play rather than one project advanced.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Parry ~6.1% (C$6.8M) — how acquired (market vs placements) not verified; CEO comp ~C$340k (88% salary). No recent open-market buying/selling found. 2026 circular not retrieved. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-vcu/vizsla-copper-shares/management

Thesis

A district-scale copper-gold skarn–porphyry land package in the Las Bambas belt, run by a proven discovery-and-sale CEO, with Teck on the register and a funded Phase 2 drill programme about to test the high-grade surface skarn at Nioc.

The Gate

Turning surface grade into a drill discovery. Channel samples show copper at surface; only drilling shows continuity at depth. The 2024 drilling at Ccascabamba underwhelmed, so Phase 2 at Nioc and Tipicancha is effectively a second test of the thesis. Drill permit expansion approved Aug 2026; drill contract signed Sep 10, 2026. Sombrero is held under an option (with Aceros Arequipa, extended to 2029), plus concessions optioned in Apr 2026.

Risk score5/5No resource and no drill discovery; the first drill campaign (2024) was weak, and the high grades so far are surface channel samples. It sits in a belt with a long record of community conflict, and funding is modest.
Market cap2 Oct 2026: ~US$55M (C$0.40 · ~C$78M on ~195.9M shares). ~US$60M (~C$81M at ~C$0.42 on ~193M shares, Sep 2026; up ~140% over 12 months). C$5.5M unit raise at C$0.35 in Jun 2026 (warrants at C$0.50) plus ~C$1M strategic financing in Aug 2026.
Capex / IRRNo economic study — no discovery yet.
NPVNo NPV — no resource.
DepositNo resource.Nioc surface channels: 52 m @ 1.06% Cu + 0.19 g/t Au (Sep 2025); 155 m of continuous mineralisation averaging 0.54% Cu (Jan 2026); 70.1 m @ 0.92% Cu + 0.25 g/t Au (May 2026). Ccascabamba first drilling (2024): 7,100 m in 18 holes, broad but low grade (e.g. 21.85 m @ 0.22% Cu). Sombrero covers ~57,000 ha; Tipicancha is a new multi-kilometre target.
NPV : capexn/a — no study.
Valuation Anchor

~US$60M for a district-scale land position, Teck backing and high-grade surface skarn — a lottery ticket with a dated draw. No pounds to value. Same bucket as Kincora and Vizsla; better evidence than Kincora, less diversification than Vizsla.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~4.8% (CEO Ivan Bebek ~3.5%, a repeat small on-market buyer through 2026; director Jeffrey Mason ~1%). Strategic: Teck ~9.9% (topped up in the Aug 2026 placement). Institutions <1%.

Read: Modest stake, consistent buying; Teck's top-up is the real validation.

Jurisdiction risk

National: mixed — Peru has world-class geology and volatile politics. Local: meaningful — the Andahuaylas–Yauri corridor, including Las Bambas, has a long history of community blockades. Coppernico co-invests with communities and government in agricultural programmes (AGROIDEAS) and reports incident-free exploration since inception.

Of the names in this file, this is the one where social licence is most likely to set the pace.

Differentiator

Proven dealmaker, major on the register, and the right belt. Ivan Bebek built and sold Cayden Resources to Agnico Eagle (C$205M); Teck holds 9.9%; the ground sits along trend from Las Bambas, Constancia and Haquira.

Unlike the prospect generators, it keeps its discovery — but it also pays for the drilling itself.

Exploration upside

Surface high-grade, drill-unconfirmed · moves the needle: medium–high if drilling confirms. Channel intercepts approaching 1% Cu over 50–90 m at surface are real evidence of a mineralised skarn. Whether they persist at depth is exactly what Phase 2 tests.

Next Catalyst

Phase 2 drilling (contract signed Sep 10, 2026) — first assays likely late 2026 or early 2027; Tipicancha initial drilling; financing.

Open Questions
  • Do Phase 2 holes at Nioc confirm the surface grades at depth?
  • Does Tipicancha produce a porphyry target worth drilling?
  • How much more dilution does it take to reach a discovery — and does Teck participate?

Track record
  • Bebek: Cayden Resources sold to Agnico Eagle for ~US$205M in 2014 - win (2011-14 cycle)source

Fit to this job
Stage: early explorer, first real drilling - fits the Bebek/Rios background (Peru discovery and promotion). Deposit: Cu-Au skarn/porphyry in Peru; Rios did Peru discoveries at Bear Creek (silver). Region: Peru - yes, with community-permitting that took years. New for them: Bebek has sold a gold explorer but never advanced a copper project; the company's own timeline shows permitting, not geology, has been the constraint.

Thesis

A 100%-owned, multi-zone copper-gold porphyry in BC's Quesnel Terrane with a fresh 2.4 Blb resource bought at ~2¢/lb — run by the team behind Great Bear Resources (sold to Kinross for C$1.8B), with a free option on Arizona through the Teck deal.

The Gate

Proving that 0.24–0.28% copper is economic. That grade sits below Los Andes' reserve (0.36%) and near the bottom of what open-pit porphyries can mine profitably. The PEA, not more drilling, is what answers it. Secondary: most of the resource is Inferred, and future PEA and drilling work will need funding.

Risk score4/5A defined, 100%-owned resource in a tier-one jurisdiction, but it's mostly Inferred and low-grade (0.24–0.28% Cu), with no economic study yet. Whether this grade is economic is an open question, and a small company will need more money to reach a PEA.
Market cap2 Oct 2026: ~US$55M (C$0.70 · ~C$78M on 111.9M shares). ~US$55M (~C$75M on ~99M shares, Sep 2026; verify live). An upsized, oversubscribed LIFE financing (Paradigm-led) closed Jun 25, 2026.
Capex / IRRNo economic study yet — PEA planning under way, likely 2027.
NPVNo NPV — pre-PEA.
DepositIndicated 82.9 Mt @ 0.39% CuEq (0.28% Cu) + Inferred 356.3 Mt @ 0.32% CuEq (0.24% Cu)~2.4 Blb Cu, ~1.7 Moz Au across seven zones (Dec 2025 MRE, pit-constrained, 0.2% CuEq cut-off). Lower cut-off cases give significantly more tonnes.
NPV : capexn/a — no study.
Valuation Anchor

~2.3¢/lb Cu on total resource (~US$55M / 2.4 Blb) — cheap, close to Copper Giant and Aldebaran, and in a better jurisdiction than Copper Giant. The discount is a grade discount, not a mispricing, until a PEA shows the economics.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~3% (SEDI-based tally: CEO Claudia Tornquist ~1.9%, Chairman Chris Taylor ~1.3%; Simply Wall St shows ~1.8%, which appears to omit indirect holdings; both bought open-market 25 Jun 2026 and were expected to take part in the C$13.1M June financing). Funds: Konwave ~6.5%, ALPS, Middlefield. Teck holds no Kodiak equity (it takes ~26.4% of the Kay Copper spin-out, per the 21 Sep release). Discovery Group affiliation through Taylor, no disclosed %.

Read: Modest — small holdings, but the two leaders are buying with their own money.

Jurisdiction risk

National: excellent — BC, Canada, established porphyry mining belt. Local: moderate — BC First Nations consultation is substantive and slow; engagement with Indigenous rightsholders is under way. No organised opposition campaign known.

Differentiator

100% ownership of a defined multi-zone resource at a microcap price, plus a free Arizona option. Unlike the prospect generators, Kodiak keeps the whole discovery. Under the pending Kay Copper transaction, Kodiak's Mohave project and Teck's Copper Hill (both Arizona) go into a new company that Kodiak and Teck would each own ~26.4% of (21 Sep 2026 release), with Teck taking offtake rights. Founder Chris Taylor (Great Bear) and CEO Claudia Tornquist (ex-Rio Tinto).

Read honestly: the low grade is the reason the pounds are cheap.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, mostly more tonnes · moves the needle: medium. The resource is open in multiple directions and at depth across seven zones; near-surface, higher-grade material at West, Adit and South is the "better tonnes" angle. Metallurgical testwork (May 2026) again returned robust recoveries and concentrates. 2026 programme targets expansion ahead of a PEA.

Next Catalyst

2026 drilling (expanded to 16,500 m, two rigs); updated MRE planned Q1 2027; PEA to follow; Kay Copper transaction expected to close in October 2026 (if not closed by 7 Nov 2026 the escrowed financing is returned).

Open Questions
  • Is 0.24–0.28% Cu economic at MPD's scale — and at what copper price?
  • How much Inferred converts?
  • Does the Kay Copper deal close, and at what value to Kodiak?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 4/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 4/5

Chair Chris Taylor (Great Bear, C$1.8B) buys in the market and timelines have been met; the CEO has no exit of her own and three raises in 15 months.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Claudia Tornquist (President & CEO, Director, since Nov 2017 (as CEO of predecessor Dunnedin; Kodiak since 2020 rename)): M.Eng/MBA; ex-GM Rio Tinto copper, EVP Business Development Sandstorm Gold; chaired Kennady Diamonds special committee (C$176M sale to Mountain Province, 2018). Will also become Chair of Kay Copper. · Chris Taylor (Founder & Chairman, since Founder): Ex-CEO Great Bear Resources (sold to Kinross for C$1.8B, 2022). Discovery Group. · Dave Skelton (VP Exploration, since Mar 2025 (on MPD since 2020)): Ex-VP Project Development Stornoway (Renard). · John Robins (Discovery Group founder, advisor, since n/a): Kaminak (sold to Goldcorp C$520M, 2016), Great Bear, Bluestone, Fireweed - not an officer of Kodiak.
Track record
  • Chair Taylor: Great Bear Resources CEO - Dixie discovery, sold to Kinross for C$1.8B in 2022 (2020-22 cycle) - major winsource
  • CEO Tornquist: no prior CEO exit; corporate-development career (Rio Tinto, Sandstorm); at Kodiak since 2017 - took MPD from 2020 Gate discovery to maiden resource (Jun/Dec 2025)source
  • Discovery Group misses: Bluestone Resources (Cerro Blanco, Guatemala) failed to build and was sold cheaply to Aura in 2024 - general knowledge, unverified here
  • Kodiak financings: C$5.5M Mar 2025, C$8M Sep 2025, C$15M Jun 2026 - serial but each funded drilling and delivered stated metressource
  • Teck deal: Mohave (AZ) contributed to Kay Copper NewCo alongside Teck's Copper Hill; Kodiak 26.4%, Teck 26.4%; Tornquist becomes NewCo chair while staying Kodiak CEOsource

Boards today: Tornquist: Kodiak CEO/director, American Lithium director (per bio), incoming Kay Copper chair - 3. Taylor: Kodiak chair plus other Discovery Group boards (count unverified).

Fit to this job
Stage: explorer with maiden resource moving toward PEA - the team has done discovery-to-resource (Great Bear, Kaminak) but in gold; porphyry Cu-Au in BC is new ground for the chair, less so for VP Exploration Skelton. Region: BC - yes. New for them: taking a BC porphyry through PEA/permitting and finding a buyer in copper rather than gold.
Skin & pay
4/5 — meaningful stake with real market buying. Insiders ~1.8% per Simply Wall St (~C$1.37M; the card's SEDI-based tally is ~3%: CEO ~1.9% + chair ~1.3%, so Simply Wall St likely omits indirect holdings); insiders net buyers ~C$371k in 12 months incl. chair Taylor buying ~260,000 sh at C$0.96 (Apr 2026) in the market. CEO total compensation not available (circular not fetched; Simply Wall St shows n/a). Market cap ~C$78M. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-kdk/kodiak-copper-shares/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • CEO will chair a second listed company (Kay Copper) while running Kodiak - split attention.
  • Three equity raises in 15 months; typical for a drill-stage explorer but dilution is continuous.
  • Financials: money into the ground fell every year (C$9.5M FY23 → C$2.8M in 9M FY26) while cash overhead stayed ~C$2M, so overhead is now ~43% of spend (17% in FY23); travel, promotion and IR the biggest G&A line.

Thesis

Pure-play porphyry project generator in Australia's premier copper-gold province (home of Cadia and Northparkes), with a >100 km strike position on the covered northern Macquarie Arc — the undercover extension majors are now paying to explore.

The Gate

A discovery. Kincora has land, targets and partners, but no discovery hole. Under the AngloGold Ashanti earn-in on the Northern Junee-Narromine Belt (up to A$50M for 80%), a discovery there leaves Kincora with ~20%. A formal partner process is under way for Trundle, Fairholme, Cowal East and Cundumbul.

Risk score5/5No discovery and no resource anywhere; drilling to date has returned anomalous, not economic, copper. The generator model limits dilution (cash just under A$14M, plus the final US$3.5M of the Mongolia sale due by 31 Dec), but the most likely failure is simply that nothing is found inside the horizon.
Market cap2 Oct 2026: ~US$35M (C$1.05 · ~C$50M on 48.0M shares). ~US$30M (~C$40–45M at ~C$0.85–0.94 on ~45M post-consolidation shares; verify live).
Capex / IRRNo economic study — no discovery yet.
NPVNo NPV — no resource.
DepositNo resource.Best historic results are anomalous (e.g. 80 m @ 0.16% Cu + 0.11 g/t Au and 10 m @ 1 g/t Au + 0.34% Cu at Fairholme, 2022). Eight NSW projects along the Macquarie Arc; Mongolian assets being sold for US$10M.
NPV : capexn/a — no study.
Valuation Anchor

~US$30M for a district-scale land position and partner-funded drilling — cheap per drill metre, but no pounds to value. Same bucket as Vizsla, and earlier than Gladiator.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~7% (board & management; CEO Sam Spring ~1.8%; director Jeremy Robinson ~2.6%; John Holliday sold ~208k sh Mar–Aug 2026). Anchors: Bloomfield Group / Big Ben ~11–12%, RareX ~8% (has been selling), Sprott AM ~4.6% (unverified). The Sep 2025 C$4M raise was cornerstoned by Rick Rule and Jeff Phillips. AngloGold holds no equity (project-level earn-in).

Read: Moderate — Rule/Phillips and Bloomfield are the votes of confidence; management's holding is small and one director has been trimming.

Jurisdiction risk

National: excellent — NSW, tier-one rule of law, state co-funded drilling grants. Local: low — farming land in a long-established mining district (Cadia, Northparkes, Cowal).

Jurisdiction isn't the risk; geology is.

Differentiator

District-scale position with partner funding in a tier-one belt. One of the largest junior land positions on the covered northern Arc; AngloGold funding the most advanced targets; non-dilutive NSW grants; the Mongolia sale adds cash without issuing shares. Technical committee led by John Holliday (ex-Newcrest, Cadia).

The generator model caps dilution — and caps the upside of any single discovery.

Exploration upside

Still searching · moves the needle: very high if it hits, but low odds. Targets are covered porphyry intrusive complexes (Nevertire, Nyngan, Wongarbon) with anomalous copper-gold and signs of "increasing proximity" to system centres in AngloGold-funded drilling. No step-outs from a defined body yet — this is the grassroots end of the risk spectrum.

Next Catalyst

AngloGold-funded drill results (Nevertire/Nyngan); Wongarbon grant-hole assays; new asset-level partner deals; completion of the Mongolia sale (definitive agreements Jul 2, 2026 with Tumen Ail Coal; final tranche in escrow, close expected by year-end); air-core programmes late spring–summer 2026.

Open Questions
  • Does AngloGold's drilling at Nevertire vector into a porphyry centre?
  • Which partners take Trundle, Fairholme, Cowal East and Cundumbul, and on what terms?
  • How much of any discovery would Kincora actually keep?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 2/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Thirteen years under the same CEO with no discovery, Mongolia to NSW: disclosure is plain and partners fund the drilling, and the 9% odds already say it.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Jonathan (Sam) Spring (President, CEO & Executive Director, since Apr 2013 (per company; Jul 2014 per ASX director data)): Ex-Goldman Sachs / Ocean Equities mining analyst; CFA. 13 years as CEO. · Cameron McRae (Chairman, since Aug 2018): 28 yrs Rio Tinto; President Oyu Tolgoi LLC, CEO Richards Bay Minerals, MD Murowa Diamonds. · Peter Leaman (SVP Exploration, since n/a): 40+ yrs; ex-BHP/PanAust; credited on Reko Diq and Crater Mountain discoveries. · John Holliday (Director, chairs Technical Committee, since n/a): Known Macquarie Arc porphyry geologist (Cadia discovery credit per general knowledge - unverified here).
Track record
  • Spring: 13 years as CEO; company spent 2011-2024 on Bronze Fox (Mongolia) with no economic discovery; Mongolian assets sold 2026 for US$10M staged (US$6.5M received by Sep 2026)source
  • Pivoted to NSW Macquarie Arc (Trundle, Nyngan, Condobolin, Fairholme) from ~2020; no discovery yet; model is partner-funded: AngloGold Ashanti earn-ins at Nyngan/Nevertire South, 10% management fee to Kincorasource
  • Spring has never sold a company or built a mine; prior career was sell-side research - no CEO wins or outright failures, just a long driftsource
  • Chair McRae ran Oyu Tolgoi (operator) and Richards Bay Minerals - operator credentials, not junior-explorer financing/discovery credentialssource
  • Cash ~A$12M at Jun 2026 after C$4M placement (Rule/Phillips-led) and Mongolia proceeds; market cap ~A$51Msource

Boards today: Spring: Kincora CEO; ASX data lists one other holding (OB1, shares only, not a board seat verified). McRae: other boards not verified.

Fit to this job
Stage: explorer/prospect generator - matches. Deposit type: porphyry Cu-Au in the Macquarie Arc; Leaman and Holliday have porphyry discovery backgrounds, Spring does not. Region: Australia - fine. New for them: nothing - this is the job they have been doing for a decade; the issue is that it has not produced a discovery.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Spring: 854,549 shares (1.67%) + 990,048 options (May 2026); exercised 106,667 options at A$0.75 in May 2026. No open-market buying found. CEO total comp C$656,692 (2024). Market cap ~A$51M. Sources: https://www.marketindex.com.au/asx/directors/sam-spring ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/au/materials/chia-kcc/kincora-copper-shares/management (2025 circular PDF returned 404)

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • 13 years, two continents, no discovery; shareholder capital repeatedly raised (dual ASX listing 2022, placements) for a programme that keeps restarting.
  • CEO pay (C$657k in 2024) has risen while the company stays unprofitable (Simply Wall St note); that is ~1.3% of market cap per year.
  • Financials: almost none of its own cash went into the ground 2024–Q1 2026 (~C$7.0M of C$7.2M exploration reimbursed by partners) while operating outflows ran ~C$3.4M; shares roughly doubled in 18 months.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$7.0M at 31 March 2026 and about A$12M at 30 June after the first US$1.5M from selling the Mongolian assets for US$10M.
  2. Very little of Kincora's own money went into the ground: partners reimbursed about C$7.0M of C$7.2M exploration, while overhead ran C$1.7M a year.
  3. Shares roughly doubled from 24.7M to about 48M in 18 months across three placements, after a 10-for-1 consolidation in September 2025.
  4. Sole-funded drilling at Condobolin began in Q2 2026, so own-funded burn rises from here.
  5. Attached options are carried as a C$1.4M derivative liability, a Mongolian tax re-audit is possible, and the auditor flags going concern.

Thesis

Prospect generator whose shareholders get several partner-funded drill programmes — Moxico at Zaha, Minsur at Lacsha, Daura at Cerro Bayo — without paying for the drilling.

The Gate

A partner-funded discovery big enough to matter at a 20–25% retained interest. Minsur can earn 75% of Lacsha by drilling 60,000 m over six years (~C$40M) plus ~C$2.5M cash, with a pre-negotiated path to 100% — total cash to Latin Metals could reach ~US$42M across all stages; the definitive agreement is due within 90 days of the Aug 18, 2026 LOI. Moxico is advancing a 15,000 m programme at Zaha.

Note: the Peruvian copper projects Para and Auquis were spun out into Latin Explore (completed 2026) and are no longer inside LMS.

Risk score5/5No resource anywhere. Diversification across ~15 projects and minimal burn make a wipe-out unlikely; the more likely failure is a slow drift, because a re-rate needs a discovery on someone else's drill budget.
Market cap2 Oct 2026: ~US$26M (C$0.24 · ~C$36M on 151.6M shares). ~US$26M (~C$36M at ~C$0.26 on ~139M shares, Sep 2026; up ~200% over 12 months).
Capex / IRRNo economic study — no resource.
NPVNo NPV — no resource.
DepositNo resource.Copper assets kept after the spin-out: Zaha (formerly Esperanza, Cu-Au porphyry, San Juan — optioned to Moxico), Lacsha (Cu-Mo porphyry, Peru — Minsur LOI Aug 2026), Terraza / Ventana North (sediment-hosted Cu, NW Argentina). Gold-silver: Cerro Bayo & La Flora (optioned to Daura Gold), Organullo (100%).
NPV : capexn/a — no study.
Valuation Anchor

~US$26M for ~15 projects, three funded partners and retained interests — cheap exposure per drill metre, but no pounds to value. The copper exposure is real but indirect: a 20–25% share of partners' discoveries.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~40% nominal (the chip counts him) — but ~36% is one financier-director, Robert Kopple / KF Business Ventures; CEO Keith Henderson ~3.5%; other officers <0.4%. Sprott Inc. ~8.5%. No Elemental Altus, Moxico or Minsur equity found. Repeat insider selling flagged (Cass, Leon, Palahanova Dec 2025–Jan 2026; Henderson bought 1.3M at C$0.13 then sold 160k).

Read: Alignment rests on one backer, not management — and management has been net-trimming.

Jurisdiction risk

Argentina: favourable — pro-investment national government and RIGI; Zaha sits in pro-mining San Juan. Peru: mixed — excellent geology, but volatile politics and frequent community conflict. Local: project-specific, with partners carrying most community-engagement cost.

Differentiator

Diversified, partner-funded optionality at a microcap price. Three partners drilling at no cost to shareholders, retained 20–25% or NSR interests, option-payment inflows, and no near-term equity need per management.

The flip side: retained interests cap the upside of any single discovery — and only part of the portfolio is copper.

Exploration upside

Mixed evidence · moves the needle: medium. Cerro Bayo has returned high-grade gold-silver intercepts and a large epithermal system (Daura drilling, 2026); Zaha is described as open in all directions; Lacsha is drill-permitted. The most advanced drilling is gold-silver, not copper.

Next Catalyst

Minsur definitive agreement (by ~mid-Nov 2026); Zaha drilling (Moxico); Daura's Phase II at Cerro Bayo and first drilling of La Flora (both under way since early Q4 2026, ~1,600 m in 20 holes, partner-funded; assay timing not given); a new partner for Organullo.

Open Questions
  • Does the Minsur Lacsha deal close on LOI terms?
  • Does Moxico's drilling at Zaha find a porphyry centre?
  • After the spin-out, is LMS really a copper story or a gold-silver one — and which will drive the stock?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 4/5

Clean, cheap, candid prospect generator with two modest exits; no discovery of its own in eleven years.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Keith Henderson (Founder, President, CEO & Director, since Jun 2015): Geologist, 30+ yrs; ex-Cardero Resource (Pampa de Pongo sold for US$100M); co-founder/CEO Velocity Minerals (Bulgaria assets sold for US$59M, Oct 2024). · Eduardo Leon (VP Exploration, since n/a): Ex-Lumina Copper senior geologist on Taca Taca (sold to First Quantum US$470M); ex-Auryn Peru exploration manager. · Mario Castelli (President, Cardero Argentina (subsidiary), since Associated since 2015): Argentine mining lawyer, 30+ yrs.
Track record
  • Henderson at Cardero Resource: Pampa de Pongo iron project (Peru) sold for US$100M (2010 cycle) - win, as executive not CEOsource
  • Henderson as CEO of Velocity Minerals: Rozino (Bulgaria) taken to PFS and permits, all Bulgarian assets sold to Turkerler for US$59M cash (US$15M at close, US$44M within 18 months), Oct 2024 - win, modest sizesource
  • Latin Metals (11 years): prospect-generator model; partners have included AngloGold (terminated Organullo Oct 2025 after ~US$3.3M), Barrick, Minsur (Lacsha, Aug 2026), Aumin (Organullo re-optioned Sep 2026, up to US$40M), Daura Gold; Para/Auquis copper spun out into Latin Explore Feb 2026source
  • No discovery or sale of a flagship from Latin Metals itself yet; market cap ~C$33Msource

Boards today: Henderson: Latin Metals CEO + director of Edge Copper (TSX: EDGE) and BP Silver (TSXV: BPAG), and likely Latin Explore (unverified) - 3 to 4 public roles.

Fit to this job
Stage: prospect generator in Argentina/Peru - exactly the job and region Henderson and Leon have done for a decade (Salta, Peru). Deposit types: epithermal gold and porphyry copper. New for them: nothing structurally; the open question is whether any option partner drills a discovery, which the model does not control.
Skin & pay
4/5 — meaningful stake with real market buying. Henderson 3.52% direct (~C$1.18M); insiders net buyers ~C$2.5M over 12 months (mostly option exercises, incl. director Kopple); CEO total comp ~C$262k (90% salary) - small relative to a C$33M company. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-lms/latin-metals-shares/management (Dec 2025 circular fetched lacked comp table).

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • CEO sits on at least three public boards; attention split.
  • A decade of optioning without a flagship outcome - earn-ins have a habit of being terminated (AngloGold).
  • Financials: cash overhead C$2.1M in 9M FY26 vs ~C$0.8M of its own exploration money (the rest is partner-funded); key-management pay C$1.1M in nine months vs C$0.5M for all of FY25.

What the numbers say
  1. Pro-forma cash is about C$3.0M after C$1.875M of warrant exercises in September 2026; at C$0.5-0.7M a quarter that is 4-6 quarters.
  2. Overhead dominates and is growing: cash G&A was C$2.08M in nine months of FY26 against about C$0.8M of own ground spend; partner Daura paid C$1.31M more.
  3. Shares grew from 71.5M in 2023 to 151.6M after the warrant exercises, more than double; 12.1M warrants at C$0.20 remain.
  4. Key management pay jumped to C$1.13M in nine months, mostly share-based, versus C$0.53M for all of FY25.
  5. No debt; the Latin Explore spin-out added one-off gains and costs, and the auditor flagged going concern in FY23 and FY25.

Caveats (5)Q4 FY24 and Q4 FY25 are derived (annual less 9M YTD); the Q3 and Q4 FY2024 links on the company site point to the wrong file (Q1 FY25), so 9M FY24 figures come from the comparatives in the Q3 FY25 statements and the FY24 balance sheet from the FY25 audited comparatives.Four-quarter sums reconcile exactly to FY25 for ni (-1.26), cfo (-1.44) and fin (2.66) by construction; FY26 is in progress (9M ni -1.73, cfo -1.78, fin 1.28).Q4 FY24 income-statement split by line (ga/sbc/fin/other) is computed from FY24 lines less the sum of the three FY24 quarterly comparatives; subtotals and net loss tie, individual lines not independently checked.Q3 FY26 MD&A not read (statements only); subsequent-event detail (Minsur, Aumin, warrant exercises) taken from the Q3 FY26 statements notes and the 28 Sep 2026 news release.FY23 current assets exclude C$0.81M of investments that were classified non-current that year (reclassified current from FY24), so FY23 working capital is not like-for-like.

C$ millions with TWO decimals (one decimal would zero most lines; quarterly G&A and exploration are C$0.03–0.8M). Quarterly cash flows are discrete quarters derived from YTD statements. 'acq' = option/property-sale proceeds plus partner-funded exploration received (Daura), i.e. inflows; 'exp_cap' = gross E&E spend incl. the partner-funded portion. 'other' includes E&E recoveries (option proceeds above carrying value), fair-value changes on investments, FX, spin-out gains/costs. spend.in.ops = option/partner receipts (the prospect-generator business model), not operating cash flow. spend.out.overhead = operating cash outflow less expensed property investigation; ground = gross E&E spend + property investigation.

How to read a card. The bucket colour on the left is the archetype. The gate is the single thing that has to go right; the differentiator is what the company has that peers don't. When those two are the same fact seen from two sides, that's usually the most honest thing to know about the name.

Reminder on cross-company comparisons: NPV/capex figures sit on each project's own copper-price deck, and CuEq uses different metal-price assumptions per company — read the anchors as shapes, not decimal-precise rankings. This is research shorthand, not investment advice.
